The contradiction is real: implicit_transitions() is AST-derived and resolves _spec(...) bindings through the delegate pass (flow_graph.py:938-957), and the validator raises redundant_with_tool from those hops (flow_graph.py:678-703) — so the same screen warns that an edge duplicates a tool whose badge says it does not move. Two of the four (request_callback, capture_lead) transition only when upsell_node is set, which the badge cannot express either way; that nuance does not weaken the finding. MINOR is right: editor-only, no runtime effect.

title: ToolResult.analytics is written by ten handlers and read by nothing, under a comment claiming Bot Analytics reads it
mechanism: `ToolResult.analytics` is populated at ten sites. `to_llm()` (domain.py:57-72) does not include it; voice's `_announce` (voice/tools.py:454-475) ignores it; `bot_tools` returns `{**result.data}` and drops it; `mcp_tools` returns the handler payload. A repo-wide search for `.analytics` outside domain.py's own `__post_init__` guard returns zero read sites. Bot Analytics reads `commercial_events` / `activity_events` directly (db_bot_analytics.py:124-128). The class docstring (domain.py:12) advertises the field as one of three things "the caller can uniformly derive", and capture_lead carries thirteen lines of comment (domain.py:544-548) asserting "Bot Analytics reads this list, and claiming an upsell_presented whose row was never written makes the funnel disagree with the commercial-events table" — the careful `emitted=analytics` out-parameter threading through `db.create_lead` (domain.py:503-505) and the conditional append at :565 are load-bearing for no consumer.
trigger: No runtime misbehaviour — the events themselves are written by `capture.*` inside the handlers. The defect is the false comment: the next person to change what `create_lead` emits will maintain a contract nobody has, and anyone auditing "how does the funnel know an offer was presented" is pointed at the wrong mechanism.
fix: Either delete the field and the three comments that justify it, or give it the one consumer it claims: have voice's `_traced` / `CrmSink` and `bot_runtime` fold `result.analytics` into the `bot_tool_calls` audit row so a call's declared events can be reconciled against `commercial_events`. Do not leave the comment standing either way.
verify_reason: ToolResult.analytics is declared at domain.py:43 and normalised at :53-55. A Grep for `\.analytics\b` across backend/**/*.py returns exactly two hits, both inside __post_init__ (domain.py:54-55) — zero read sites. to_llm() (domain.py:57-72) copies only data/ok/error/say; voice's _announce reads entity/entity_id/deep_link/spoken_summary only (voice/tools.py:454-469); bot_tools handlers return {**result.data}. Write sites confirmed at domain.py:348,591,691,791,860,934,1005,1079 plus kb.py:499 and kb.py:809 (the finding says ten; it is eleven counting kb's second site). The false comment is verbatim at domain.py:544-546: 'Bot Analytics reads this list…' — Bot Analytics in fact aggregates from interactions/commercial_events (db_bot_analytics.py:124-129). The emitted=analytics out-parameter threading (domain.py:503-505) and the conditional append (:565) are load-bearing for no consumer. Keeping MINOR rather than TRIVIAL: this is a whole dead field plus a comment that actively misdirects the next maintainer of the funnel, which is exactly the dead-config class this audit is asked to surface. No runtime misbehaviour, as reported.

title: The "read-only" MCP surface writes a commercial event, un-attributed, with no offer-sourcing guard
mechanism: catalog.py:24-35 and mcp_tools.py:1-16 both state the MCP surface is read-only ("Every mutating tool is excluded … until it does, it reads"). `check_product_eligibility` is on BOTH_AND_MCP (catalog.py:773) and its MCP handler (mcp_tools.py:97-104) calls `domain.check_product_eligibility` with `record_event` left at its default True, so `_check_and_record_eligibility` runs `capture.record_eligibility_checked` inside `db.engine.begin()` (domain.py:237-245) and emits an `eligibility_checked` commercial event (capture.py:1526-1554) — with `interaction_id=None` (so `entity_type="customer"`) and `actor_bot_id=None`. Separately, the MCP handler is the only one of the three that omits `domain.offer_sourcing_violation`, which voice (voice/tools.py:1808) and text (bot_tools.py:536-539) both apply before evaluating: an external agent can therefore probe every product id in the catalog against a named customer and each probe writes a row.
trigger: An MCP client calls check_product_eligibility for customer C across the product list. Each call writes a commercial_events row attributed to no bot and joined to no interaction, inflating the eligibility-check leg of the offer funnel and leaving an unattributable audit trail; the bot_tool_calls audit row is only written when C has a prior interaction (mcp_tools.py:249-253).
fix: Pass `record_event=False` from mcp_tools._check_product_eligibility (the parameter already exists — domain.py:200-206 documents it for capture_lead's re-check), or plumb an `actor` label through `record_eligibility_checked` so MCP-originated checks are distinguishable. Also state in the module docstring that this tool writes an analytics row, since "it reads" is currently false.
verify_reason: Both read-only claims are at the cited lines (mcp_tools.py:1-16, catalog.py:26-35). check_product_eligibility carries BOTH_AND_MCP (catalog.py:773) and is not in DENIED (mcp_tools.py:40-58) and is registered (mcp_tools.py:126). Stronger than reported: the public domain.check_product_eligibility (domain.py:296-347) has no record_event parameter at all, so the MCP path cannot opt out — it always reaches _check_and_record_eligibility with record_event defaulting True (domain.py:190-197) and runs capture.record_eligibility_checked inside db.engine.begin() (domain.py:236-248). The MCP handler passes neither interaction_id nor bot_id (mcp_tools.py:100-106), so record_eligibility_checked writes entity_type='customer' with actor_bot_id=None (capture.py:1526-1554). The offer-sourcing asymmetry is real: voice applies domain.offer_sourcing_violation before evaluating (voice/tools.py:1810-1813) and text does too (bot_tools.py:536-539), the MCP handler does not. The bot_tool_calls audit row is written only when the customer has a prior interaction (mcp_tools.py:250-260). Severity kept at the reporter's MINOR, though it is arguably understated: this is an unattributable write emitted from a surface documented as read-only.

title: limit's declared maximum is enforced on voice only and is dropped from the wire schema on text
mechanism: `get_payment_history.limit` declares minimum=1/maximum=20 and `get_emi_schedule.limit` minimum=1/maximum=24. `json_schema(strict=True)` explicitly drops minimum/maximum/default (schema.py:72-78), and `to_openai_tool` defaults to strict=True — so on WhatsApp, the sandbox and any strict text deployment the model never sees the bounds. The voice handlers clamp (`max(1, min(int(...), 20))`, voice/tools.py:1133/1164) but the text and MCP handlers do not: `int(args.get("limit") or 8)` then `ledger[:limit]` (bot_tools.py:172/181, mcp_tools.py:86/96). A negative limit is worse than unclamped — `list[:-1]` silently drops the most recent entry rather than erroring.
trigger: A model that emits `limit: 500` on WhatsApp gets the customer's entire ledger into the turn (token cost, and more history than the tool's own description promises). A model that emits `limit: -1` gets the ledger minus its newest row, and nothing anywhere reports that a bound was violated.
fix: Clamp in the two text handlers and the two MCP handlers the way voice does — or better, add a `ToolSpec.clamp_args()` next to `normalize_args` that applies minimum/maximum, and call it from all three dispatchers, since the strict renderer will keep hiding these constraints from the model.
verify_reason: Bounds are declared (catalog.py:101-118 limit 1..20 default 8; catalog.py:119-135 limit 1..24 default 6). json_schema drops minimum/maximum/default whenever strict is set (schema.py:72-79) and to_openai_tool defaults strict=True (schema.py:104); every production call site uses that default (bot_runtime.py:949,1036; sandbox_runtime.py:218), so the text model never sees the bounds. Voice clamps: max(1, min(int(...), 20)) at voice/tools.py:1133 and max(1, min(int(...), 24)) at voice/tools.py:1164. Text does not: int(args.get('limit') or 8) then ledger[:limit] (bot_tools.py:172-173, 181-182); MCP identical (mcp_tools.py:86-87, 96-97). The negative-slice consequence is correct — a negative limit silently truncates the newest rows. One nuance that does not refute it: the MCP wire schema is rendered non-strict (schema.py:141-152) so an MCP client is shown the bounds while the server still ignores them, which is a second flavour of the same gap.

title: Every WhatsApp dispute is filed as priority high; the same tool on voice files normal unless it is fraud
mechanism: `domain.flag_dispute` derives priority as `high` only for `fraud` and `normal` otherwise (domain.py:817-819), and voice passes no priority at all (voice/tools.py:1360-1370) so it gets that rule. The text handler hardcodes `priority="high"` for every dispute (bot_tools.py:278). The catalog spec exposes no `priority` argument, so this is not an author or model choice — it is a per-channel constant.
trigger: A customer raises the same `wrong_amount` grievance on WhatsApp and on the phone. The chat one lands on the disputes queue as high, the voice one as normal. Any SLA, sort order or workload split driven by `disputes.priority` treats channel as severity.
fix: Drop `priority="high"` from bot_tools.py:278 and let domain.flag_dispute decide, so both channels file the same grievance at the same priority. If chat genuinely warrants an escalation, make it a documented rule inside domain.flag_dispute rather than a channel constant.
verify_reason: domain.flag_dispute derives prio = priority if in {low,normal,high} else ('high' if dtype=='fraud' else 'normal') (domain.py:817-819). The voice handler calls it with customer_id/dispute_type/interaction_id/account_id/amount/summary/idempotency_key and no priority (voice/tools.py:1355-1364), so voice inherits the fraud rule. The text handler passes priority='high' unconditionally (bot_tools.py:278) for every dispute_type. The catalog's FLAG_DISPUTE spec exposes no priority argument, so neither the author nor the model chooses it — it is a per-channel constant, exactly as claimed. Same grievance, different queue priority by channel. MINOR is right: contained to disputes.priority ordering, no data loss.

title: add_customer_note on text raises KeyError on a missing `text`, the exact hole the PTP handler was patched for
mechanism: Under strict function calling every property is listed in `required` and optionality is carried by a nullable type (schema.py:118-124); `normalize_args` then drops explicit nulls (schema.py:196-199). `_tool_create_promise` guards against exactly this (bot_tools.py:238-241, with a comment naming the failure), and the voice handler guards too (voice/tools.py:1633-1636 returns `empty_note`). `_tool_add_note` does not: `args["text"]` (bot_tools.py:342) raises KeyError, which falls to the generic handler at bot_tools.py:855-862 and returns `tool_failed:KeyError` — a code the model cannot act on, logged as a runtime failure rather than a correctable argument error.
trigger: The model calls add_customer_note with `text: null` (or omits it on a non-strict deployment). The turn burns an iteration on an opaque `tool_failed:KeyError`, and the operator sees a KeyError traceback in the logs for what is a model argument mistake.
fix: `body = str(args.get("text") or "").strip(); if not body: return {"ok": False, "error": "empty_note"}` — the same shape as voice/tools.py:1633-1636 and bot_tools.py:238-241.
verify_reason: Mechanism verified: execute_tool normalises with CATALOG.normalize (bot_tools.py:834) after the allowed check, normalize_args drops keys whose value is None and keys not on the spec (schema.py:186-200), and there is no missing_required check before dispatch — _tool_add_note then does args['text'] (bot_tools.py:342), whose KeyError falls to the generic handler and returns {'error': 'tool_failed:KeyError'} (bot_tools.py:848-862). The asymmetry is exact: _tool_create_promise guards with a comment naming this failure (bot_tools.py:238-241) and the voice handler returns empty_note (voice/tools.py:1631-1633). One caveat that lowers confidence on the TRIGGER rather than the mechanism: ADD_CUSTOMER_NOTE.text is required=True (catalog.py:529-534), so under strict function calling — the default everywhere (schema.py:104) — the property is typed plain 'string' and listed in required, and the API is supposed to guarantee it. So the reachable path is a non-strict or non-conforming deployment. I still confirm at MINOR because the repo's own PTP guard comment ('The model can omit a "required" property') documents that the team observed this class against equally required=True args (catalog.py:244-257). Treat the confidence as SUSPECTED on the trigger, VERIFIED on the mechanism.

title: An eval grader accepts a tool named record_optout that exists in no registry, and the catalog has no opt-out tool at all
mechanism: `grade_stops_after_opt_out` passes when `"record_optout" in names`, where `names` is the observed tool-call list (graders.py:299), and the shipped fixture `evt-ob-optout` asserts a pass using exactly that tool call (fixtures.py:303-306). `record_optout` is not in `CATALOG`, not in `voice/tools.py`'s registry, not in `bot_tools.HANDLERS`, and not in `mcp_tools.HANDLERS` — it is a post-call *action* verb (defaults.py:265, `PostCallRule(when="opt_out_requested", do=["record_optout", "stop_cadence"])`, executed by post_call_actions.py). No agent on any channel can emit it, and the catalog offers no in-call way to record an opt-out.
trigger: The grader's tool-name half can never fire against a real trial, so only `fixture["optout_recorded"]` can ever satisfy it. The suite reads as covering "the agent wrote the opt-out" while it only covers "something, post-call, wrote it" — and the gap it papers over is real: a borrower who says "stop calling me" mid-call has no tool that records it before the Closer runs.
fix: Drop the `record_optout` name from graders.py:299 and fixtures.py:305 so the grader keys only on `optout_recorded`; then decide separately whether an in-call opt-out tool belongs in the catalog (the honest answer given `set_contact_preference`'s `window_would_be_empty` branch at voice/tools.py:1774-1785, which already routes the caller toward one it cannot call).
verify_reason: grade_stops_after_opt_out accepts either fixture['optout_recorded'] or the literal name 'record_optout' in the observed tool-call list (graders.py:285-308, the disjunction at :299), and the shipped fixture evt-ob-optout asserts a pass using exactly that tool call (fixtures.py:299-307, mirrored in sql/23_outbound_evals.sql:116). A repo grep for record_optout shows it exists only as a post-call action verb: defaults.py:265 PostCallRule(when='opt_out_requested', do=['record_optout','stop_cadence']), the executor at post_call_actions.py:284-301 and its registry at :487, plus the action vocabulary in compile.py:160. It is in no tool registry — not CATALOG, not voice/tools.py, not bot_tools.HANDLERS, not mcp_tools.HANDLERS. I checked the obvious refutation: set_contact_preference is not an opt-out substitute — it only narrows the calling window in hours and its own description forbids widening (catalog.py:393-433). So the second half stands too: no in-call tool records 'stop calling me'. MINOR is right.

title: "What the compiler said at the time" is true only for publishes — rollback never recompiles, so it records no gate verdict at all
mechanism: `record_rollback`'s payload is `{deploymentId, replacedDeploymentId, versionId}` — no gates and no hashes (change_log.py:238-242) — because `rollback_bot_deployment` never calls `compile_card`: it locks, validates the deployment is production and not already active, and inserts a fresh active row (db_prompt_studio.py:2292-2380; the only `compile_card` calls in the module are at :837 preview and :1908 publish). A rollback therefore re-activates a prompt version whose gates may no longer pass — a skill signature revoked since, a connector disapproved, an eval suite now failing — and the record says nothing about it. The tab's header promises "who changed what this agent says, and what the compiler said at the time" (ChangeLogTab.tsx:207) and the gate line is simply omitted when `gateCount === 0` (:149), so the absence reads as "no gates to report" rather than "no gates were run". Same for archive and restore, though those change the roster rather than the words.
trigger: Roll back a deployment after a skill has been unsigned: the chain records the rollback with no gate map, and the tab shows a Rolled-back row with no compiler verdict beside it.
fix: Either run `compile_card` against the deployment's prompt version inside `rollback_bot_deployment` and pass `report=` through to `record_rollback` (recording, not blocking — a rollback should not be gated), or make the UI say "no compile report — rollbacks re-ship a previously gated version without recompiling" instead of rendering nothing.
verify_reason: record_rollback's payload is exactly {deploymentId, replacedDeploymentId, versionId} — no gates key, no hashes (backend/agent_core/change_log.py:238-242) — and rollback_bot_deployment never recompiles: I read the whole function (backend/db_prompt_studio.py:2292-2434) and it locks (:2326-2329), rejects non-production (:2324) and already-active (:2331), re-fetches the prompt version (:2335-2342), inserts a fresh active deployment row and calls record_rollback (:2411-2422). A grep for compile_card across the module returns only :796/:837 (preview) and :1874/:1908 (publish) — no rollback call site. So a rollback re-activates a prompt version whose gates may no longer pass (a skill signature revoked since, a connector disapproved, an eval suite now failing) and the chain records nothing about it. The rendering half is also right: the gate line is guarded by {gateCount > 0 && (...)} (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:149) so absence reads as "no gates to report" rather than "no gates were run", under a header promising "what the compiler said at the time" (:207). Same for archive (change_log.py:263) and restore (:295). MINOR is correct: the tab shows no wrong verdict, only a missing one, and the rollback target was gated when it was originally published.

title: The "introspective" verb test asserts over a Python set and cannot see either of the two TypeScript maps it claims to protect
mechanism: `test_every_lifecycle_action_has_a_verb_the_log_can_render` says "A new `record_*` writing an unlisted action fails here rather than rendering as a raw `agent.whatever` on the fleet index" (test_agent_change_log.py:130-134), but its assertion is `emitted == {"agent.publish", "agent.rollback", "agent.archive", "agent.restore"}` over `vars(change_log)` — a Python-side self-check. Adding `RESTORE`-style constant #5 keeps this test green while both frontends fall through to their raw-string fallbacks (ChangeLogTab.tsx:121 `?? entry.action`, agent-roster.ts:160) — which is exactly the failure prior finding 2n.2 recorded. Reword the Python test's docstring so it stops claiming coverage it does not have.
verify_reason: Real, with a line correction. The test is at backend/tests/test_agent_change_log.py:138, not :130 (:130 belongs to test_restoring_a_card_is_recorded_too). Its docstring claims "A new record_* writing an unlisted action fails here rather than rendering as a raw agent.whatever on the fleet index" (:139-141), but the assertion is emitted == {"agent.publish", "agent.rollback", "agent.archive", "agent.restore"} over vars(change_log) filtered to uppercase str constants (:142-147) — a Python-side self-check that cannot observe either map it names. The maps that actually decide whether an action renders as a verb are ACTION_LABEL/ACTION_TONE (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:35-47) and CHANGE_VERBS (Habibi/src/lib/agent-roster.ts:152-157), in a different language and a different runner, and both fall through to raw-string fallbacks — ACTION_LABEL[entry.action] ?? entry.action (ChangeLogTab.tsx:121) and CHANGE_VERBS[action] ?? action.replace(/^agent\./, "") (agent-roster.ts:159-161). Adding a fifth record_* constant keeps the backend suite green while both surfaces print a wire string — the exact failure prior 2n.2 recorded, which is itself evidence the guard does not guard. The duplication is also real: same four keys, different casing ("Rolled back" vs "rolled back"), nothing tying them together. Not DUPLICATE_OF_PRIOR: 2n.2 was the missing restore rows, now fixed at ChangeLogTab.tsx:39/:46 and agent-roster.ts:156; this is a new claim about the regression guard. MINOR: incorrect but contained — no action is unmapped today.

title: In production the "who" column collapses to the ACTOR_USER_ID default, so every entry names one real, seeded human regardless of who acted
mechanism: `_allow_actor_header()` defaults to `not _app_is_prod()` (actor_context.py:60-73), so in production the console's `X-Actor-User-Id` is dropped and `get_actor_user_id()` falls through to `default_actor_user_id()` = `ACTOR_USER_ID` env, defaulting to the literal `"priya-nair"` (actor_context.py:36-37, db_core.py:124, .env.example:195) — a real seeded user whose existence is enforced at boot by `validate_configured_actors` (actor_context.py:161-177). `change_log.record_publish` stores `uid or "system"` from that resolution (db_prompt_studio.py:1903, :2151) and the tab prints it verbatim (ChangeLogTab.tsx:129). Unless API_KEY_MAP gives every operator their own key, the tamper-evident record attributes every publish, rollback, archive and restore to one named individual. The code itself flags the alternative as a known trade-off (WP-070, actor_context.py:64-67), but that comment is about dropping the header, not about the audit trail it feeds.
trigger: Deploy with APP_ENV=prod and no per-user API_KEY_MAP, publish as any operator: the change log records priya-nair. Not demonstrated here because it depends on the deployed env; the resolution path is unambiguous in code.
fix: Fail closed for the audit path specifically: when no actor can be resolved from an authenticated identity, write a synthetic id (e.g. `unattributed:<api-key-fingerprint>`) rather than a real users.id, so the log never puts a name on an action that name did not take. Longer term this is WP-070 / the Phase 5 JWT `sub` note at db_core.py:360.
verify_reason: The resolution path is exactly as described — _allow_actor_header() returns not _app_is_prod() when ALLOW_ACTOR_HEADER is unset (backend/actor_context.py:60-73), _resolve_shared_key_actor therefore ignores the header in prod and returns default_actor_user_id() (:229-238), which is (os.getenv("ACTOR_USER_ID") or "priya-nair") (:35-37); .env.example ships API_KEY_MAP= empty (:193) and ACTOR_USER_ID=priya-nair (:195); record_publish/record_rollback store uid or "system" (db_prompt_studio.py:2151, :2419) and the tab prints it verbatim (ChangeLogTab.tsx:129). But the finding's mechanism is materially mis-stated and that changes the severity. The console's X-Actor-User-Id is NOT a per-operator identity that prod "drops": it is a single build-time constant, const ACTOR_USER_ID = import.meta.env.VITE_ACTOR_USER_ID (Habibi/src/api/config.ts:49, sent at :57). Every operator sharing a build already sends the same id in dev, so the claimed prod-vs-dev collapse does not exist — attribution is one identity per deployment in BOTH environments unless per-user API_KEY_MAP is configured. That requirement is documented in two places as the supported answer: actor_context.py:3-6 ("API_KEY_MAP … per-user keys (preferred)") and config.ts:46-47 ("Prefer per-user API_KEY_MAP on the server for production attribution"), and actor_context.py:63-67 already names this exact consequence — "re-attributes every action to ACTOR_USER_ID" — tracked as WP-070. So this is a documented deployment-configuration requirement with a code-level fix already available, not a code defect in the change-log slice, and no code change makes the shipped .env.example correct. Real and worth recording (a mis-configured deployment does put one named human on every publish in the tamper-evident log), but MINOR, not MAJOR. Confidence SUSPECTED is right — it depends on deployed env.

title: Entries are silently capped at 50 with no truncation indicator, beside a chain count over every row in the tenant
mechanism: `useChangeLog(botId)` uses the default `limit = 50` (agent-studio.ts:977) and the tab never passes another (ChangeLogTab.tsx:177). `read_entries` clamps to `max(1, min(limit, 500))` and applies `ORDER BY seq DESC … LIMIT :n` (change_log.py:316, :327). A card with more than 50 lifecycle events therefore shows the newest 50 with no "showing 50 of N", no pagination and no limit control, directly beneath a banner reading "{chain.checked} entries verified across the tenant" — a number computed over every audit row and unrelated to what is listed. On the screen the file itself calls "the first artefact an auditor asks for", truncation renders as completeness.
trigger: Any card with >50 publish/rollback/archive/restore entries: the 51st-oldest is unreachable from the UI and nothing on screen says so.
fix: Have `read_entries` return a total count (a windowed `count(*) OVER ()` costs one column) and render "showing 50 of 137 for this card" with a Load more that raises `limit` toward the 500 ceiling; or paginate on `seq`.
verify_reason: Verified at every link. ChangeLogTab calls useChangeLog(botId) with no second argument (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:177) and the hook defaults limit = 50 (Habibi/src/api/agent-studio.ts:977, forwarded by fetchChangeLog at :970-975). Backend clamps to max(1, min(int(limit), 500)) (backend/agent_core/change_log.py:316) and applies ORDER BY seq DESC, id DESC / LIMIT :n (:327-328); the endpoint's own Query default is 50 with le=500 (backend/main.py:2173). Nothing in the tab renders a total, a "showing 50 of N", a page control or a limit selector — EntryRow list is a bare map at :224-228 with no footer. The number sitting next to it is chain.checked, which verify_chain computes as len(rows) over EVERY audit_log row in the tenant (change_log.py:357-368, :379) and the banner prints as "{chain.checked} entries verified across the tenant" (ChangeLogTab.tsx:101-104). The banner copy does at least say "across the tenant", so the two numbers are not presented as the same thing — but the 50-row cap itself is entirely silent. MINOR is the right severity: contained, no wrong verdict, but the 51st-oldest entry is unreachable from the UI on the screen the file header calls "the first artefact an auditor asks for" (:8).

title: The fleet Recent-changes panel feeds the raw Postgres timestamp to new Date() without the space→T fix the tab documents as necessary
mechanism: `read_entries` returns `"at": str(row["created_at"])` (change_log.py:342), i.e. Python's `str(datetime)` — `"2026-09-05 12:34:56.789012+00:00"`, space-separated and not ISO-8601. `ChangeLogTab.stamp()` handles exactly this: `Date.parse(at.replace(" ", "T"))` plus a `Number.isNaN` guard that falls back to printing the raw string (ChangeLogTab.tsx:54-59). The fleet panel does neither — it calls `new Date(latest.at).toLocaleDateString(...)` in the collapsed header (agent-studio.index.tsx:302-306) and `new Date(entry.at).toLocaleString(...)` in the expanded list (:365-372). V8 accepts the space form through a lenient fallback parser; engines that do not (Safari has historically returned Invalid Date for a space-separated datetime with an offset) render "Invalid Date" as the when of every audit row, and the collapsed header reads "priya-nair published kaia-v2-4 · Invalid Date".
trigger: Open the Agent Studio fleet index in a browser whose Date parser rejects the non-ISO form. Not reproduced here (no browser run), but the asymmetry with the sibling component — which carries a comment explaining why the replace exists — is unambiguous in code.
fix: Export `stamp`/a shared `parseLogTimestamp` from ChangeLogTab (or Habibi/src/lib) and use it in both places; better, normalise on the server — `row["created_at"].isoformat()` in `read_entries` — so no consumer has to know Postgres's repr.
verify_reason: The asymmetry is exactly as described and the line numbers are right. read_entries emits "at": str(row["created_at"]) (backend/agent_core/change_log.py:342) — Python str(datetime), i.e. "2026-09-05 12:34:56.789012+00:00", space-separated with 6-digit fractional seconds, not ISO-8601 — and AgentStudioChangeLogEntryResponse types at as str | None (backend/schemas.py:3548) so Pydantic passes it through verbatim. ChangeLogTab.stamp() handles exactly that shape: Date.parse(at.replace(" ", "T")) with a Number.isNaN guard falling back to the raw string (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:54-59). The fleet panel does neither transform nor guard: new Date(latest.at).toLocaleDateString(...) in the collapsed header (Habibi/src/routes/agent-studio.index.tsx:304) and new Date(entry.at).toLocaleString(...) in the expanded list (:366-371). Reachability is the browser's parser, which I cannot exercise read-only, so SUSPECTED is correct — V8 accepts the space form through its lenient fallback, engines that reject it render "Invalid Date" as the when of every audit row and the collapsed header reads "priya-nair published kaia-v2-4 · Invalid Date". MINOR holds: it degrades the audit surface's timestamps but fails loudly rather than lying, and the sibling component two files away carries the guard.

title: Both empty states enumerate three of the four recorded verbs, dropping "restored" — the same omission the file header says was already fixed
mechanism: `agent.restore` is a recorded action (change_log.py:45, :275) and the tab's own header comment (ChangeLogTab.tsx:31-34) narrates adding it to ACTION_LABEL/ACTION_TONE (:39, :46) precisely because "the one screen an auditor reads" must not spell an action in wire format. Two prose strings on the same screen were not updated: the zero-chain banner says "No agent has been published, rolled back or archived in this tenant" (:88-90) and the empty-list state says "This card has never been published, rolled back or archived" (:219-221). The fleet panel gets it right in both of its equivalents — "nothing published, rolled back, archived or restored yet" (agent-studio.index.tsx:307, :340). So the tab's empty state asserts a scope narrower than what the endpoint actually records, on the screen whose job is to state its own scope precisely.
trigger: Open the Change log tab for a card with no entries: the copy tells the reader restores are outside this record when they are inside it.
fix: Add "or restored" to both strings, and pull the verb list from `Object.values(ACTION_LABEL)` so the maps and the prose cannot drift again.
prior_ref: 2n.2 (the maps half was fixed; the prose half was not)

(Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:87-90). Empty-list state: "This card has never been published, rolled back or archived." (:218-221). agent.restore is genuinely a fourth recorded action — the constant at backend/agent_core/change_log.py:45, record_restore at :275-304, written by db.restore_agent_studio_card (backend/db_prompt_studio.py:746-755) behind POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/restore (backend/main.py:2160-2163). The same file's own header comment narrates adding it to ACTION_LABEL/ACTION_TONE precisely so an auditor is not shown a wire string (ChangeLogTab.tsx:31-34, maps at :35-47), so the prose is out of step with the fix that landed beside it. The fleet panel gets it right in both equivalents: "nothing published, rolled back, archived or restored yet" (Habibi/src/routes/agent-studio.index.tsx:307) and "Nothing published, rolled back, archived or restored yet." (:340). Not a duplicate of prior 2n.2 — that was the missing ACTION_LABEL/ACTION_TONE rows, which are present today at :39 and :46; this is the untouched prose. title: The evidence is fetched and dropped — the six component digests, prevHash, seq, versionId and deploymentId are never rendered anywhere
mechanism: `record_publish` stores `hashes` — one SHA-256 per prompt/persona/voice/guardrails/flow/agent_card (change_log.py:197, :212) — plus `versionId`, `deploymentId`, `previousVersionId`, `seq` and `prevHash`. All are typed on `ChangeLogEntry` (agent-studio.ts:900-923) and returned by the API (schemas.py:3531-3562). `EntryRow` renders none of them: it shows the action lozenge, version labels, actor, timestamp, summary, the `changed` component NAMES, the rollout line, the gate line, and a 12-character prefix of `entryHash` (ChangeLogTab.tsx:117-171). So the screen tells the auditor WHICH components moved but never lets them check a digest against a `prompt_versions` row, and shows no `prevHash`, so the chain cannot be followed by hand from the artefact the doc calls the first thing an auditor asks for. The digests are the whole reason the module stores hashes instead of copies (change_log.py:18-21).
trigger: Open any publish entry: `hashes` arrives over the wire on every request and is discarded by the renderer.
fix: Render the digests behind a disclosure on each entry — component name, 12-char digest, and the full value in a title/copy affordance — and show `prevHash` beside `entryHash` so the link is checkable. At minimum surface them in the row's title attribute rather than dropping the response's most load-bearing field.
verify_reason: The substance holds; one supporting claim is wrong and I correct it. record_publish stores hashes = component_hashes(version), one SHA-256 per prompt/persona/voice/guardrails/flow/agent_card (backend/agent_core/change_log.py:70-73, :197, :213), plus versionId, previousVersionId, deploymentId (:200-204); _write adds seq and prevHash to the same payload (:154-155) and read_entries spreads every payload key that is not action/botId onto the row (:343), so all of them cross the wire. The API returns them: AgentStudioChangeLogEntryResponse declares seq, entryHash, prevHash, previousVersionId, versionId, deploymentId and hashes: dict[str, str] | None (backend/schemas.py:3546-3560) and the route sets response_model_exclude_unset=True (backend/main.py:2167-2170) so present keys survive. EntryRow renders the action lozenge, version labels, actor, timestamp, summary, the changed component NAMES, the rollout line, the gate line and a 12-character prefix of entryHash — and nothing else (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:117-171). Correction to the auditor: the claim that all of these are "typed on ChangeLogEntry (agent-studio.ts:900-923)" is false for the one that matters — the TS type declares seq, entryHash, prevHash, versionId, deploymentId, previousVersionLabel etc. but has NO hashes field at all (Habibi/src/api/agent-studio.ts:899-922), so the digests arrive as untyped JSON and are dropped twice over. That strengthens rather than weakens the finding. MINOR stands: an auditor cannot check a digest against a prompt_versions row, and prevHash is never shown so the chain cannot be followed by hand — on the artefact change_log.py:17-21 says stores hashes instead of copies precisely so it can be.

title: Snapshotted allow_prefixes outrank the registry forever, so narrowing a connector's prefixes revokes nothing from bound cards
mechanism: Bind copies `conn.allowPrefixes` into the card (AgentCardPanels.tsx:1003). bound_tool_names then prefers the card's copy: `ref.allow_prefixes or ref.allowPrefixes or conn["allowPrefixes"]` (persist.py:224). Tightening the registry's prefix list — the natural way to revoke one remote tool without de-approving the whole connector — has no effect on any card that already snapshotted the wider list, and the tab's banner (:949-953) prints the stale card copy with no comparison against the registry.
trigger: Ops narrows bank-mcp's allow_prefixes from ["ext.bank."] to ["ext.bank.read_"] to revoke a write tool. Every already-published card keeps binding the full ext.bank. set.
fix: Intersect rather than override — `set(card_prefixes) & set(registry_prefixes)` — so a registry narrowing always applies; and show a staleness badge in the tab when the two lists differ.
verify_reason: Verified. Bind snapshots the registry list into the card — toggle([conn.slug, conn.id], conn.allowPrefixes ?? []) writes { connector_id, allow_prefixes: prefixesFor } (AgentCardPanels.tsx:932-938, :1003) — and bound_tool_names prefers that copy: `prefixes = ref.get("allow_prefixes") or ref.get("allowPrefixes") or conn["allowPrefixes"]` (persist.py:224), with the match at :233. G10 likewise validates only ref.allow_prefixes (compile.py:805-809), never comparing it to the registry. So tightening a registry row's allow_prefixes revokes nothing from an already-bound card, while de-approving does revoke (persist.py:222-223) — the asymmetry is the defect. The banner prints the stale card copy with no registry comparison (AgentCardPanels.tsx:949-953). MINOR is right: narrowing is the unusual operation and the blunt revocation still works.

title: Postgres array literals are built by string concatenation, so a comma in a slug or allowPrefix injects extra array elements — including an empty prefix that matches every remote tool
mechanism: prefixes default to [f"ext.{slug}."] (persist.py:140) and both arrays are serialised as `"{" + ",".join(prefixes) + "}"` (:180-181) rather than bound as a list. A slug or an explicit allowPrefixes entry containing a comma splits into extra elements. Nothing validates registry prefixes: attach_connector_to_card validates only card-side prefixes (clone.py:111-112) and G10 only checks `ref.allow_prefixes` (compile.py:808-809). An injected empty-string element makes `prefixed.startswith(p)` (persist.py:233) true for every cached remote tool name.
trigger: POST /connectors with allowPrefixes=["ext.bank.,"] (or a slug containing a comma) writes {ext.bank.,""}; every tool in that connector's tools_cache then binds regardless of the intended prefix restriction.
fix: Pass the lists as bound parameters (psycopg adapts a Python list to a text[]) instead of concatenating, and reject slugs/prefixes that do not match ^[a-z0-9._-]+$ in upsert_connector.
verify_reason: Mechanism verified: prefixes default to [f"ext.{slug}."] (persist.py:140) and both arrays are hand-serialised — "{" + ",".join(prefixes) + "}" (persist.py:180) and the same for data_class (:181) — then cast with CAST(:pref AS text[]) (:158-159), so an element containing a comma splits into two array elements. Nothing validates registry-side prefixes: upsert_connector has no prefix check, clone.py:111-112 validates only the card-side list, and compile.py:808 only inspects ref.allow_prefixes. The match is `prefixed.startswith(p)` (persist.py:233), so an empty element would match every cached tool of that connector. Confidence stays SUSPECTED and that is the right label — I did not execute Postgres to confirm that '{ext.bank.,}' parses to {'ext.bank.',''} for text[] rather than erroring, and the UI never sends allowPrefixes (McpConsole.tsx:152-159), so the trigger is POST /connectors by an actor holding perm-integrations-write (authz.py:328), or a slug typed with a comma. MINOR: contained to one connector's own tools_cache, and it is array-element injection, not SQL injection (the literal is a bound parameter).

title: Three uncoordinated writers of prompt_versions.agent_card with no version guard; the connector-attach client is dead code
mechanism: POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/connectors read-modify-writes the latest draft's agentCard (clone.py:113-126); PATCH /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id} (main.py:2127-2145) and PATCH /prompt-versions/{id} (main.py:3228-3232) each replace the whole agent_card column (db_prompt_studio.py:1774-1777). None carries an etag/updated_at precondition, so it is last-write-wins. The Studio's 1200 ms autosave (routes/prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:646-657) re-PATCHes its in-memory card after every edit, so a connector attached out-of-band is silently reverted by the next keystroke. Additionally all three call restore_prompt_version_as_draft when no draft exists (clone.py:119, main.py:2137), so two concurrent calls can produce two drafts and the next publish 409s ambiguous_draft_to_publish (main.py:2244-2252). The frontend client for the attach endpoint, useAttachConnector (agent-studio.ts:840-845), is exported and called from nowhere.
trigger: A script (or agent) POSTs /agent-studio/cards/kaia-v2-4/connectors while an author has the Studio open. 1.2 s after their next edit, the autosave PATCH writes the card without the new connector; the attach silently vanishes with no conflict and no message.
fix: Give the draft an updated_at/version precondition and 409 on mismatch (the publish path already does this for the unique published index), or delete the attach endpoint and its unused client and keep PATCH as the single writer.
verify_reason: Verified. Three writers of prompt_versions.agent_card with no precondition: attach_connector_to_card read-modify-writes the latest draft's card (clone.py:113-126, ending in db.patch_prompt_version(draft['id'], {'agentCard': card})) behind POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/connectors (main.py:2244-2258); PATCH /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id} replaces the whole column (main.py:2126-2144); PATCH /prompt-versions/{version_id} does the same (main.py:3227-3231). All land in db_prompt_studio.patch_prompt_version, whose write is `UPDATE prompt_versions SET ... WHERE id = :id` with agent_card = CAST(:agent_card AS jsonb) (db_prompt_studio.py:1776-1779, 1784-1787) — no etag, no updated_at guard: last write wins. The Studio's 1200 ms autosave re-sends its in-memory card on every edit (routes/prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:636, :645-653, :681). Both the attach path and the PATCH path call restore_prompt_version_as_draft when no draft exists (clone.py:119, main.py:2136), and two drafts make the next publish 409 ambiguous_draft_to_publish (main.py:2232-2240). useAttachConnector is defined at agent-studio.ts:839-846 and referenced nowhere else in Habibi/src — dead client. Trigger is API-only (perm-connector-attach, authz.py:305), which is what keeps it MINOR. Note there is a fourth writer of the column at db_prompt_studio.py:1951.

title: attach_connector_to_card binds an unapproved connector without complaint
mechanism: The docstring says "Stamp an approved connector onto the latest draft card" but the function checks only existence (clone.py:107-109) and that prefixes start with "ext." (:111-112). Status is never read. The Studio tab filters to approved rows client-side (AgentCardPanels.tsx:925), so the API is looser than the only UI that uses it. G10 does catch it at publish (compile.py:820-822).
trigger: POST /agent-studio/cards/{id}/connectors with a draft connector returns 200; the failure surfaces much later as a G10 not_approved at publish, and per CONNECTORS-6 the tab will not show the binding so it cannot be removed.
fix: Raise ValueError("connector_not_approved") in attach_connector_to_card when conn_row["status"] != "approved" — _handle_write already maps it to a 409 — so the rejection lands where the operator made the mistake.
verify_reason: Verified. attach_connector_to_card's docstring says 'Stamp an approved connector onto the latest draft card' (clone.py:104) but the body reads conn_row only for existence (:107-109) and then validates that the prefixes start with 'ext.' (:110-112); conn_row['status'] is never referenced anywhere in the function (:98-126). The endpoint passes straight through (main.py:2244-2258). The Studio's own tab is stricter, filtering to approved client-side (AgentCardPanels.tsx:925), so the API is looser than its only UI. G10 does catch it at publish with {'not_approved': id} (compile.py:820-821), which is why MINOR is the right level — and the late failure combines with CONNECTORS-6, since the tab will not render the offending binding.

title: "Add connector" hardcodes dataClass to ["pii"] with no control, and G10 only checks the list is non-empty
mechanism: The registration form sends `dataClass: ["pii"]` unconditionally (McpConsole.tsx:158) — there is no input for it. upsert_connector would default to ["pii"] anyway (persist.py:141). G10's only data-class test is `if not conn.get("dataClass")` (compile.py:826-827), so any non-empty value passes and the declared class is never compared against what the connector actually returns or against the card's own data_class.
trigger: A core-banking connector returning balances and payment references is registered through the UI and permanently labelled pii-only. The Connectors tab renders "pii · healthy" (AgentCardPanels.tsx:995) and every downstream data-class review reads the wrong classification.
fix: Add a multi-select for data class to the form (money / pii / marketing / internal), and have G10 compare the connector's declared classes against the binding card's identity.data_class rather than only checking non-emptiness.
verify_reason: Verified. The registration form sends dataClass: ['pii'] unconditionally (McpConsole.tsx:158) and I read the whole form (McpConsole.tsx:129-164) — the only inputs are slug, url and a vault-ref select, so there is no data-class control; upsert_connector would default to ['pii'] anyway (persist.py:141). G10's only data-class test is `if not conn.get("dataClass")` (compile.py:826-827), and approve's is `if not row.get("dataClass")` (persist.py:199-200) — non-empty is the whole check, never compared against the card's own data_class or the payload the connector returns. The Studio tab then renders the label as fact, '{dataClass} · {health}' (AgentCardPanels.tsx:994-996), as does the Integrations table (McpConsole.tsx:82-88). MINOR is right: mislabelling with no runtime effect, since nothing reads dataClass beyond the non-empty test.

title: ext.* names sit in the Tool Grant but in no Offer, so the only way one executes is a name the model was never shown — and that path skips skill gating
mechanism: effective_tools unions ext.* into the Grant (intersect.py:117-123) and bot_runtime assigns it to ctx.allowed_tools (bot_runtime.py:943). execute_tool's only guard is `name in ctx.allowed_tools` (bot_tools.py:806-808), and the ext.* branch (:810-823) runs before the handler lookup, before CATALOG.normalize, and outside the SKILL_GATED_TOOLS machinery. Because ext.* is stripped from every offer (intersect.py:164,168), a model can only emit such a name by hallucination or by prompt injection carrying the string — precisely the case the Offer⊆Grant design is supposed to make harmless, except here the Grant is strictly wider than anything ever offered.
trigger: A borrower message containing `ext.paylink.get_status` induces the model to emit that tool call on a card that binds paylink; it executes against real payment_intents rows with no skill attached and no verification step in the path.
fix: Either register ext.* names in the catalog so they are offered deliberately, or keep them out of ctx.allowed_tools until a pack activates them — the Grant should not be permanently wider than the union of reachable offers.
verify_reason: Verified, and SUSPECTED is the honest label. effective_tools unions ext.* into the Grant after the catalog intersection (intersect.py:106/:115 then :117-123), bot_runtime assigns that Grant to ctx.allowed_tools (bot_runtime.py:943) while offering only tool_state.offered through CATALOG.openai_tools (:949), and every offer strips ext.* (intersect.py:164, :168). execute_tool's sole guard is `if ctx.allowed_tools is None or name not in ctx.allowed_tools` (bot_tools.py:806-808), and the ext.* branch (:810-821) runs before HANDLERS.get and before CATALOG.normalize (:827, :835) and outside any SKILL_GATED_TOOLS check — the skill machinery only ever shapes the Grant at intersect.py:108-114, and ext.* names are unioned in after it. So a name the model was never shown, arriving by hallucination or by injected borrower text, dispatches against the connector if the card binds it. Reachable only on text (voice has no ext handler, voice/tools.py:2918-2919) and only with MCP_CLIENT_ENABLED true, which is why MINOR/SUSPECTED holds: the trigger is a model behaviour, not an operator action.

title: allowed_env is written, displayed and never enforced — a sandbox-only connector dispatches in production
mechanism: upsert_connector defaults allowed_env to "sandbox" (persist.py:184) and _public surfaces it as allowedEnv (:120), but no runtime module reads it: dispatch (persist.py:238-289) checks status and circuit only, and G10 (compile.py:800-830) checks approved/https/dataClass/health and never env. A grep for allowed_env/allowedEnv across agent_core/, voice/, bot_tools.py, bot_runtime.py, sandbox_runtime.py and outbound.py returns no reader.
trigger: Register a bank connector for sandbox testing (the form sends no env, so it lands as "sandbox"), approve it, bind it. Its tools dispatch identically on the production bot — the field that exists to prevent exactly this is inert.
fix: Gate dispatch on env: read the deployment env once and return {"ok": False, "error": "connector_env_not_allowed"} when conn["allowedEnv"] is neither "both" nor the running env. Add the same check to G10 so the publish is blocked rather than the call failing at runtime.
verify_reason: The dead-config core is real: upsert_connector defaults env to 'sandbox' (persist.py:184), _public exposes allowedEnv (persist.py:120), and no reader exists — a whole-backend grep for allowed_env/allowedEnv returns only persist.py:120/155/168/184/419, seed_postgres.py:1525 and the migration's CHECK (alembic/versions/20260815_0076_mcp_phase3.py:86-87). dispatch (persist.py:238-289) checks flag/status/circuit only; G10 (compile.py:753-829) checks approved/https/dataClass/health and never env. But MAJOR is inflated on two counts. (a) 'displayed' is false: allowedEnv appears in the frontend only as a type field and in mock rows (integrations.ts:126, 243, 255) — no column in ConnectorsPanel (McpConsole.tsx:43-119), no field in ConnectorsTab (AgentCardPanels.tsx:988-996), and no form control, so nothing on any screen tells an operator the connector is sandbox-scoped. (b) the stated consequence needs a production/sandbox split that this runtime does not have — there is no environment resolver anywhere in agent_core/connectors, and the rows are per-tenant DB rows, so nothing today reads a 'production bot' against them. What is left is an inert column with a CHECK constraint and no UI: incorrect but contained. Also note compile.py:800 is inside the G10 lookup-failure helper, not the checks; the checks are compile.py:804-829.

title: Connector registration and approval write no audit row and require no admin role
mechanism: approve() (persist.py:193-206), upsert_connector() (:132-190) and cimd_connect() (:424-444) each run a bare UPDATE/INSERT and return; none calls db.record_activity (db.py:404-416), the convention used elsewhere (agent_core/authority/enact.py:245). The endpoints take no `Depends(require_admin)` — require_admin exists (main.py:843-852) and is used exactly once in the whole file, on /tts/voices/sync (main.py:3078). Approval is the control that decides whether a remote MCP server receives a vault bearer token and answers with payment data.
trigger: Any authenticated non-admin actor POSTs /connectors/{id}/approve. The connector goes live; nothing records who approved it or when, and there is no change-log entry for an auditor to reconstruct.
fix: Add `Depends(require_admin)` to POST /connectors, /approve and /cimd, and write a db.record_activity row (entity_type="connector") inside each write, carrying the actor from actor_context. The hash-chained agent change-log at main.py:2166-2180 is the model to follow.
verify_reason: The authorization half is refuted. Every route in the app carries a global permission dependency — app = FastAPI(..., dependencies=[Depends(_authz_guard)]) (main.py:607-611) with _authz_guard at main.py:532-577 — and the registry classifies exactly these routes: ('POST','/connectors'), ('POST','/connectors/{connector_id}/approve'), ('POST','/connectors/{connector_id}/test') and ('POST','/connectors/{connector_id}/cimd') all require INTEGRATIONS_WRITE (authz.py:328-332), with an unregistered route denied outright (authz.py:849-868). So approve is not open to 'any authenticated non-admin actor' — it needs perm-integrations-write, which is a deliberate classification, and require_admin's single use is not evidence of a hole because roles are enforced through the table rather than per-route Depends. The audit half survives: approve (persist.py:193-206), upsert_connector (:132-190) and cimd_connect (:424-444) each run a bare UPDATE/INSERT and return, none calls db.record_activity (db.py:404-415) the way agent_core/authority/enact.py:245 does, and main.py has no global write-audit middleware (the only audit surfaces are /routing-audit at main.py:2015 and the consent audit at :1954). Real but contained: a missing audit trail on connector approval, not an authorization bypass.

title: Approve and Add-connector mutations have no error handler — a rejected write is rendered as nothing happening
mechanism: useConnectorMutations defines only onSuccess (integrations.ts:302-311). `mut.approve.mutate(r.id)` (McpConsole.tsx:104) swallows the rejection entirely; `void mut.upsert.mutateAsync(...).then(...)` (:152-160) leaves an unhandled rejection with no toast. The backend rejects both with real 409/422s — connector_data_class_required and connector_url_https_only from approve() (persist.py:198-200), connector_slug_required / connector_url_https_only from upsert (persist.py:135,139). The `cimd` button is the one that gets it right (:203-205).
trigger: Operator clicks Approve on a connector with an empty data_class, or an http:// URL. The button does nothing visible, the row stays draft, no message appears; the operator retries or concludes the button is broken.
fix: Give the mutations an onError that toasts the detail, or mirror the cimd button's `.catch((err) => toast.error(err.message))` on approve and upsert.
verify_reason: Verified. useConnectorMutations defines onSuccess only on all four mutations (integrations.ts:298-326; upsert :302-306, approve :307-311), the QueryClient sets no global mutation onError (router.tsx:6-17), `mut.approve.mutate(r.id)` (McpConsole.tsx:104) discards the rejection, and the upsert call is `void mut.upsert.mutateAsync({...}).then(...)` with no .catch (:152-160). The backend really does reject: approve raises connector_url_https_only / connector_data_class_required (persist.py:196-200) and upsert raises connector_slug_required / connector_url_https_only (:134-139), mapped to 4xx by _handle_write (main.py:825-830). The cimd button is the counter-example that gets it right (:203-205). Operator action: click Approve on a connector with an http:// URL — nothing renders, the row stays draft, no message. MINOR is right: contained, and the row visibly fails to change.

title: Connectors tab warns that connector tools count toward the voice cap; they cannot reach voice at all
mechanism: The warning-styled banner reads "Activated connector tools still count toward the voice cap." G6 counts idle_offered_tools, which strips every ext.* name (intersect.py:164,168), and voice/tools.py:2918-2919 filters a hardcoded handler dict that contains no ext.* key, so no connector tool exists on voice under any activation.
trigger: Author binds a connector, sees a warning telling them their 12-tool voice budget is at risk, and removes a real tool to make room for a cost that does not exist.
fix: Replace the sentence with the truth: connector tools are text-channel-only and are never offered on voice, so they do not count against G6.
verify_reason: Verified, and the tab contradicts itself. The warning-toned banner (AgentCardPanels.tsx:949-953, border-border-warning/text-text-warning-bolder) reads 'Activated connector tools still count toward the voice cap', while the paragraph six lines above says the opposite — 'ext.* tools stay off the idle mouth so G6 does not count them' (:943-946). G6 counts `idle` minus platform tools (compile.py:687, 691-692), `idle` is idle_offered_tools which strips every ext.* name on both branches (intersect.py:164, :168), and voice cannot host one at all (voice/tools.py:2918-2919). No pack can re-add one through offered_tools:198 either, since none lists an ext.* name. So the warning is false under every activation. MINOR: it can cost an author a real tool, but it changes no runtime behaviour.

title: Every critique is filed against skill "ptp-negotiate" regardless of which grader failed or which card ran the suite

title: Every trial's transcript, tool calls and CRM outcomes are written as empty literals, so a failed report cannot be inspected

The eval_trials INSERT binds "transcript": _jsonb([]), "tools": _jsonb([]), "crm": _jsonb({}) at db_inbox.py:1662-1664 — literal, never derived from the trial — while the columns exist for it (sql/14_agent_factory.sql:60-63) and the harness holds the fixture and verdict at that moment (harness.py:19-26). title: GET /eval/reports/{report_id} has no tenant predicate, unlike every other eval read

title: The canary auto-rollback trigger named "eval_fail" only ever samples red-team; a red regression or outbound report rolls nothing back
mechanism: The watchdog's eval branch is `if "eval_fail" in triggers: report = db.get_latest_eval_report(bot_id=exp["bot_id"], kind="redteam")` (canary.py:381-384). The trigger's name is generic and the Ship tab offers it as one choice; regression and outbound reports — the other two kinds the compiler gates on — are never read here. A card canarying at 40% whose nightly regression suite turns red keeps taking traffic, while the identical failure in the red-team suite pulls it. Note also that the report it samples is the newest for the bot with no version scoping, the same defect as EVALS-1, so the rollback can fire on a report belonging to a different version than the canary.
trigger: Publish with traffic_pct=40 and auto_rollback=["eval_fail"]. Let the nightly regression run fail. Nothing rolls back and no signal reaches the operator.
fix: Sample every kind the card requires (card.eval.require) rather than hardcoding redteam, or rename the trigger to redteam_fail so the Ship tab stops promising more than it does.
verify_reason: Verified at canary.py:381-384: `if "eval_fail" in triggers: report = db.get_latest_eval_report(bot_id=exp["bot_id"], kind="redteam")` and the rollback fires only when that red-team report is 'fail'. No branch anywhere in the watchdog samples kind='regression' or kind='outbound', although both are gate kinds at publish (compile.py:716, :464) and "eval_fail" is offered as one generic trigger in the shared vocabulary (schema.py:41-49 RollbackTrigger). So a canary at traffic_pct=40 whose nightly regression suite turns red keeps taking traffic. The version-scoping caveat is real too — get_latest_eval_report is bot-keyed only (db_inbox.py:1592).

title: The Twin hint claims replays of real calls; no eval suite of any kind executes the candidate agent
mechanism: The Twin checkbox's hint reads "replays of real calls against the candidate" (AgentCardPanels.tsx:256). title: A suites-query failure renders as "no suites" and falsely tells the operator their pinned suite does not exist
mechanism: useEvalSuites has no isPending/isError branch anywhere in EvalsTab; every read is `(suitesQuery.data ?? [])`. Two consequences. (a) The suite list at :421-443 renders empty on both first paint and outright failure, so "there are no suites to run" is indistinguishable from "the suite catalogue could not be loaded" — the operator concludes evals are not configured for this tenant. (b) The staleness check at :377-379 is `card.eval?.suite_id && !(suitesQuery.data ?? []).some(...)`, so with data undefined it asserts, in a warning lozenge, `<suite id> is not a suite that exists`. That statement is false on every mount of a card with a pinned suite and stays on screen permanently if /eval/suites is down. This is the same class as prior finding 2i.1 on the Connectors tab, which was rated MAJOR.

But MAJOR is inflated. (b) The empty Run list is an ambiguous empty state, not business advice: unlike prior 2i.1, which told the author to go approve connectors on Integrations while the live API returned two, nothing here instructs an action or contradicts live data. title: An exception inside a grader aborts the whole run, files no report, and the 'error' status the schema reserves is never written
mechanism: run_suite_fixtures loops `verdict = run_grader(...)` with no try/except (harness.py:19-21) and computes status as only "pass" or "fail" (harness.py:28). eval_reports.status permits 'error' (sql/14_agent_factory.sql:47) and nothing can ever produce it. grade_skill_jailbreak imports agent_core.skills.intersect at call time (graders.py:125-126) and grade_crm_card_injection calls into prompt_render (graders.py:61), so a broken import or a renderer exception on one task propagates out of run_named_suite before save_eval_report is reached (run.py:91-92) — the whole suite is lost, no report row exists, and the endpoint 500s. Combined with EVALS-5 the operator sees nothing at all; the gate then reports "suite has not been run" as if nobody had tried.
trigger: Any exception in one grader (renderer change, missing module, malformed fixture producing a TypeError) discards the other N-1 graded trials and files no report.
fix: Wrap run_grader per task, record the failure as a failed trial with the exception text, and set the report status to 'error' when any trial errored — the vocabulary the table already reserves and that reportTone (AgentCardPanels.tsx:49) already renders.
verify_reason: Verified, with line corrections. run_suite_fixtures loops `verdict = run_grader(...)` with no try/except (harness.py:14-15) and computes status as only pass/fail (harness.py:27), while eval_reports.status permits 'error' (sql/14_agent_factory.sql:47) — nothing in the repo writes it. run_grader itself only converts an UNKNOWN grader name into a failing verdict (graders.py end-of-file dispatch); an exception inside a grader body propagates: grade_skill_jailbreak imports agent_core.skills.intersect at call time (graders.py:122-125) and grade_crm_card_injection calls format_untrusted_crm_card (graders.py:61). The raise escapes run_suite_fixtures before save_eval_report is reached (run.py:89-99), and the endpoint catches only KeyError (main.py:2790-2793), so it 500s, no report row exists and the other N-1 graded trials are discarded. Combined with EVALS-5 the operator gets no message, and the gate then reads as "suite has not been run" (compile.py:969).
