title: Debt-word leak graders match substrings, so a compliant voicemail containing "reminder" is graded as disclosing a debt
mechanism: _DEBT_WORDS includes "emi" and "due" (graders.py:207,211) and all three consumers test membership with a bare substring `w in script` / `w in said` / `w in first` (graders.py:256, 276, 393) against a lower-cased join, with no word boundary. "emi" is a substring of "reminder"/"remind"/"reminders" — the single most likely word in a compliant callback voicemail — and of "chemistry", "academic" etc.; "due" catches any token containing it. The failure detail then reads "voicemail names emi", which points the operator at a word that is not in their script.
trigger: Author an outbound task whose voicemail_script is "This is a reminder to call us back on 1800 123 4567; our grievance officer is on the same line." — a message that discloses nothing — and grade_voicemail_discloses_nothing fails it. The same substring rule fails an opening turn of "Reminder — am I speaking with Vikram?" in grade_outbound_opens_by_confirming. The shipped fixtures happen to avoid the word (fixtures.py:250-256), so the seeded suite is green and the trap is latent.
fix: Match on word boundaries — tokenise, or use re.search(rf"\\b{re.escape(w)}\\b", text) — and keep the list of stems explicit.
verify_reason: Verified, with two line corrections: "emi" is graders.py:209 and "due" is :211 (tuple opens at :201). All three consumers use bare substring membership over a lower-cased join with no word boundary: graders.py:256 (`w in script`, voicemail), :276 (`w in said`, third party) and :393 (`w in first`, outbound opening). "emi" is a substring of "reminder"/"remind", so a compliant callback voicemail fails grade_voicemail_discloses_nothing with the detail "voicemail names emi" (:262-263), a word the operator never wrote. Latent only because the shipped fixtures avoid it (fixtures.py PUBLISH_OUTBOUND_TASKS) — the trap fires on any author-supplied voicemail_script or opening turn.

title: Archive does not stop handoffs to the retired card: G5 and db.handoff_to_agent accept archived targets, so 'stops taking traffic immediately' is enforced nowhere
mechanism: Archive only retires bot_deployments rows (db_prompt_studio.py:670-680). The publish compiler's G5 builds known_bots from `SELECT id FROM bots` with no archived filter (:1877) so a caller card keeps or newly gains a handoff to an archived bot with a green gate (compile.py:665-678); db.handoff_to_agent only checks `SELECT 1 FROM bots WHERE id=:id` (db_inbox.py:1459) and then sets interactions.handler_bot_id to the archived bot. Nothing in voice/, bot_runtime.py or agent_core/tools reads archived_at. The AlertDialog copy 'the card stops taking traffic immediately' (index.tsx:728) describes only the deployment row; the conversation graph still routes to it and analytics/QA/compliance attribute those interactions to a retired bot (canary.py:206, live_qa/scorecard.py:265, compliance/context.py:166).
trigger: Archive a clone that appears in Collections' handoffs; publish Collections (G5 passes); on a live call have the model call handoff_to_agent(target=<archived clone>) — it succeeds and handler_bot_id becomes the archived id.
fix: Filter known_bots to `archived_at IS NULL` in publish (and in compile preview), and have db.handoff_to_agent raise ValueError('target_bot_archived'); soften the dialog copy until then.
verify_reason: Verified all four legs. archive_agent_studio_card sets bots.archived_at and flips only bot_deployments to 'retired' (db_prompt_studio.py:656-690); nothing else changes. publish_prompt_version builds `known_bots = {r["id"] for r in _rows(conn.execute(text("SELECT id FROM bots")))}` (db_prompt_studio.py:1877) with no archived filter, and G5 only tests membership in that set (compile.py:661-678), so a caller card can keep or newly add a handoff to an archived bot and pass green. db_inbox.handoff_to_agent's only target check is `SELECT 1 FROM bots WHERE id = :id` (db_inbox.py:1459) before it writes handler_bot_id. The archived_at grep across backend/*.py confirms no reference in voice/, bot_runtime.py, agent_core/tools/ or agent_core/deployment.py. The AlertDialog copy "the card stops taking traffic immediately" (index.tsx:726) is therefore true only of the deployment row. MINOR is right: reachable on the text channel (the caller's published card must still list the archived target, so _handoff_allowlist passes), and on voice the Python-constant allowlist would happen to block an archived clone.

title: Template catalog failure renders as an empty dropdown with a disabled Create button — error as absence
mechanism: useAgentStudioTemplates() (index.tsx:389) exposes isError/isLoading, but the Clone panel reads only templates.data: the <select> maps `(templates.data ?? [])` (:491), templateId stays '' (:430-439), and Create is disabled by `!templateId` (:503) with no reason. A 5xx or network failure on GET /agent-studio/templates therefore looks identical to a tenant with no templates: a blank select and a dead button, no message, no Retry — the same pattern the fleet grid itself handles correctly at :527-542.
trigger: Make GET /agent-studio/templates fail (API down mid-session, 500), click 'Clone card'.
fix: Branch on templates.isLoading / templates.isError inside the panel (spinner, then an error line with a Retry that calls templates.refetch), and give the disabled Create a reason via ReasonedAction.
verify_reason: index.tsx:389 `const templates = useAgentStudioTemplates()` and the panel then reads only `templates.data`: the <select> maps `(templates.data ?? [])` (:491-495), the seeding effect returns early on an empty list (:433-439 `if (!rows.length) return;`) leaving templateId '', and Create draft is `disabled={clone.isPending || !templateId}` (:503) with no reason surfaced (it is a plain Button, not the ReasonedAction used elsewhere). useAgentStudioTemplates (agent-studio.ts:787-819) exposes isError/isLoading; neither is read. A 500 on GET /agent-studio/templates is pixel-identical to an empty catalog. MINOR stands — contained to the clone panel, and the same file handles the fleet grid's error correctly at :527-542, which is what makes it an inconsistency rather than a house style.

title: Eval trend dots come from the tenant's newest 50 reports and vanish silently on error, so 'no dots' means nothing
mechanism: useEvalReports() is called with no kind/botId/limit (index.tsx:392; agent-studio.ts:415-419 builds an empty query string), so the server applies `limit: int = Query(default=50)` (main.py:2817) over the whole tenant newest-first. A card whose last runs are older than the 50 most recent tenant-wide reports gets zero dots even though its evalStatus lozenge (server-side, per bot) says pass — two adjacent verdicts about the same history disagree. evalReports.isError is never read (index.tsx:392-399), so a failed request also renders as 'no recent runs' (EvalTrend returns null at :102).
trigger: Run the eval schedule a few times on a busy tenant (or run one suite 50+ times on kaia-v2-4), then look at any other card's row.
fix: Either fetch per-bot with a small limit (useEvalReports(undefined, botId) inside the card, or a server aggregate 'last 3 per bot'), and render an explicit error/empty state instead of null when evalReports.isError.
verify_reason: index.tsx:392 calls `useEvalReports()` with no arguments; the hook builds an empty query string when kind and botId are absent (agent-studio.ts:414-419), and the server applies `limit: int = Query(default=50, ge=1, le=200)` (main.py:2818) over `WHERE r.tenant_id = :tenant ... ORDER BY r.created_at DESC LIMIT :n` (db_inbox.py:1671-1700) — tenant-wide newest 50, then grouped client-side into reportsByBot (:393-399). A card whose runs fall outside that window gets an empty bucket and EvalTrend returns null (:101-102), rendering nothing, while the server-computed per-bot evalStatus lozenge on the same row still says pass. evalReports.isError is never read anywhere in the file, so a failed request is also silence. MINOR: contained to a decorative trend indicator, but it is the second verdict about the same history and it disagrees with the first.

title: 'Clone card' clones a code template, not the card: tenant edits to the source's published card are dropped while its prompt/flow are copied
mechanism: The UI always sends templateId (index.tsx:505-506), so clone_card takes `card = template_card(template)` (clone.py:42-43), which starts from card_dump(<first-party constant>) (templates.py:128,150,158,166) — the published card's `agentCard` is used only on the sourceBotId path the UI never exercises (:44-45). Meanwhile prompt, persona, voice, guardrails and flow ARE taken from the source's published version (:70-74). A tenant who removed tools, added a connector, changed handoffs or configured outbound on Collections and then clicks 'Clone card' → 'Collections' gets the shipped default card with their edited mouth: mixed provenance the header copy ('clone a card, attach connectors, canary, then ship', :448-449) does not disclose, and the button is labelled 'Clone card' while the panel says 'Clone a template'.
trigger: Edit kaia-v2-4's Tools tab to drop three tools and publish; Clone card → Collections; open the clone's Tools tab: all 23 default tools are back, but the flow/prompt are the tenant's.
fix: Either derive the template from the source's published card when one exists (apply template deltas on top of it) or rename the control 'New agent from template' and state in the panel that the card comes from the template while the mouth comes from the source's published version.
verify_reason: clone_card (clone.py:41-49): `if template: card = template_card(template)` wins over the published-card branch, which is only reachable when template_id is empty. template_card (templates.py:124-171) starts every branch from card_dump(<first-party constant>) — lapse from INSURANCE_BOT_ID, hardship and the default from COLLECTIONS_BOT_ID, clerk from SUPERVISOR_BOT_ID — i.e. shipped code, never the tenant's published card. Meanwhile clone.py:70-87 takes prompt, persona, voice, guardrails and flow from `db.get_published_prompt_version(source)`. The UI has no sourceBotId path at all: useCloneAgentCard's body type is `{templateId: string; name?: string}` (agent-studio.ts:822-829) and the call site sends `{templateId, name}` (index.tsx:505-506). So a tenant who dropped tools or edited handoffs on Collections and clicks Clone card → Collections gets the shipped default card with their edited prompt/flow. Header copy is "clone a card, attach connectors, canary, then ship" (index.tsx:448-449) while the panel title is "Clone a template" (:467). MINOR is correct — surprising provenance and misleading copy, no wrong runtime behaviour (the clone is a draft and must pass the compiler before it ships).

title: 'direct only' claims the card is addressable by bot id, but no production entry point ever passes a bot id other than BOT_ID
mechanism: The `direct` state exists so Intake (live deployment, no inbound edge) is not called unreachable, and its help says 'Addressed directly by bot id — it has its own live deployment' (index.tsx:72-73; routing.py:17-21). The full caller list of load_active_bundle is voice/bot.py:427 (no bot_id → DEFAULT_BOT_ID), bot_runtime.py:712 (env BOT_ID), copilot.py:285 (handler_bot_id, display chip only), sandbox_runtime.py:512 (no bot_id; explicit promptVersionId otherwise). No inbound channel, dialler or router resolves a card by bot id, so for inbound traffic 'direct only' is operationally the same as 'unreachable' rendered in a calmer information tone. It also blocks nothing: the chip is purely descriptive.
trigger: Look at Intake on the fleet: 'direct only' in information tone, while established runtime facts say every inbound call resolves BOT_ID and handoff_to_agent never loads Intake's bundle.
fix: Reword the help to 'Has a live deployment but no inbound route today — only the sandbox and copilot can load it' and use warning tone, or drop `direct` until a router that dispatches by bot id exists.
verify_reason: Enumerated every load_active_bundle caller with a targeted grep over backend/*.py: bot_runtime.py:712 (bot_id=_bot_id(), env BOT_ID), voice/bot.py:427 (no bot_id → DEFAULT_BOT_ID), sandbox_runtime.py:512 (no bot_id; an explicit promptVersionId short-circuits the call entirely), agent_core/copilot.py:285 (bot_id = interactions.handler_bot_id, used only to read display_name and skills for a chip), and deployment.py:133 inside resolve_prompt_bundle, whose only non-test caller is voice/bot.py:404-406 on a sandbox session's promptVersionId. No inbound channel, dialler or router resolves a card by bot id, so the `direct` help text "Addressed directly by bot id — it has its own live deployment" (index.tsx:69-74) describes a dispatch path that does not exist for inbound traffic, and it is rendered in information tone, which is what separates it from `unreachable`'s warning tone. MINOR: descriptive copy only (the chip gates nothing), but it is on the exact screen whose stated job is to distinguish live routing from dead config.

title: 'Line spoken on entry' is ignored on 'Say verbatim' nodes, yet the validator demands it for listen-first outbound entries
mechanism: flows_dynamic.py:386-392 handles `instructionType == 'say'` by emitting a single tts_say pre_action from `instructions`; `entry_line` is only emitted in the else branch (:399-407). The inspector shows the entry-line field whenever 'Listen before speaking' is on, regardless of instruction type (FlowInspector.tsx:710-722), and the card renders it as spoken (FlowNodes.tsx:416). silent_outbound_entry (flow_graph.py:562-575) errors on `not respondImmediately and not entryLine` even though a say node speaks its text on entry, so the author is forced to add a line that is then discarded.
trigger: Make a 'Say verbatim' step the entry for dpd_reminder with 'Listen before speaking' on; validator errors; add an entry line; publish; the line is never spoken.
fix: In the say branch prepend the entry line as a second tts_say (or hide the field for say nodes) and make silent_outbound_entry accept a non-empty say text as speech on entry.
verify_reason: backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py:386-392: when `node.data.instructionType == 'say' and instructions`, the config gets a single `tts_say` pre_action built from `instructions` and a fixed 'you have just said the scripted line' task message — `entry_line` is computed at :385 but only used in the else branch (:399-407), so it is discarded on say nodes. The inspector shows the 'Line spoken on entry' field on `!node.data.respondImmediately` alone, with no instructionType test (Habibi/src/components/flow/FlowInspector.tsx:706-725), and the node card renders it as spoken text regardless (FlowNodes.tsx:416, `{(d.entryLine ?? '').trim() && <SpokenLine label="on entry" .../>}`). backend/flow_graph.py:562-573 silent_outbound_entry errors on `not node.data.respondImmediately and not node.data.entryLine.strip()` for every non-inbound entry node, again without consulting instructionType — so an author making a 'Say verbatim' outbound door that listens first is forced to add a line the runtime then drops.

title: End-node instructions are consumed at runtime but hidden from the inspector
mechanism: For `type == 'end'` flows_dynamic renders `node.data.instructions` as the farewell developer message, falling back to 'Close the call politely in one short sentence.' (:373-378). NodeInspector wraps every content section in `!isEnd &&` (FlowInspector.tsx:661), so the farewell can never be seen or edited: a reloaded built-in graph carries _FAREWELL_TASK on call_ended invisibly, and a hand-added End node (emptyGraph flow.ts:191-207 or the 'End' button) ships the hardcoded fallback with no way to change wording.
trigger: Select the End node: no instruction field; publish; the farewell wording is whatever the JSON holds.
fix: Show a single 'Farewell line' textarea for end nodes bound to data.instructions (and render it on the EndNode card).
verify_reason: backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py:370-380: for `node.type == 'end'` the config's task_messages is `[{role:'developer', content: variables.render(node.data.instructions) or 'Close the call politely in one short sentence.'}]` — the farewell is read from the node. In NodeInspector every content section after Identity is wrapped in `{!isEnd && (<>...</>)}` (Habibi/src/components/flow/FlowInspector.tsx:659-661 onward), so an end node's inspector shows only Name, Key and Delete: the farewell text can neither be seen nor edited. Confirms both consequences named: an export carries call_ended's _FAREWELL_TASK invisibly (flow_export.py:187 sets type 'end' for call_ended and _instructions fills data.instructions), and a hand-added End node from emptyGraph ships `instructions: ""` (Habibi/src/api/flow.ts:198-210) so the hardcoded fallback is spoken with no way to change it.

title: 'moves' badge is a hand list that misses four tools whose ghost edges the canvas draws (capture_call_goal, flag_dispute, request_callback, capture_lead)
mechanism: `transitions` in /flow/tools comes from the frozenset _TRANSITIONING_TOOLS (flow_graph.py:788-803, :828), while ghost edges come from the AST reader implicit_transitions(). tools.py returns `_node(...)` from capture_call_goal (:682), flag_dispute (:1391), request_callback (:1608) and capture_lead (:2358) — and test_flow_transitions.py:81-82 asserts two of them — but none is in the frozenset. test_flow_tool_catalog.py:60-64 only checks the listed keys are flagged, not the converse. So ToolRow shows no 'moves' badge (FlowInspector.tsx:379) and the node card no arrow for tools that do transition, while the canvas draws their hop.
trigger: Tick request_callback on a node: no 'moves' badge, yet a dotted edge to wrap_up appears.
fix: Compute `transitions` as `key in implicit_transitions()` (or assert `_TRANSITIONING_TOOLS == set(implicit_transitions())` in the test).
verify_reason: backend/flow_graph.py:788-804 declares _TRANSITIONING_TOOLS as a hand-written frozenset of twelve keys, and tool_catalog reports `"transitions": key in _TRANSITIONING_TOOLS` (:828). Ghost edges come from the independent AST reader implicit_transitions() (:856+), consumed by the canvas via /flow/transitions (FlowCanvas.tsx:550-593). I located the four claimed tools' `_node(...)` returns and their enclosing handlers by def boundaries in backend/voice/tools.py: line 682 `_node("verify_identity")` inside `_capture_call_goal_handler` (def at :628); line 1391 `_node("escalate_close")` inside `_flag_dispute_handler` (def at :1327); line 1608 `_node("wrap_up") if upsell_node else None` inside `_request_callback_handler` (def at :1546); line 2358 `_node("wrap_up") if upsell_node else None` inside `_capture_lead_handler` (def at :2273). None of the four is in the frozenset. backend/tests/test_flow_transitions.py:81-83 positively asserts `transitions['flag_dispute'] == ['escalate_close']` and `transitions['capture_call_goal'] == ['verify_identity']`, and backend/tests/test_flow_tool_catalog.py:61-64 only checks the forward direction (every frozenset member is flagged true), never the converse — so the drift is untested. Result: no 'moves' badge on ToolRow (FlowInspector.tsx:376-386) and no arrow on the node card, while the canvas draws their hop.

title: Export and runtime drop the non-tts pre_actions and the close-probe offer clause: summarize_context/mesh_activate_insurance are dead under an authored graph
mechanism: _entry_line keeps only `tts_say` pre_actions (flow_export.py:154), so gated_upsell's `summarize_context` and `mesh_activate_insurance` (flows.py:640-644) are not represented in FlowNodeData and flows_dynamic can only ever emit tts_say/function/end_conversation actions. bot.py:1515 and :1540 still register both actions on every call, so under VOICE_FLOW_GRAPH=auto with a published graph they are registered and never invoked (topic-hop summarisation is lost on the upsell hop). Likewise pre_close's `_PRE_CLOSE_TASK.format(offer=state.close_probe_offer_clause)` (flows.py:683-687) is rendered at export time with an empty offer, and flows_dynamic's pre_close special-case (:450-464) appends a KB message but never the live offer clause.
trigger: Publish the reloaded built-in graph; reach gated_upsell or pre_close on a call.
fix: Either add an explicit `actions: ["summarize_context", ...]` node field (validated against bot.py's registered names) or document in the export/tab that these hooks are built-in-only; render the pre_close offer clause in flows_dynamic when the node key is pre_close.
verify_reason: backend/voice/flow_export.py:143-159 _entry_line skips any pre_action whose type is not 'tts_say', and FlowNodeData (backend/flow_graph.py:148-181, extra='forbid') has no field for other actions — so gated_upsell's `"pre_actions": [{"type":"summarize_context"},{"type":"mesh_activate_insurance"}]` (backend/voice/flows.py:657-661) is not representable. backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py:384-407 and :496-505 can only ever emit tts_say pre_actions and function/end_conversation post_actions. backend/voice/bot.py:1499-1518 and :1519-1545 still register both actions on the FlowManager for every call, so under an authored graph they are live and never invoked — the topic-hop context summarisation is lost on the upsell hop. Separately, pre_close's `_PRE_CLOSE_TASK.format(offer=state.close_probe_offer_clause or '')` (flows.py:683-687) is rendered at export time against a stub session, so the exported instruction carries an empty offer, and flows_dynamic's pre_close special-case (:450-464) appends only the KB/end_call developer message, never the live offer clause.

title: Flow tab is shown for every card and its empty state claims the version 'runs the built-in collections script', but only the voice runtime reads the graph
mechanism: TABS always includes flow (lazy.tsx:1111). bot_runtime.py (WhatsApp/text) and sandbox_runtime.py contain no reference to `flow`/FlowGraph (grep: zero matches), and the only consumer is bot.py:1167-1176. The empty-state copy (lazy.tsx:1490-1500) tells the author of a text-channel card that this version 'runs the built-in collections script' and that loading the graph will change what it does, which is false for that channel; nothing in the tab says the graph governs voice only.
trigger: Open a WhatsApp-only card's Flow tab.
fix: State 'Voice calls only' in the tab header/empty state and, if the card has no voice channel, render the tab read-only with that note.
verify_reason: TABS is a plain array literal always containing `{ key: 'flow', label: 'Flow', icon: Workflow }` (Habibi/src/routes/prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1109-1111) with no channel test. `grep -n flow backend/bot_runtime.py` and `grep -n flow backend/sandbox_runtime.py` both return zero matches, so neither the WhatsApp/text runtime nor the text sandbox reads the column; the only consumer is backend/voice/bot.py:1167-1176 (`_authored = bundle.get('flow')` → voice_uses_authored_flow → build_authored_flow). The empty-state copy at lazy.tsx:1490-1500 nonetheless tells the author 'This version runs the built-in collections script … Load it here to turn it into a graph you own', which is false for a text-only card, and nothing in the tab says the graph governs voice only.

title: Runtime special-cases node keys (confirm_identity, escalate_close, pre_close) invisibly; confirm_identity is not in the reserved-key list the editor shows
mechanism: flows_dynamic appends extra developer messages when node.key is confirm_identity (:437-449) or escalate_close/pre_close (:450-464). The inspector's only hint about key semantics is RESERVED_NODE_KEYS (FlowInspector.tsx:614-628), which deliberately excludes confirm_identity (flow_graph.py:47-53) and says nothing about injected instructions, so an author renaming or reusing those keys changes behaviour they cannot see, and an author who reads the 'Reserved key' hint believes the list is exhaustive.
trigger: Rename node key confirm_identity to outbound_greet: the 'no tool before confirmation' guard silently disappears.
fix: Move the injected text into the exported node instructions (so it is visible and editable) or list these keys in /flow/reserved-keys with a 'runtime adds instructions' note.
verify_reason: backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py:433-449 appends an extra developer message when `node.key == 'confirm_identity'` ('Do not call any tool until the caller has spoken and confirmed they are the account holder'), and :450-462 appends another when `node.key in {'escalate_close','pre_close'}` — neither is in the node's authored instructions. The only key-semantics hint in the editor is the reserved-key FieldLabel hint fed by /flow/reserved-keys (FlowInspector.tsx ~637-651, `reservedHint ? <>Reserved key. {reservedHint} : 'The stable name the runtime transitions by…'`), and backend/flow_graph.py:49-53 explicitly excludes confirm_identity with a comment explaining why, while none of the three entries mention injected instructions. So renaming confirm_identity silently removes the no-tool-before-confirmation guard, and the hint reads as an exhaustive list of the keys that matter. Note the auditor's FlowInspector line range is stale — the reserved-key hint is at roughly 637-651, not 614-628.

title: Condition/variable editor advertises no variable names; flows_dynamic's claim that SESSION_VARIABLES is 'the contract the Flow editor advertises' is false
mechanism: SESSION_VARIABLES (call_goal, identity_verified, outstanding, …) plus date/time are the only system names an instruction can interpolate or an edge can test, but no endpoint exposes them (grep: only flows_dynamic.py/flow_export.py reference the tuple) and the inspector offers a free-text `variable` input (FlowInspector.tsx:935-941) and a generic '{{variable}}' hint (:692-695). A typo renders literally into the developer message (flow_vars.py:98-110, by design) and an expression edge on it evaluates false forever, with no validator warning.
trigger: Type `{{customer_name}}` in a step or `identity_verfied is true` on an edge: validates green, never resolves.
fix: Expose GET /flow/variables (SESSION_VARIABLES + date/time) and offer a datalist of system + captured variables in both editors; warn in validate_graph on unknown names.
verify_reason: SESSION_VARIABLES is declared at backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py:81-93 with the comment 'Keys are the contract the Flow editor advertises'. A targeted grep across backend/main.py, backend/flow_graph.py, backend/schemas.py, backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py and backend/voice/flow_export.py finds the name only at flows_dynamic.py:83 — no endpoint exposes it, and there is no /flow/variables route in main.py's flow block (:2058-2101). The editor offers a free-text `variable` Input in the clause editor (FlowInspector.tsx:940-946) and only a generic '{{variable}}' hint on the instructions field (:692-695). A misspelled name renders literally by design (backend/voice/flow_vars.py:98-110 leaves unknown keys as written) and an expression clause on it returns False via the `actual is None` branch (flow_vars.py:127-129), with no validator rule for unknown variable names anywhere in validate_graph. One correction to the mechanism text: flow_export.py does NOT reference the tuple — flows_dynamic.py is the only file that does, which makes the claim slightly stronger, not weaker.

title: Graph-level 'Tools available from every step' offers four CRM reads that flows_dynamic silently strips from globals
mechanism: GraphInspector renders the full catalog as global-tool checkboxes and counts the selection in its label (FlowInspector.tsx:500). validate_graph only checks membership in the catalog (flow_graph.py:517-519). flows_dynamic.py:510-518 builds global_functions excluding get_customer_context, get_payment_history, get_emi_schedule and request_documents with no log and no validator warning, so an author who adds them as globals sees a green graph and a counter that includes tools the runtime never exposes.
trigger: Deselect everything, tick request_documents under 'Tools available from every step', publish: the tool is offered on no node.
fix: Either drop the strip (the card grant already decides exposure) or surface it: emit a validate_graph warning `global_not_allowed` for those keys and disable the rows in GraphInspector with the reason.
verify_reason: GraphInspector renders the full /flow/tools array as global-tool checkboxes and puts the selection count in the section label (Habibi/src/components/flow/FlowInspector.tsx:499-521, ToolList at :406-435 with `tools={toolsQuery.data ?? []}` from FlowCanvas.tsx:1318). validate_graph's only global-tool rule is membership in the catalog: `for tool in graph.globalTools: if tools and tool not in tools: err('unknown_tool', ...)` (backend/flow_graph.py:511-513). backend/voice/flows_dynamic.py:507-518 then builds `global_functions = [tools[key] for key in graph.globalTools if key in tools and key not in _crm_reads]` where _crm_reads = {get_customer_context, get_payment_history, get_emi_schedule, request_documents} — no log line, no validator warning. So a green graph and a counter that includes four tools the runtime never exposes anywhere. Contained (the strip mirrors the built-in script's own policy); MINOR is right.

title: Validator outage reports '0 flow errors — publish blocked' and a stale canvas verdict; the off-canvas path still keeps the last verdict
mechanism: On a failed /flow/validate the canvas now reports `{ok:false, issues:[warning validator_unreachable]}` (FlowCanvas.tsx:505-517) — but it does not put that warning into its own `issues`, so the toolbar pill and the GraphInspector issue list keep showing the previous verdict (dimmed) with nothing about the outage. The parent sets flowValid=false (lazy.tsx:745) while flowErrorCount counts severity=error only, so the header renders '0 flow errors — publish blocked' (StudioHeader.tsx:100) and Publish toasts 'Fix conversation-flow errors before publishing' (lazy.tsx:942) with no error to fix. Off the Flow tab the effect at lazy.tsx:724-731 still swallows the failure and keeps the last verdict with the gate starting open (:227) — the original 2b.4 shape.

fix: Merge the validator_unreachable issue into the canvas `issues` and treat it as blocking in the header copy ('flow not checked — publish blocked'); apply the same unreachable handling in the lazy.tsx:724 effect.

FlowCanvas.tsx:481-518: the .catch calls `onValidationRef.current?.({ok:false, issues:[{severity:'warning', code:'validator_unreachable', ...}]})` but never calls setIssues, and never updates validatedGraph — so the canvas's own `issues` state, which feeds issuesByNode/issuesByEdge and the GraphInspector IssueList (`issues={issues}`, FlowCanvas.tsx:1320), keeps the previous verdict with nothing about the outage. In the parent, onFlowValidation sets flowValid = r.ok = false (lazy.tsx:744-746) while StudioHeader receives `publishBlocked={!flowValid}` and `flowErrorCount={flowIssues.filter(i => i.severity === 'error').length}` (lazy.tsx:1267-1268) — the only issue is a warning, so StudioHeader.tsx:98-101 renders literally '0 flow errors — publish blocked', and publish() toasts 'Fix conversation-flow errors before publishing' (lazy.tsx:941-942) with no error to fix. Off the Flow tab the parent's own effect still swallows the failure with `/* transient: keep the last known result */` (lazy.tsx:729-731) over a gate that starts open (`useState(true)`, lazy.tsx:227) — the original 2b.4 shape, so 2b.4 remains open on that path. New information beyond 2b.4 (the '0 errors — blocked' copy and the canvas's unmerged warning) so not a duplicate.

title: MissionEntries renders a failed vocabulary query as 'No outbound missions available' and hides the node's existing entryFor claims
mechanism: The section branches on `missions.length === 0` and distinguishes only `vocab.isPending`; `vocab.isError` falls through to 'No outbound missions available. They come from the card vocabulary.' (FlowInspector.tsx:203-206) — an error rendered as a business statement, the pattern 2i.1 flagged on Connectors. The checkbox list is the only view of `node.data.entryFor`, so while the query fails a node's existing claims are neither visible nor removable, yet G-OB2 keeps failing on them.
trigger: Break /outbound/card-vocabulary (or open the inspector while it 500s) and select the confirm_identity node.

verify_reason: MissionEntries (Habibi/src/components/flow/FlowInspector.tsx:183-231) computes `missions = (vocab.data?.objectives ?? []).filter(m => m !== 'inbound')` and branches on `missions.length === 0`, distinguishing only `vocab.isPending`; every other reason — including isError — falls through to 'No outbound missions available. They come from the card vocabulary.' (:203-205), an error rendered as a business statement. The checkbox list built from `missions.map(...)` is the only rendering of `node.data.entryFor` in the inspector (claimed is only used as `checked={claimed.includes(mission)}`), so while the query fails the node's existing entryFor claims are neither shown nor removable, while G-OB2 (backend/agent_core/cards/compile.py:298-330) keeps failing publish on them. useOutboundVocabulary has no error surface of its own (Habibi/src/api/outbound.ts:282-290).

title: ToolList shows 'Tool catalog unavailable.' for loading, error and empty alike; a node's attached tools vanish from the inspector

FlowCanvas hands the inspectors `tools={toolsQuery.data ?? []}` with no pending/error signal at FlowCanvas.tsx:1281 (NodeInspector) and :1318 (GraphInspector). ToolList's only empty branch is `tools.length === 0 ?

Tool catalog unavailable.

` (FlowInspector.tsx:418-423), which therefore covers loading, error and genuinely-empty identically. title: Intake's HumanGate on handoff_to_agent (require identity) has no enforcer

The `payload` arg ('Compact JSON context for the receiving card', catalog.py:591) is stringified, passed to db_inbox.handoff_to_agent, echoed in the return dict (:1507) and then discarded: the UPDATE (:1479-1492) and _activity row (:1493-1501) do not store it, and domain.py:1071-1080 does not surface it either. A grep for payload_schema across backend/*.py returns only schema.py:122, templates.py:139 (stamping an empty dict into a template) and three tests; across Habibi/src only the TS type and the AgentCardPanels.tsx:607 comment explaining the spread. title: A handoff to an archived (or other-tenant) bot passes G5 and is invisible and unremovable in the editable allowlist
mechanism: G5's known_bot_ids is list_bot_ids() = `SELECT id FROM bots` with no archived_at and no tenant predicate, so a handoff to a retired card (or another tenant's bot id) passes the gate. The graph endpoint's nodes come from list_agent_studio_cards() with include_archived=False (:2291, :326), so the archived target has no node; the editable UI renders rows only for nodes (:685-687), so the stale edge is not listed and has no Remove button, while legalTargets (:615) still treats it as a legal walk. At runtime db_inbox.handoff_to_agent:1459 also accepts the archived bot, so the hop is a no-op re-attribution to a card that takes no traffic. Reachability correctly excludes archived cards' edges, so the two vocabularies disagree about the same edge.
trigger: Allow a cloned card as a target, archive that clone on the fleet index, return to the source card's graph tab: the edge vanishes from the editor, compile stays green, and the published card keeps a dead handoff.
fix: In compile_agent_studio_card pass known_bot_ids filtered to non-archived bots of the current tenant (or add an archived_at IS NULL / tenant predicate to list_bot_ids), and have the graph tab render card handoffs whose target is not a node as a removable 'unknown/retired target' row.
verify_reason: Every link verified. db_inbox.list_bot_ids (:1511-1514) is `SELECT id FROM bots` with no archived_at and no tenant_id predicate; db_prompt_studio.compile_agent_studio_card passes it straight into compile_card as known_bot_ids (:842), and compile.py:665 tests `h.to_bot_id not in known_bot_ids` — so an archived or other-tenant target passes G5. The graph endpoint's nodes come from `db.list_agent_studio_cards()` with the default include_archived=False (main.py:2291; db_prompt_studio.py:306, :326 appends ' AND archived_at IS NULL'), so the archived target has no node. The editable list renders `nodes.filter((n) => n.id !== botId).map(...)` (AgentCardPanels.tsx:685-687), so a card handoff whose target is not a node gets no row and no Remove button — while `edges`/`legalTargets` (:611-615) are built from card.handoffs and still report 'Legal walk'. At runtime db_inbox.handoff_to_agent:1458-1459 only checks `SELECT 1 FROM bots WHERE id = :id`, so the hop succeeds as a re-attribution to a card that takes no traffic. Reachability does exclude archived cards' edges (db_prompt_studio.py:351-356, _handoff_edges' `b.archived_at IS NULL`), so the two vocabularies genuinely disagree about one edge. MINOR is right: contained, needs the archive step, and the worst outcome is a dead handoff plus an unremovable row.

title: Graph tab renders a failed or pending /graph fetch as an empty allowlist
mechanism: useAgentGraph's isPending/isError are never read (the component only destructures data at :588). On error or while loading, nodes=[] so the chip row and the 'Handoff allowlist' list render empty, the hint reads 'Select a card above…', and if the card has no handoffs the dashed box asserts 'No handoffs on this card. Every conversation stays on <bot>' — a statement of fact made without data. A card with handoffs shows chips-less edges and no target rows, so Remove is unavailable with no explanation.

title: Tool-driven voice handoff flips the mesh role without publishing it; the flow pre_action does both
mechanism: voice/tools.py:2805 calls voice_mesh.activate_role directly, so no mesh.role event is published and no BusActivateWorkerMessage reaches the insurance LLMWorker sidecar, whereas the two flow-driven paths (bot.py:1115, :1528) go through mesh_bus.activate_and_publish with customer/interaction/bot ids. Under Redis the sidecar and Floor observers therefore see handoffs made by the flow but not those made by the model calling handoff_to_agent; under local bus neither path changes behaviour (GRAPH-1).

title: escalateAbuse / escalateLegal cannot switch escalation off on voice (or abuse on WhatsApp); the toggles only edit the prompt line and a flag
mechanism: On voice, CrmSink's customer-turn tripwire calls detect_abuse / detect_legal unconditionally and escalates via _trigger_escalate → _live_escalate (crm_sink.py:943-945, 824-848; bot.py:1568-1577) without consulting self.guardrails. On WhatsApp hard_abuse = lexicon.is_abusive(customer_text) is unconditional (bot_runtime.py:815, 823-826); only the legal path is gated through evaluate_guardrails' auto-escalate (guardrails.py:217-223). On WhatsApp hard_abuse = lexicon.is_abusive(customer_text) at bot_runtime.py:815 is likewise unconditional and escalates at :823-831, while the legal path does run through evaluate_guardrails' escalateLegal-gated 'auto-escalate' (guardrails.py:208-215). So both switches change the '## Guardrails' prompt line (prompt.py:88-92) and whether an 'auto-escalate' flag is written, but not whether a live call or thread is handed to a human — the switch labelled 'Escalate on abusive language' (GuardrailsPanel.tsx:17-21) does not control escalation on abusive language. title: Turn critic tells the live model it 'broke a compliance rule' for session-limit and caller-conduct flags
mechanism: crm_sink passes every flag returned by evaluate_and_flag_bot_turn to enqueue_critique (crm_sink.py:1560-1565). _guardrail_correction has no filter (turn_critic.py:172-186) and, for any non-omission flag, injects 'Your last reply broke a compliance rule (max-turns). Do not repeat that wording' (:207-212). persist.py:588-593 explicitly documents 'max-turns', 'max-seconds', 'auto-escalate' and 'politics-religion' as flags describing the caller or a session limit, not bot misconduct — so once maxTurns/maxSeconds is crossed on a voice call the model receives a high-severity correction about a mistake it did not make, spending one of the per-call correction budget slots (crm_sink.py:638-649).

Do not repeat that wording…' at SEVERITY_HIGH. persist.py:588-593 documents those exact four names as describing the caller or a session limit, not bot misconduct. Each such correction consumes a slot of the per-call/per-kind budget (crm_sink.py:630-650, turn_critic.MAX_CORRECTIONS_PER_CALL). elapsed_seconds on voice is real (crm_sink.py:1534 at_sec), so the maxSeconds trigger is reachable on any call past the configured 480s. MINOR is the right severity: the directive is wrong and wastes a correction slot, but it is contained to one nudge per rule per call.

title: Sandbox judges the voice-only disclosure guardrail against a prompt that tells the model it is in a text chat and must not disclose
mechanism: assemble_turn_messages calls build_system_prompt without a channel (turn.py:78-84), so the sandbox system message takes channel='text' (prompt.py:151), drops the disclosure rule and adds 'This is NOT a phone call ... never state a call-recording disclosure' (prompt.py:120-127). sandbox_runtime.py:897-906 nevertheless evaluates alwaysDiscloseRecording and reports 'missing-recording-disclosure' on every bot turn of any run whose persona openingBot does not itself disclose (recording_disclosed comes only from history, :755-761). The model cannot clear the flag without violating its prompt; test_the_flag_still_fires_when_nothing_ever_disclosed pins the behaviour. The Guardrails tab's 'Prompt rehearsal' therefore shows a compliance flag the voice runtime would not raise the same way (voice's greet_disclose node always discloses).

title: Lint 'recording_disclosure_unenforced' claims nothing on the card discloses recording, but inbound voice always discloses via the greet_disclose flow node
mechanism: With alwaysDiscloseRecording off and no disclosure in the prompt, lint_prompt warns 'Nothing on this card discloses call recording' (prompt_lint.py:156-170; mock mirror prompt-studio.ts:791-796). On inbound voice the entry node is greet_disclose (flows.py:942), whose task message says 'say the call is recorded for quality and compliance' and requires the disclose_recording tool (flows.py:213-222, 243), which records the disclosure and injects the never-repeat note (tools.py:579-613) — none of it conditioned on the toggle. On inbound voice the entry node is greet_disclose (flows.py:936-943 — entry is greet_disclose unless call_type == 'outbound'), whose task message orders 'say the call is recorded for quality and compliance' and whose functions require disclose_recording (flows.py:210-244); voice/tools.py:579-613 records the disclosure and injects the standing never-repeat note. title: The card-less bot's rollout baseline filters experiments by a status the schema forbids, so every Studio publish silently re-ships at 100% traffic
mechanism: `legacyShipBaseline` is the documented resting value and publish-diff baseline for a bot with no authored Agent Card: `const live = (experimentsQuery.data ?? []).find((e) => e.status === "active")` (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:460). `deployment_experiments.status` is constrained to `('running','rolled_back','promoted')` (sql/18_phase5.sql:13) and the only writer inserts `'running'` (canary.py:114-124), so `live` is always undefined and the memo always returns the hardcoded `{trafficPct:100, shadow:false, autoRollback:[]}` at :461. `DeploymentExperiment.status` is typed `string` (api/agent-studio.ts:457) so nothing catches it, and ShipTab.tsx:79 — reading the same list — uses the correct `'running'`, which is what makes this a typo rather than a convention. Consequences: (a) `ship = legacyShipEdit ?? legacyShipBaseline` (:469) resets to 100/false/[] on every reload, so the operator's canary setting is discarded exactly as the comment at :250-255 says must never happen again; (b) publish() sends `trafficPct: ship.trafficPct` = 100 (:958), and db_prompt_studio.py:1888 takes that over the card, so `record_experiment` promotes the running canary (canary.py:99-102) and inserts nothing new (pct>=100 returns early at :107); (c) `publishBaseline.rollout` (:1155) is the same always-100 object, so PublishDialog prints "Rollout: unchanged" (PublishDialog.tsx:216-226) on a publish that takes a 40% shadow canary to full production traffic.
trigger: On a bot whose agentCard has no `identity.bot_id` (isAuthoredCard false — every cloned/legacy card), set Canary traffic to 40% on the Ship tab and publish. Reload the Studio: the slider reads 100%. Publish again for any unrelated prompt edit — the dialog says "Rollout: unchanged" and the publish moves the bot to 100% traffic and marks the experiment 'promoted'.
fix: Change `e.status === "active"` to `e.status === "running"` at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:460, matching ShipTab.tsx:79. Then narrow `DeploymentExperiment.status` in api/agent-studio.ts:457 to `"running" | "promoted" | "rolled_back"` so the next such comparison fails to compile.
verify_reason: Mechanism is real and I reproduced it by reading: legacyShipBaseline matches e.status === "active" (lazy.tsx:460) against a column whose CHECK admits only running/rolled_back/promoted (sql/18_phase5.sql:13), the only writer inserts 'running' (canary.py:111-133) and list_experiments passes status through verbatim (canary.py:344), so the memo always returns the hardcoded {100,false,[]} at :461; ShipTab.tsx:79 uses the correct 'running', and publish sends ship.trafficPct (:958) which db takes over the card (db_prompt_studio.py:1890 — cited as 1888, off by two). What is inflated is the blast radius, and the trigger as written is wrong. isAuthoredCard is Boolean(card?.identity?.bot_id) and the card the Studio reads is never card-less: _agent_studio_card_summary resolves draft card -> published card -> card_dump -> scaffold_card and always returns one of them under "agentCard" (db_prompt_studio.py:429-441, 502), scaffold_card stamps identity.bot_id (defaults.py:367-370), and clone_card stamps identity.bot_id on every clone (clone.py:53-57) — so "every cloned/legacy card" is false, clones take the authored branch. asCard maps {} to null (lazy.tsx:141-144) so effectiveCard falls through to that always-authored card, and a failed card read blocks the editor entirely (lazy.tsx:1193-1208) rather than falling into the legacy branch. The legacy branch is therefore reachable only for a bot whose stored card is non-empty but carries no identity.bot_id (backend is_authored, schema.py:416-419, accepts any non-empty dict) — legacy data I cannot show exists here, and the prior audit already recorded this whole branch as dormant ("All four seeded bots are authored", AGENT_STUDIO_BUG_HUNT.md item 2m.4, which this finding does not cite). Real defect, worth fixing, but not "every Studio publish silently re-ships at 100%". What would settle MAJOR: one row of SELECT bot_id, agent_card FROM prompt_versions WHERE agent_card->'identity'->>'bot_id' IS NULL AND agent_card <> '{}' in a live tenant.

title: Deployment rollback never closes the running canary experiment, so the Ship tab keeps reporting a canary that routes nothing
mechanism: `rollback_bot_deployment` retires the active deployment, re-publishes the prior prompt version and inserts a fresh deployment row (db_prompt_studio.py:2368-2409). It never touches `deployment_experiments`: there is no `record_experiment` and no `rollback_experiment` call in the function, unlike publish (which promotes the running row at canary.py:99-102). The experiment therefore keeps `status='running'` while its `canary_deployment_id` points at a deployment now marked `rolled_back` (:2370-2377). ShipTab still renders "Running experiment — 40% canary" from that row (ShipTab.tsx:79, 216-227) and `sweep_rollbacks` keeps evaluating auto-rollback triggers for it (canary.py:355-365). The header's own rollback control (VersionHistory.tsx:179-189 → prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:992) is the button that produces this state.
trigger: Publish at 40% canary, then use Rollback in the version-history drawer. The Ship tab still shows a running 40% experiment for a deployment that is serving nothing.
fix: Inside the rollback transaction in db_prompt_studio.py (after the deployment swap at :2409), mark any `status='running'` experiment for this bot+environment as `'rolled_back'` with a reason of `'deployment_rollback'`, mirroring canary.py:175-183.
verify_reason: Confirmed by reading the whole function: rollback_bot_deployment (db_prompt_studio.py:2290-2424) archives the published version, republishes the target, marks the current deployment rolled_back (:2364-2374) and inserts a fresh active row (:2376-2394) — and touches deployment_experiments nowhere, in contrast to the publish path which promotes the running row via record_experiment (canary.py:99-102). The experiment therefore keeps status='running' with canary_deployment_id pointing at a deployment now marked rolled_back, so ShipTab keeps rendering "Running experiment — N% canary" from that row (ShipTab.tsx:79, 216-227) and sweep_rollbacks keeps selecting it (canary.py:351-365). Reachable through the UI on any card, authored or not: publish with the Ship slider below 100 (which is what makes record_experiment insert a row, canary.py:107-133), then use Rollback in the history drawer (VersionHistory.tsx:179-189 -> lazy.tsx:992). One thing the finding understates and I did not chase to a verdict: if the auto-rollback sweep later fires on that stale row, rollback_experiment reactivates the old baseline deployment (canary.py:160-170) while the rollback's own row is already active — a possible second active production deployment. That is a reason to fix it, not a reason to change the severity here.

title: restore-as-draft stores a NULL label, so publishing a restored version stamps a row id as the version label and the next label falls back to v1.0
mechanism: `restore_prompt_version_as_draft` inserts `"label": None` (db_prompt_studio.py:2252) with id `f"{source['id']}-r-{uuid4hex6}"` (:2221). `_map_prompt_version` then substitutes the id for the missing label (`label = r.get("label") or r.get("id")`, :180), so the API serves the restored draft as label `"v1_3-r-ab12cd"`. The editor picks that up as `draftLabel` (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:546-549) and `toPatchInput` sends `label: body.label` on every autosave (api/prompt-studio.ts:107), so patch_prompt_version writes that id string into the label column for real (db_prompt_studio.py:1729-1731). Publish it and `publishedRow.label` is `"v1_3-r-ab12cd"`; `nextVersionLabel` only matches `/^v\d+\.\d+$/` and otherwise returns the literal `"v1.0"` (prompt-studio-seed.ts:362-364). So `nextLabel` at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:541 collapses to v1.0 and the header offers "Publish v1.0" on a card that was at v1.6. The header lozenge also reads "v1_3-r-ab12cd published" (StudioHeader.tsx:81). Every one of those labels is hashed into the change-log entry (db_prompt_studio.py:1806, change_log.record_publish :2143-2156), which is the regulated record of what the agent was told to say and when. The VersionHistory docstring at VersionHistory.tsx:74-76 asserts the opposite behaviour ("A draft inherits the label of the version it descends from"), so nobody reading the UI would expect this.
trigger: Card is live at v1.6. Open History, click Restore on archived v1.3, type one character (autosave writes label), Publish. Header now reads "v1_3-r-ab12cd published" and the next Publish button says v1.0. The change log records the sequence v1.6 → v1_3-r-ab12cd → v1.0.
fix: In db_prompt_studio.py:2252 carry the source label across (`"label": src_label` — it is already computed at :2222) or mint a proper successor label there. Independently, harden prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:541 so a non-matching current label bumps from the newest matching `v<major>.<minor>` in history rather than resetting to v1.0.
verify_reason: Every link of the chain is real at the cited lines: restore inserts new_id = f"{source['id']}-r-{hex6}" (2221) with "label": None (2252); _map_prompt_version substitutes the id (label = r.get("label") or r.get("id"), :180); draftLabel picks that up (lazy.tsx:546-549); toPatchInput always sends label (prompt-studio.ts:106-107) and patch_prompt_version writes it (db_prompt_studio.py:1724-1726 — cited as 1729-1731, off by five); publish PATCHes with the same label before publishing (prompt-studio.ts:970-983), so publishedRow.label becomes the id string, nextVersionLabel's regex misses and returns the literal "v1.0" (seed:362-364), and the header renders both (StudioHeader.tsx:81, 173). Restore is reachable on every non-draft row (VersionHistory.tsx:287-292). MAJOR is inflated: nothing about the shipped configuration is wrong — same prompt, persona, voice, guardrails, flow and card ship as before — and the regulated record is not corrupted, because change_log.record_publish stores versionId and the per-component hashes alongside versionLabel (change_log.py:200, 212), so an auditor can still identify exactly which row went live. The damage is display text: a header lozenge showing a row id, a Publish button offering v1.0 after v1.6, and duplicate labels later in the timeline (masked by attemptSuffixes, VersionHistory.tsx:82-101). Contained and cosmetic-plus, i.e. MINOR.

title: Load draft / Restore / post-discard reload silently destroy up to a full autosave window of authored prompt text, with no confirmation
mechanism: Autosave is debounced 1200ms (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:681). `loadDraft` sets `skipAutosave.current = true` and then replaces prompt/persona/voice/guardrails/flow/card (:848-860). That state change re-runs the autosave effect, whose cleanup clears the pending timer (:683-685), and the effect body returns immediately on `skipAutosave.current` (:617) — so no timer is rescheduled. `markSaved` is then called with the newly loaded fingerprint (:867-876), so `unsaved` is false and nothing remains to trigger a save. The edits made in the last debounce window (plus any in-flight-network window) are gone with no record and no undo. The same path is reached from the drawer's "Load" (VersionHistory.tsx:214), from `restore` (:933) and from `discardDraft`'s live-reload branch (:899-921). The codebase already holds the opposite standard one function away: `applyPreset` (:829-845) refuses to overwrite authored text without an in-app confirmation dialog, for exactly this reason.
trigger: Type a sentence into the System Prompt tab, then within ~1.2s open History and click Load on another draft (or Restore on an archived version). The sentence is not in either version and was never sent to the server.
fix: Await the pending save before switching: if `unsaved` is true, either flush the autosave (call ensureDraft synchronously) before mutating state in `loadDraft`, or gate Load/Restore behind the same AlertDialog pattern `applyPreset` uses, naming what is about to be discarded.
verify_reason: Confirmed at the lines, with two off-by-one citations: the debounce is 1200ms at :682 (cited :681) and the cleanup that clears the pending timer is :684-686 (cited :683-685). The path is exactly as described — loadDraft sets skipAutosave.current = true (:848) and replaces prompt/persona/voice/guardrails/flow/card (:849-860); the resulting state change re-runs the effect, whose cleanup clears the pending timer (:684-686) and whose body returns at :617 before scheduling another; markSaved with the loaded fingerprint (:867-876) leaves unsaved false, and skipAutosave is cleared in a setTimeout(0) that changes no dependency, so nothing re-enters the effect. Reachable from Load (VersionHistory.tsx:280-286 -> lazy.tsx:1565-1568), Restore (:933) and the discard reload branch (:899-921). Two corrections to the write-up rather than the verdict: confidence is SUSPECTED, not VERIFIED — the History sheet is modal, so the operator cannot type while it is open, and the loss window is "open the drawer and click Load/Restore within 1200ms of the last keystroke", which I did not demonstrate; and the in-flight-network case is not loss (savingRef/resaveRef, :639-643 and :673-678, still write those edits). MINOR stands: silent, unrecoverable loss of up to one debounce window of authored prompt text, with applyPreset (:829-845) one function away as the codebase's own opposite standard.

title: Discarding the only draft leaves draftId pointing at the archived row, so Publish stays enabled and republishes the text just discarded
mechanism: `discardDraft` only clears editor state and `setDraftId(null)` inside `if (live)` (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:898-922). On a card whose only version was that draft, `live` is null (:894-897 excludes v.id) and the whole block is skipped: the editor keeps the discarded text and `draftId` still names the now-archived row. `canPublish={Boolean(draftId) || dirty}` (:1252) is therefore true and `publishDisabled` is false (StudioHeader.tsx:67), so Publish is live. Confirming it runs publishStudioDraft, whose PATCH 409s (`prompt_version_not_draft`, db_prompt_studio.py:1720), is classified as a fallback error (api/prompt-studio.ts:927) and falls through to `createPromptVersion` (:981) from the still-populated editor body — publishing the discarded content to production. The success toast at :924 has already told the operator the draft is gone.

title: Test in Sandbox and Publish create drafts outside the in-flight-save guard, so a click during the autosave window can fork a second draft
mechanism: `savingRef`/`resaveRef` exist precisely so that a second write cannot start while `ensureDraft` is creating a draft with `draftId` still null — the comment at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:305-311 spells out the duplicate-draft failure. Only the autosave body honours them (:638-643, :673-678). `onTestSandbox` calls `ensureDraftMutation.mutateAsync` directly (:1067) and `publish` calls `publishMutation.mutateAsync` (:947) → `publishStudioDraft` → `createPromptVersion` (api/prompt-studio.ts:980-983); neither checks `savingRef.current` nor cancels the pending `autosaveTimer`. If the button's request is slower than the remainder of the 1200ms debounce, the timer fires with `draftId` still null and creates a second draft for the same edit. The result is two open drafts: the version drawer grows a phantom row, and `POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/publish` starts 409-ing `ambiguous_draft_to_publish` (main.py:2231-2239) for that bot.
trigger: On a card with no open draft, type, then click "Test in Sandbox" (or Publish) within the debounce window on a slow connection. Two drafts appear in History for one edit.
fix: Have both handlers take the same guard: clear `autosaveTimer.current`, set `savingRef.current = true` for the duration of the mutation, and honour `resaveRef` on completion — or factor the create-or-patch into one `flushDraft()` all three callers share.
verify_reason: Confirmed as SUSPECTED/MINOR. The guard is real and applies only to the autosave body (savingRef/resaveRef at :639-643 and :673-678, purpose spelled out at :305-311); onTestSandbox calls ensureDraftMutation.mutateAsync directly at :1067 and publish calls publishMutation.mutateAsync at :947, and neither reads savingRef nor clears autosaveTimer, so a debounce firing at :682 while the button's create is still in flight sees draftId null and creates a second draft. I checked for a server-side dedupe and there is none: ensureStudioDraft falls through to createPromptVersion when draftId is null (prompt-studio.ts:1017-1025), and create_prompt_version resolves an id collision by appending a uuid suffix rather than reusing the row (db_prompt_studio.py:1629-1631), so two open drafts with the same label are a legitimate outcome. One correction: the ambiguous_draft_to_publish consequence is API-only — main.py:2233-2241 belongs to POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/publish, which no frontend client calls (the Studio publishes by version id, prompt-studio.ts:679), so the operator-visible damage is the phantom draft row in History, not a broken Publish button. Line correction: that raise is 2233-2241, not 2231-2239.

title: Version history is a single unpaginated 200-row page — the History count, the Live group and the by-bot publish endpoint all truncate silently
mechanism: `fetchPromptVersions` sends no `limit` (api/prompt-studio.ts:167-168), so `clamp_list_limit(None)` resolves to `DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT = 200` (db_core.py:211,221-222) and the query is `ORDER BY created_at DESC ... LIMIT 200` (db_prompt_studio.py:243). Nothing in the client pages past that: `history` is the whole model behind `versionCount={history.length}` (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1265), the drawer's per-group counts (VersionHistory.tsx:244), `publishedRow` (:429-432) and `nextLabel` (:541). Once a card accumulates 200 versions newer than its published row, `publishedRow` is undefined, the header claims "never published" for a live card (StudioHeader.tsx:78-79), `nextLabel` resets to v1.0, and the drawer shows no Live group. Below that threshold the count itself is still a quiet lie once 200 is exceeded overall. The by-bot publish endpoint inherits the same window: `db.list_prompt_versions(bot_id=bot_id)` with no limit (main.py:2214) means a caller naming an older draft's `versionId` gets 404 `prompt_version_not_found` for a draft that exists (main.py:2222-2229).
trigger: A card with more than 200 prompt_versions rows: the History button's count stops growing and the older half of the timeline is unreachable. With 200 rows created since the last publish, the header reports a live card as never published.
fix: Either page the drawer (pass `limit`/`offset` and add a "load older" control) or, at minimum, fetch the live row independently — `GET /prompt-versions/published?botId=` (main.py:2031) already exists and is not window-dependent — and drive `publishedRow`/`nextLabel`/the header lozenge from it. Add `limit=db.MAX_LIST_LIMIT` at main.py:2214 so the by-bot publish enumerates every draft.
verify_reason: Confirmed as SUSPECTED/MINOR. fetchPromptVersions sends only botId and no limit (prompt-studio.ts:167-168); the route's limit defaults to None (main.py:2021-2022); clamp_list_limit(None) resolves to DEFAULT_LIST_LIMIT = 200 (db_core.py:211, 221-222) and the query is ORDER BY p.created_at DESC, p.id DESC LIMIT :limit OFFSET :offset (db_prompt_studio.py:243-244) with no caller paging. history is the raw page (setHistory(versionsQuery.data), lazy.tsx:386), so versionCount={history.length} (:1265), publishedRow (:429-431) and nextLabel (:541) all read a truncated window, and with 200 rows newer than the published one the header would say "never published" for a live card. The by-bot publish endpoint inherits the same window at main.py:2217 (cited as 2214-2215) and 404s at :2225-2228 (cited as 2222-2229). Not demonstrated is the accumulation itself — autosave patches an existing draft rather than creating one, so 200 rows per bot takes a long life — which is why SUSPECTED is the right confidence and MINOR the right severity.

title: The response_model guard stops at the literal prefix /agent-studio, leaving 41 studio routes with no declared wire shape
mechanism: `_studio_routes()` filters `route.path.startswith("/agent-studio")` (test_agent_studio_response_models.py:53) and then asserts `len(routes) == 26` and `route.response_model is not None` (:59, :64). Every other endpoint the Studio's fifteen tabs call sits under a different prefix — /connectors, /vault, /mcp, /a2a, /eval, /gateway, /roles, /bot-deployments/experiments, /sandbox/tuning, /voice/sandbox, /providers/bindings, /outbound/card-vocabulary — and none of them declares a response_model. The docstring at test_agent_studio_response_models.py:1-6 states exactly why this matters — FastAPI silently filters undeclared fields — and the guard's own coverage assertion (a hardcoded 26) is what conceals the gap: adding a route under any other prefix does not move the number.
trigger: Add or rename a key in `agent_core/canary.list_experiments`'s row, or in `list_eval_suites`, and the Ship or Evals tab renders `undefined` with a green suite; nothing in the backend suite fails, and `tsc` still compiles because the TS type was hand-written to match the old shape.

TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:272 already names this as the intended mechanism ("the same table shape, added after 178 → 0").
verify_reason: Mechanism half-true, severity and one file wrong. Verified: test_agent_studio_response_models.py:53 filters `route.path.startswith("/agent-studio")`, :59 asserts `len(routes) == 26`, :64 asserts response_model is not None; and main.py:2527 /connectors, :2573 /vault/refs, :2599 /mcp/keys, :2740 /a2a/partners, :2781 /eval/suites/{id}/run, :2890 /gateway/canary, :2928 /roles, :3205 /bot-deployments/experiments, :3468 /sandbox/tuning/presets, :3482 /voice/sandbox/start, :5233 /outbound/card-vocabulary all declare no response_model. But (a) /providers/bindings is NOT one of them — main.py:5463 `response_model=list[ProviderBindingItem]`, :5488 `ProviderBindingItem`, :5525, :5534, and :5407 `list[ProviderModelItem]` — so the claim that api/providers.ts:210 is 'hand-written against nothing' is false; (b) the harm named in the guard's own docstring (test_agent_studio_response_models.py:1-6, FastAPI filters undeclared fields) is caused by declaring a too-narrow model, not by declaring none: an undeclared route serializes the mapper dict verbatim, so there is no silent field drop today; (c) the '41 studio routes' count is asserted, not derived — main.py has 317 @app decorators and no enumeration is offered. The G6 sub-claim also fails: compile.py:683 emits G6 `skipped` only when `card is None`, and AgentCardPanels.tsx:132 renders that lozenge only under `isAuthoredCard(card)`, so the green-for-unknown branch at :133 is unreachable for G6.
