title: Compile never passes channel_tools, so G4/G6 and the report's effective_tools ignore the channel filter the runtime applies
mechanism: compile_card accepts channel_tools (compile.py:526) and forwards it into effective_tools/idle_offered_tools (:627-639), but neither the dry-run (db_prompt_studio.py:837-857) nor publish (:1908-1926) supplies it, so the preview's idle count and effective_tools are computed channel-agnostically while voice/bot.py:1141-1143 filters to CATALOG.for_channel(voice). A TEXT_ONLY tool on include (identify_customer, ingest_customer_document) counts toward the voice cap in G6 and appears in effective_tools though the voice runtime drops it. The UI cannot add these (tool_catalog is voice-filtered), so the trigger needs a hand-edited or imported card.
trigger: Publish a card whose include JSON contains identify_customer: G6 counts it as an idle voice tool; the voice grant does not contain it.
fix: Pass `channel_tools={s.name for s in CATALOG.for_channel('voice')}` (or compute per card channel) from both compile call sites, or report per-channel effective lists in CompileReport.
verify_reason: Verified at both call sites: db_prompt_studio.py:838-857 (dry-run) and :1908-1925 (publish) each pass catalog_names=set(CATALOG.specs) and omit channel_tools entirely, though compile_card declares it (compile.py:526) and forwards it to effective_tools (:627-633) and idle_offered_tools (:634-639). intersect._apply_channel (intersect.py:79-82) returns names unchanged when channel_tools is None, so preview and publish compute a channel-agnostic set while voice/bot.py:1141-1143 builds the live grant with channel_tools={spec.name for spec in CATALOG.for_channel(CHANNEL_VOICE)}. identify_customer (catalog.py:214-231) and ingest_customer_document (catalog.py:684-709) are TEXT_ONLY, so either on include would be counted by G6 (compile.py:687) and listed in report.effective_tools while the voice grant drops it. The auditor is right that the UI cannot create the state (flow_graph.py:817-821 filters /flow/tools to voice) — it needs a PATCH of the draft's agentCard, which ensureStudioDraft/patchPromptVersion accepts verbatim. Contained and latent: MINOR.

title: Missing non-mouth locked engines fail G3 but no tab can show or repair them
mechanism: G3 fails with missing_locked when recommend_treatment or evaluate_live_qa is absent from card.tools.locked (compile.py:603-613). The Tools tab has no rows for them (not in CATALOG, flow_graph.py:817-821) and its toggle only writes include (:103-112); the Policy tab reads policy_bindings, not tools.locked (:203,226-235). So the only surface for tools.locked content is the raw JSON, and the failure reads 'engines cannot be unbound' with no pointer to which screen fixes it.
trigger: Import or PATCH a card whose tools.locked is ['recommend_next_offer','evaluate_authority']; every tab is green until Publish reports G3 missing_locked.
fix: Have PolicyTab also render each LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES entry's presence in card.tools.locked (red when missing) and offer a one-click 'restore locked engines' that writes the full LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES list.
verify_reason: compile.py:600-615: locked_set = set(card.tools.locked); missing_locked = [n for n in LOCKED_POLICY_ENGINES if n not in locked_set]; the gate fails with detail 'engines cannot be unbound' and the two names only inside issues[0]['missing_locked'] — and CompileReportList (AgentCardPanels.tsx:1019-1040) renders g.gate, g.name and g.detail and never g.issues, so the operator sees the sentence without the names. No tab can show or repair the state: recommend_treatment and evaluate_live_qa have no ToolSpec so flow_graph.py:817-821 gives them no row, ToolsTab.toggle writes only include (:103-112), and PolicyTab (:202-241) reads card.policy_bindings, never card.tools.locked — a card with all six bindings 'required' and a truncated tools.locked paints six green lozenges. Only reachable by a card not authored through the UI (CardTools.locked defaults to the full four at schema.py:114), which is why it is a diagnosability gap rather than a live defect. MINOR as rated.

title: Skill lint warnings reach the wire and die at the TypeScript boundary — the author is still told nothing
mechanism: `upsert_skill_from_pack` attaches non-blocking lint findings to the saved row (`saved["lintWarnings"] = warnings`, persist.py:317). `AgentStudioSkillResponse` declares `lintWarnings: list[dict[str, Any]] | None` (schemas.py:3655) and POST/PATCH/import /agent-studio/skills all serve that model with `response_model_exclude_unset=True`, so the warnings genuinely go out on the wire. The TypeScript `SkillSummary` (agent-studio.ts:463-483) — the return type of `useCreateSkill` (agent-studio.ts:690), `usePatchSkill`, `importSkillZip` and `useAgentStudioSkill` — declares no `lintWarnings` member, and grepping Habibi/src for `lintWarnings` returns nothing. So the field is dropped at the type boundary and no component renders it. The lint module's own test file opens with "The skill linter was dead code" and asserts `description_too_long` is reported "or the author was told nothing" (test_skill_lint_wiring.py:96) — that assertion passes at the Python API and is false at the screen.
trigger: Create or edit a skill whose description exceeds CATALOG_PREFIX_TOKEN_CAP (e.g. via the Skills tab or a .md import). The save succeeds, the server logs a warning (persist.py:316), the response carries `lintWarnings: [{code: "description_too_long", ...}]`, and the studio shows a plain success. The author discovers it later as a G6 / skill_description_tokens failure on the card that attaches the skill — the exact late rejection the linter was wired up to prevent.
fix: Add `lintWarnings?: Array<{ code: string; message?: string; [k: string]: unknown }>` to `SkillSummary` in Habibi/src/api/agent-studio.ts, and surface it after a save in the skill editor (agent-studio.skills.$skillId.tsx) as a non-blocking warning banner. Give `usePatchSkill` / `useSignSkill` / `useRevertSkill` a real return type instead of the untyped `apiPatch`/`apiPost` they use today, so the field is reachable from every write.
verify_reason: Mechanism is real and I reproduced every link: assert_pack_lints returns non-blocking findings (agent_core/skills/lint.py:63-70, BLOCKING_LINT_CODES=lint.py:40 is only unknown_tools/malformed_tool_name); upsert_skill_from_pack attaches them to the returned row (persist.py:315-317); AgentStudioSkillResponse.lintWarnings is declared (schemas.py:3655) and POST (main.py:2322-2331), PATCH (main.py:2333-2342), GET detail (main.py:2308-2319) all serve that model with response_model_exclude_unset=True, so the key really is on the wire; TS SkillSummary (agent-studio.ts:463-483) omits it and `grep lintWarnings Habibi/src` returns zero hits; the import handler shows an unconditional toast.success("Imported as unsigned draft") (agent-studio.skills.index.tsx:142-144). But MAJOR does not survive. Nothing runs wrong, nothing is lost, and no publish verdict is wrong: the write is correct and the toast ("saved"/"imported") is true, not a lie. The one warning class at issue (description_too_long) is caught blockingly and legibly later by G6 — compile.py:693-694 appends {"skill_description_tokens": n, "cap": 800} and compile.py:696-704 fails the gate with the detail "skill prefix n/800 tokens" — so the operator IS told, at the publish button, by a gate that fails closed. What is lost is earliness, not correctness. That is incorrect-but-contained: MINOR.

title: The Agent Card drift test guards 14 top-level names and leaves ~80 nested fields — including all of CardOutbound — unasserted
mechanism: `test_top_level_members_match` compares `set(AgentCard.model_fields)` against the `AGENT_CARD_MEMBERS` literal, and `test_the_declared_type_covers_every_member` compares that literal against the `type AgentCard` block. Both operate only on the 14 top-level names. Nothing walks into `CardIdentity`, `CardTools`, `CardHandoff`, `CardConnector`, `CardSkillRef`, `CardMemory`, `Compaction`, `HumanGate`, `CardEval`, `CardExperiment`, `CardA2A`, `CardOutbound`, `CardObjective`, `CardCadence`, `VoicemailPolicy`, `CardPostCall` or `PostCallRule` — ~80 fields across 17 models, every one of them under `extra="forbid"`. The file's own docstring claims the broader guarantee ("The TypeScript Agent Card and the Pydantic one must describe the same card") and the type's docstring says "`test_agent_card_schema_drift.py` fails if the two lists of top-level members stop matching" — which is the honest reading, but the file heading is not. I verified by hand that the nested mirror is correct *today*; the exposure is that it is correct by luck rather than by check, and CardOutbound's 10 fields plus CardObjective's 9 and CardCadence's 8 are the newest and least-walked.
trigger: Add a field to any nested card model (or rename one) and both tests still pass. The corresponding editor panel silently cannot write it — or, in the invented-field direction, writes a key that `parse_card` rejects at G0 with a message naming a field the author picked from a control the app drew.
fix: Extend test_agent_card_schema_drift.py with a recursive comparison: walk `AgentCard.model_fields` into every nested BaseModel and compare each model's field set against the members declared in the corresponding `export type X = {…}` block in agent-card.ts (the file already names each type identically to its Pydantic class, so the mapping is mechanical). Assert both directions, with the same two error messages the top-level test already writes.
verify_reason: Verified at the cited lines. test_top_level_members_match (test_agent_card_schema_drift.py:55-68) compares set(AgentCard.model_fields) to AGENT_CARD_MEMBERS; test_the_declared_type_covers_every_member (:70-85) compares that constant to the `type AgentCard` block via a regex that only captures top-level `^\s*(\w+)\??:` inside `export type AgentCard = {…};`. Both walk 14 names only. Nothing in the file mentions CardIdentity, CardTools, CardHandoff, CardConnector, CardSkillRef, CardMemory, Compaction, HumanGate, CardEval, CardExperiment, CardA2A, CardOutbound, CardObjective, CardCadence, VoicemailPolicy, CardPostCall or PostCallRule; every one of those sets extra="forbid" (schema.py:79-419). I also independently re-checked the nested mirror field-by-field against agent-card.ts:126-300 and it is correct today — CardOutbound's 10, CardObjective's 9 and CardCadence's 8 all match — so this is exactly what the author claimed: correct by luck, not by check. The file's own heading ("The TypeScript Agent Card and the Pydantic one must describe the same card", :1) overstates what the tests do. MINOR is right: it is a missing guard, not a live defect.

title: agent-studio.ts mirrors 14 Pydantic response models with no drift guard of any kind
mechanism: `test_agent_studio_response_models.py` proves the HTTP body equals the *mapper* output key-for-key (`_assert_same_shape`, lines 28-46) — a backend-to-backend check. Nothing compares either side to `agent-studio.ts`. `nullability.test.ts` reads three files (`api/types/customer360.ts`, `api/types/audit.ts`, `api/customers.ts`) and asserts string literals in them; it names nothing in the studio. So `AgentCardSummary`, `CompileReport`, `CompileGate`, `AgentGraph`, `ChangeLogEntry`, `ChainVerdict`, `SkillSummary`, `CloneTemplate`, `EvalSuite`, `EvalReport`, `DeploymentExperiment`, `SkillCritique`, `QaDisagreement` and `RolesCatalog` are hand mirrors with a zero-test blast radius. The four concrete drifts I found (TYPES-04, -05, -06, -07) are all in this file, which is what an unguarded surface looks like after a few months.
trigger: Any change to a model in schemas.py:3470-3690 or to CompileReport in compile.py. Backend tests stay green; the studio silently stops reading the new field, or keeps reading a removed one as `undefined`.
fix: Add a source-reading drift test alongside test_agent_card_schema_drift.py, keyed on the docstring each Pydantic model already carries ("Mirrors Habibi AgentCardSummary", schemas.py:3477; "Mirrors Habibi PromptVersion", schemas.py:2206; "Mirrors Habibi TtsVoice", schemas.py:2253): parse the named `export type X = {…}` block out of the TS file and compare member sets against `model_fields`. The docstrings already declare the pairing — nothing reads them.
verify_reason: Verified. test_agent_studio_response_models.py:1-6 states the check is HTTP-body-vs-mapper-output; _assert_same_shape (:28-46) compares two Python values and never opens a .ts file. nullability.test.ts:11-63 reads only api/types/customer360.ts, api/types/audit.ts and api/customers.ts. I also checked the two other candidate guards in backend/tests: test_schema_parity.py is sql/*.sql vs the migrated database (:1-22), and test_sandbox_turn_schema.py reads sandbox.ts but only for the REQUEST body (:198-213, `test_every_key_the_studio_posts_is_a_field_on_the_request_model`) — no response-side TS assertion anywhere. So the studio's ~14 hand-written response mirrors in agent-studio.ts have a zero-test blast radius, and TYPES-04/06/07/10 are four independently-confirmed drifts inside that surface, which is the evidence the claim needs. MINOR (structural coverage gap, no live wrong behaviour).

title: ChangeLogEntry omits `hashes` and `previousVersionId` — the per-component hashes that make the audit entry checkable never reach the screen
mechanism: `record_publish` writes `previousVersionId` and `hashes` (the per-component SHA of prompt/persona/voice/guardrails/flow/agent_card, from `component_hashes(version)`) into the audit payload; `read_entries` spreads the whole payload onto the entry (change_log.py:343); `AgentStudioChangeLogEntryResponse` declares both (schemas.py:3542, 3549). The TypeScript `ChangeLogEntry` declares neither. `ChangeLogTab` renders `entry.entryHash` — the chain link — and has no access to the component hashes, which are the half that lets a reader tie an entry to a specific version's contents rather than only to its neighbours in the chain.
trigger: Publish any version, then open the Change log tab. `changed` shows which components moved; the hashes that would let an auditor verify *what* they moved to are on the wire and unreachable from the type. Same for `previousVersionId`: the tab shows `previousVersionLabel` (a human label, not stable) with no id to link to.
fix: Add `previousVersionId?: string | null` and `hashes?: Record<string, string>` to ChangeLogEntry (agent-studio.ts:892-916). Render the component hashes in the expanded entry beside `changed`, and use `previousVersionId` to make the "previous version" label a link.
verify_reason: Every link holds. record_publish builds the payload with "previousVersionId" (change_log.py:202) and "hashes": after (change_log.py:212) where after = component_hashes(version) (change_log.py:197); read_entries spreads the whole payload onto the entry (change_log.py:343); AgentStudioChangeLogEntryResponse declares previousVersionId and hashes: dict[str,str]|None. TS ChangeLogEntry declares neither, and ChangeLogTab renders only entry.entryHash (ChangeLogTab.tsx:166-169) — `grep hashes|previousVersionId ChangeLogTab.tsx` matches nothing but a prose line at :103. Trigger is real and needs no special state: publish anything, open the Change log tab. Note this contradicts the prior audit's own checked_fine line ("templates/cards/change-log response shapes match their TS types field-for-field", AGENT_STUDIO_BUG_HUNT.md:39), so it is new information, not a restatement. Line numbers for the two schema fields are wrong by ten — corrected below. MINOR stands: the audit chain link (entryHash) IS rendered, so tamper-evidence is not lost; what is lost is tying an entry to a version's contents.

title: AgentGraph.edges[].to is typed non-nullable while the endpoint emits `h.get("to_bot_id")` and the response model allows null
mechanism: The graph endpoint reads handoffs straight off the stored draft JSON without parsing the card (`raw.get("handoffs")`, main.py:2266) and builds `{"from": bot_id, "to": h.get("to_bot_id")}` — `None` for any handoff row missing the key. `AgentStudioGraphEdgeResponse.to` is correspondingly `str | None = None` (schemas.py:3584). The TypeScript `AgentGraph` declares `edges: { from: string; to: string }[]` (agent-studio.ts:317). The null is reachable because drafts are persisted unvalidated — `patch_prompt_version` casts `agentCard` to jsonb with no `parse_card` (db_prompt_studio.py:1775-1779) — and `CardHandoff.to_bot_id` is optional on the TS side too (agent-card.ts:148). AgentGraphTab already defends against the value its own type says cannot exist (`.filter((e) => e.to)`, AgentCardPanels.tsx:610), which is the tell.
trigger: A draft whose `handoffs` array contains a row without `to_bot_id` (hand-edited JSON, a partially-applied migration, or any future editor that stages an empty row). Today's only consumer filters it out; a new consumer trusting `to: string` gets `null` where the type promised a bot id.
fix: Type it as the server declares it: `edges: { from: string; to: string | null }[]` in agent-studio.ts:317. Optionally tighten the backend instead by dropping edges with a falsy target at main.py:2282 and making `to: str` required — but pick one, do not leave the two disagreeing.
verify_reason: Confirmed at the code, with lines corrected. get_agent_studio_graph reads the stored draft JSON without parse_card (main.py:2266-2267 `raw.get("handoffs")`) and emits {"from": bot_id, "to": h.get("to_bot_id")} (main.py:2281-2285) — h.get returns None for a row missing the key. AgentStudioGraphEdgeResponse.to is `str | None = None` (schemas.py:3593), so the model passes the null through rather than 500ing. TS AgentGraph declares `edges: { from: string; to: string }[]` (agent-studio.ts:318). The null is reachable through the real API, not only by hand-editing the DB: patch_prompt_version casts agentCard straight to jsonb with no parse_card and no validation (db_prompt_studio.py:1774-1778), so PATCH /prompt-versions/{id} with {"agentCard":{"handoffs":[{"when":"x"}]}} persists it and the next GET .../graph returns to:null. Pydantic CardHandoff.to_bot_id is required (schema.py:118-124) but that model is never on this path. The tell the author names is real: AgentCardPanels.tsx:614 already filters `.filter((e) => e.to)` against a value its own type says cannot exist. MINOR — today's only consumer defends itself.

title: SkillSummary collapses the backend's summary/detail split and drops three declared fields
mechanism: The backend has two models: `AgentStudioSkillSummaryResponse` (16 required fields, served by GET /agent-studio/skills) and `AgentStudioSkillResponse` which subclasses it and adds six optional detail fields. TypeScript has one `SkillSummary` typed for both endpoints, which (a) loses the distinction — a list row is typed as if it might carry `body`, `markdown`, `frontmatter`, `versions`; (b) omits `contentHash` (schemas.py:3634, required), `evalSuite` (schemas.py:3633, required) and `lintWarnings` (see TYPES-01); (c) declares `latestVersionId?: string` where the wire is `str | None`, so `null` is assignable to nothing and a strict `!`-assertion would lie; (d) types `versions?: Array<{ id; version; status }>` — three of the fourteen fields on `AgentStudioSkillVersionResponse` (schemas.py:3596-3614), so `signedBy`, `signature`, `contentHash` and `allowedTools` per version are unreachable even though the detail route serves them and the version list at agent-studio.skills.$skillId.tsx:344-360 is exactly where they would be shown.
trigger: Read-only: the studio simply cannot display a skill's content hash, its bound eval suite, or per-version signature provenance. `latestVersionId` null-vs-undefined bites only if someone writes a non-null assertion.
fix: Split into `SkillSummary` and `SkillDetail extends SkillSummary` mirroring the two Pydantic models; add `contentHash: string`, `evalSuite: unknown | null`, `lintWarnings?`, widen `latestVersionId` to `string | null`, and type `versions` against the full `AgentStudioSkillVersionResponse`.
verify_reason: All four sub-claims verified against the models. AgentStudioSkillSummaryResponse (schemas.py:3624-3644) has 16 required fields including contentHash (:3640), evalSuite (:3639) and latestVersionId: str | None (:3633); AgentStudioSkillResponse subclasses it and adds six optional detail fields (schemas.py:3647-3655). The single TS SkillSummary (agent-studio.ts:463-483) is used as the return type of the list query (:645), the detail query (:655), create (:677) and importSkillZip (:753) — so a list row is indeed typed as if it might carry body/markdown/frontmatter/versions. It omits contentHash, evalSuite and lintWarnings, types latestVersionId as `?: string` where the wire is `str | None`, and types versions as three of the fourteen fields on AgentStudioSkillVersionResponse (schemas.py:3605-3621) — so signedBy, signature, contentHash and allowedTools are unreachable exactly where the version list is drawn (agent-studio.skills.$skillId.tsx:342-360, which already renders v.version/v.status/v.id). One extra drift the author missed, in the same file: bodyTokens and referenceFiles are optional in TS (agent-studio.ts:481-482) and required on the summary model (schemas.py:3643-3644). MINOR: read-only display gap, no wrong behaviour.

title: BotDeployment omits trafficPct, shadow and evalReportId — the three fields that say what a deployment is actually taking
mechanism: `BotDeploymentResponse` carries `trafficPct: int = 100`, `shadow: bool = False` and `evalReportId: str | None` (schemas.py:2338-2340) — the record of what split and what eval evidence a deployment shipped under. The TypeScript `BotDeployment` (prompt-studio.ts:33-46) declares 12 of the 15 fields and none of those three. The Ship tab gets its split from a different source, `DeploymentExperiment` on GET /bot-deployments/experiments (agent-studio.ts:449-459, consumed at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:458-466), so a deployment row rendered from `useBotDeployments` can never say what traffic it holds.
trigger: Any deployments list rendered from the `BotDeployment` type shows the deployment without its split; a canary at 40% is indistinguishable from a full ship, and `evalReportId` — the link from a live deployment to the eval that let it through G7/G8 — is unreachable.
fix: Add `trafficPct: number; shadow: boolean; evalReportId: string | null;` to `BotDeployment` in prompt-studio.ts:33-46, and render the split on the deployment row so the experiment query stops being the only place it exists.
verify_reason: Verified, with the schema lines corrected and one naming error. BotDeploymentResponse spans schemas.py:2339-2358 and carries trafficPct: int = 100 (:2356), shadow: bool = False (:2357) and evalReportId: str | None = None (:2358) — the cited 2320-2341/2338-2340 point at TtsSyncRunResponse instead. TS BotDeployment (prompt-studio.ts:33-46) declares 12 fields and none of those three. There is no `useBotDeployments` hook — the list fetcher is fetchBotDeployments (prompt-studio.ts:452, :477); the type is also the return of rollbackBotDeployment (:708) and fetchActiveBotDeployment (:884-895) and is consumed by VersionHistory (VersionHistory.tsx:20-21). The traffic split is separately reachable via DeploymentExperiment (agent-studio.ts:451-459) consumed at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:459-467, which softens the split half of the claim — but evalReportId is not: it is selected (db_prompt_studio.py:1448, :1592) and mapped (db_prompt_studio.py:1577) and `grep -rn evalReportId Habibi/src` returns zero hits, so the link from a live deployment to the eval that cleared G7/G8 is genuinely unreachable from the studio. MINOR stands.

title: Sandbox read types drop five served fields, including the tool-loop trace
mechanism: `SandboxBotTurn.toolCalls: list[dict[str, Any]]` (schemas.py:2624, commented "Tool-loop trace from sandbox_runtime") is on the POST /sandbox/runs/{id}/turns response and absent from the TypeScript `SandboxTurnResult.botTurn` (sandbox.ts:67-82); no frontend consumer exists (the `toolCalls` matches in Habibi/src are trace.ts:60 and the live-voice event stream, which are different payloads). Separately, `SandboxRunTurnResponse` declares `sentimentLabel`, `retrievedChunkIds`, `tokenCount` and `createdAt` (schemas.py:2487-2494) that `SandboxRunDetail.turns` (sandbox.ts:98-115) does not name — so a replayed run shows a raw sentiment float with no label while a live turn shows the label from `customerTurn.sentimentLabel`.

verify_reason: Both halves verified; two schema line numbers were wrong. SandboxBotTurn.toolCalls: list[dict[str, Any]] sits at schemas.py:2634 under the comment "Tool-loop trace from sandbox_runtime" at :2633 (the cited 2624 is `tokens`), is populated by the runtime (sandbox_runtime.py:1106 "toolCalls": tool_trace, from sandbox_runtime.py:252) and is absent from the TS botTurn object literal (sandbox.ts:67-82). I checked every `toolCalls` hit in Habibi/src: trace.ts:60 (a different endpoint's TraceToolCall, rendered by TurnTraceView.tsx:106 and InspectorPanel.tsx:63,114) and the live-voice event reducer (liveEvents.ts:174, useSandboxLiveCall.ts:366-443) — neither reads this response. So the text-sandbox tool trace has no consumer. Second half also holds: SandboxRunTurnResponse declares sentimentLabel (schemas.py:2487), retrievedChunkIds (:2489), tokenCount (:2494) and createdAt (:2496), and SandboxRunDetail.turns (sandbox.ts:98-115) names none of the four, so a replayed run has a raw sentiment float where a live turn has customerTurn.sentimentLabel. Nothing else guards it — test_sandbox_turn_schema.py only asserts the REQUEST body (:198-213). MINOR.

title: Every /eval/* route serves an untyped dict, so the Evals tab's TypeScript types mirror nothing and the response-shape test cannot see them
mechanism: GET /eval/suites, /eval/reports, /eval/reports/{id}, /eval/critiques, /eval/disagreements and /eval/twin-corpus declare no `response_model`. `list_eval_suites` returns `[dict(r) for r in rows]` over `SELECT id, kind, name, description, created_at` (db_inbox.py:1728-1737) — raw snake_case `created_at` reaches the wire, and TS `EvalSuite` (agent-studio.ts:353) names four of the five. `test_every_agent_studio_route_declares_a_response_shape` filters on `route.path.startswith("/agent-studio")` (test_agent_studio_response_models.py:53), so it asserts nothing about /eval/*, and by the same filter nothing about /flow/*, /sandbox/*, /prompt-versions, /connectors*, /mcp/*, /a2a*, /bot-deployments* or /outbound/*. That is most of the Studio's wire.
trigger: Any change to the eval_suites or eval_reports SELECT list silently changes the wire. There is no model to fail, no mapper comparison to fail, and no TS drift test — three layers of guard that all stop at the /agent-studio prefix.
fix: Declare response models for the /eval/* routes the studio reads (suites, reports, critiques, disagreements) mirroring the existing AgentStudio* naming, and widen the route filter in test_agent_studio_response_models.py:47-64 from `/agent-studio` to the set of studio prefixes the audit enumerates.
verify_reason: Read every cited route: GET /eval/suites (main.py:2796-2798), /eval/reports (:2801-2810), /eval/reports/{id} (:2812-2822, which returns `dict(row)` over `SELECT *`), /eval/critiques (:2847-2851), /eval/disagreements (:2864-2868) and /eval/twin-corpus (:2871-2875) all declare no response_model. list_eval_suites selects `id, kind, name, description, created_at` and returns `[dict(r) for r in rows]` (db_inbox.py:1726-1739), so raw snake_case created_at reaches the wire while TS EvalSuite (agent-studio.ts:342) names four of the five. The test filter is verbatim `route.path.startswith("/agent-studio")` (test_agent_studio_response_models.py:53), and test_every_agent_studio_route_declares_a_response_shape (:57-64) therefore asserts nothing about /eval/*, /flow/*, /sandbox/*, /prompt-versions, /connectors*, /mcp/*, /a2a* or /bot-deployments*. Fair mitigation the author did not note: list_eval_reports does hand-map to camelCase (db_inbox.py:1700-1714), so EvalReport is accurate today — the exposure is that nothing holds it there. MINOR.

title: Retired provider_models rows are never disabled by the seed upsert, so the panel can bind a Fish/OpenRouter voice to a stale model row that reports runtime 'live'
mechanism: sync_seed upserts ON CONFLICT (provider_id, kind, model_id) (persist.py:69) and never disables rows absent from SEED. When the OpenRouter model id moved from the expired free promotion to 'fish-audio/s2.1-pro' (registry.py:440-461 names the old id), the old row stays enabled and list_models returns both. For that row find_model returns None, so runtime defaults to (RUNTIME_LIVE, '') and sampling False (main.py:5440-5442, 5471) — an audition-only provider reported as live. VoicePanel picks the first row per provider (240-242), so which of the two wins depends on display_name ordering.
trigger: Any deployment whose provider_models table predates commit 5c143eb: open a voice from that provider and compare RuntimeNotice / 'New take' against the registry.
fix: In sync_seed, `UPDATE provider_models SET enabled=false WHERE id NOT IN (seed ids)`; in list_provider_models, report RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE ('not in registry') when find_model is None.
verify_reason: The code half is certain: sync_seed upserts ON CONFLICT (provider_id, kind, model_id) and never disables or deletes a row absent from SEED (persist.py:57-88 — nothing in the module or the two provider migrations issues a DELETE/UPDATE enabled=false on provider_models), list_models returns every enabled row (persist.py:97-118), and list_provider_models reports `runtime_status(spec) if spec is not None else (RUNTIME_LIVE, "")` (main.py:5441-5442) with sampling False (main.py:5471) when find_model misses. The stale row is not hypothetical: commit 5c143eb (2026-09-04) changed the OpenRouter ModelSpec's model_id from 'fish-audio/s2.1-pro-free:free' to 'fish-audio/s2.1-pro' while leaving display_name 'Fish Audio S2.1 Pro' unchanged, so a DB seeded before it keeps both rows, both enabled, with an identical display_name — and list_models' ORDER BY kind, provider name, display_name therefore ties, making which one VoicePanel.tsx:240-242 picks arbitrary. If it picks the stale one the panel reports runtime 'live' and hides RuntimeNotice for a model the registry declares live_capable=False (registry.py:454), i.e. audition-only sold as callable, and hides 'New take' for a sampling engine. Confidence SUSPECTED is right and I could not confirm the row exists in any live DB (read-only, no psql), but that is a deployment question, not a code one.

title: 'Speaking style' selector is dead config: preview ignores it and runtime derives style from warmth
mechanism: The Select at VoicePanel.tsx:688-702 writes voice.style and schedules a live preview; previewTts sends `style` (prompt-studio.ts:1118) and TtsPreviewRequest accepts it (schemas.py:2660), but tts_preview never reads payload.style — azure_speech.synthesize has no style parameter (azure_speech.py:460-469) and picks express-as from warmth (189-220). At save/publish apply_voice_config_overlay is called without style (db_prompt_studio.py:1740-1748, 2012-2018; signature tuning.py:359-366) and sets tts.style from warmth (397-406). The stored value only reaches deployments.voice_config (1992-2000), which the runtime reads solely for azureVoiceName (deployment.py:78-80). selectVoice also silently writes styles[0] on every selection (VoicePanel.tsx:388), and the 'style not offered' banner (555-562) advises picking a replacement that changes nothing.
trigger: Pick an Azure voice with styles, change 'Speaking style', press Preview — the audio is identical; publish — the call uses friendly/empathetic from warmth regardless.
fix: Either pass voice.style through TtsPreviewRequest into azure_speech.synthesize and into apply_voice_config_overlay (tts.style/style_degree, overriding the warmth mapping when set), or remove the selector and the styles[0] write.
verify_reason: Verified end to end. The Select at VoicePanel.tsx:688-702 writes voice.style through onSlider; previewTts puts it on the wire (prompt-studio.ts:1118) and TtsPreviewRequest declares it (schemas.py:2663), but tts_preview reads only speed/pitch/warmth/pauseMs (main.py:3163-3171) and azure_speech.synthesize has no style parameter at all (azure_speech.py:460-468) — express-as is derived from warmth in _warmth_express_as (189-220). On save and publish, apply_voice_config_overlay is called without style (db_prompt_studio.py:1740-1748 and 2012-2018) and its signature has no such parameter (tuning.py:359-366); it sets tts.style/style_degree from warmth alone (397-409). The stored value only reaches deployments.voice_config (db_prompt_studio.py:1992-2000), and bot.py:579-589 uses only vparams['voiceName'] out of voice_params_from_config, which never reads style (voice_ssml.py:29-58). selectVoice writing styles[0] on every selection (VoicePanel.tsx:388) is confirmed, as is the 'style not offered' banner at 555-562. Contained to prosody, so MINOR is right.

title: PersistenceNotice promises 'a published call is synthesized with what you hear here' but pause_ms never reaches a call and speed/warmth are rendered differently at runtime
mechanism: PARAM_AZURE_TTS declares pause_ms as an SSML control (registry.py:121-122) and the panel writes it to voice.pauseMs (VoicePanel.tsx:740). apply_voice_config_overlay takes no pause argument (tuning.py:359-366) and tts_settings_kwargs emits none (tuning_apply.py:232-254); build_voice_ssml, the only runtime consumer of pauseMs (voice_ssml.py:57,83), has no caller. For the other three: preview clamps speed to 0.5-1.5 and adds a warmth pitch/rate bias plus catalog-aware express-as (azure_speech.py:246-252, 177-220), while runtime uses rate=clamp(0.85..1.25, speed*1.03), pitch=p*2%, and a fixed friendly/empathetic style regardless of the voice's StyleList (tuning.py:391-406). The notice at VoiceParamsPanel.tsx:333-343 asserts equivalence.
trigger: Set Sentence pause to 1200 ms (or speed 1.5) on an Azure voice, preview, publish, call: the pause is absent and the speed is capped at 1.25×1.03.
fix: Either fold pauseMs into tuning (e.g. tts.params.pause_ms consumed by a sentence-break text filter) and unify the warmth/speed mapping into one shared function used by both azure_speech.build_ssml and apply_voice_config_overlay, or reword the notice to name which controls ship and mark pause_ms 'preview only' in the schema.
verify_reason: pause_ms is declared as an SSML control with default 320 (registry.py:121-122) and the panel writes it to voice.pauseMs (VoicePanel.tsx:740), yet apply_voice_config_overlay takes no pause argument (tuning.py:359-366) and build_voice_ssml — the only runtime consumer of pauseMs (voice_ssml.py:61-84) — has no caller anywhere in backend/ (grep: only the agent_core/__init__ re-export). The one live use of pause_ms is the preview (main.py:3170 → azure_speech.build_ssml:246). One refinement: tts_settings_kwargs does not 'emit none' — the params bag is copied in by setdefault (tuning_apply.py:252-253), so pause_ms/warmth do reach kwargs once the operator drags the slider; they are then dropped by the Settings-class filter (factory.py:235-239 / tuning_apply.py:269-277), so the outcome the finding states is right. The speed/warmth divergence is confirmed: preview clamps speed*_warmth_rate_scale to 0.5-1.5 with a warmth pitch bias and catalog-aware express-as (azure_speech.py:177-220, 246-252), while runtime uses clamp(0.85..1.25, speed*1.03), pitch*2%, and a fixed friendly/empathetic pair (tuning.py:391-409). The notice asserting equivalence is at VoiceParamsPanel.tsx:332-343.

title: Azure controls display schema defaults while the wire/runtime use the VoiceConfig columns when params lacks the key
mechanism: VoiceParamsPanel renders `values[spec.key] ?? spec.default` (line 190) with values = voice.params (VoicePanel.tsx:254,723). The Azure preview path ignores params and uses payload.speed/pitch/warmth/pauseMs (main.py:3163-3171), and the runtime fold uses voice.speed/pitch/warmth (db_prompt_studio.py:1740-1748). A version whose columns differ from the schema defaults (rate 1.0, pitch 0, warmth 62, pause 320 — registry.py:114-122) but whose params bag lacks those keys (every version saved before params existed, every Sandbox-promoted or restored one: _restorable_voice resets params to {} at 2190) shows the default in the slider while preview and call use the column. Only once the operator drags the slider do the two reconverge (VoicePanel.tsx:733-741 writes both).
trigger: Open the Voice tab on a version with e.g. warmth 45 and params {} (the mock seed's v1.1 shape): the Warmth control reads 62, Preview plays warmth 45.
fix: In VoicePanel, seed the four Azure display values from the columns: pass `values={{...modelParams, rate: value.speed, pitch: value.pitch, warmth: value.warmth, pause_ms: value.pauseMs}}` for the azure provider (display only, no write).
verify_reason: VoiceParamsPanel renders `values[spec.key] ?? spec.default` (line 190) over values=modelParams=value.params ?? {} (VoicePanel.tsx:254, 723). The Azure schema defaults are rate 1.0 / pitch 0 / warmth 62 / pause_ms 320 (registry.py:114-123), while the preview request carries cfg.speed/pitch/warmth/pauseMs from the columns (VoicePanel.tsx:438-448 → main.py:3163-3171) and the save fold reads the same columns (db_prompt_studio.py:1740-1748). _prompt_voice always yields params {} when the stored jsonb has no params key (db_prompt_studio.py:122), so any pre-params version whose columns were edited displays the default and previews/speaks the column. The trigger example is real: the seed's v1_1 is `{...DEFAULT_VOICE, warmth: 45}` with no params (prompt-studio-seed.ts:268). One overreach: _restorable_voice resets params to {} only when the warning code is missing/removed (db_prompt_studio.py:2185-2190), not on every restore/promote. Display-only divergence, so MINOR.

title: Language-agnostic voices (locale 'und') trip the locale-mismatch lozenge and G15 as 'voice speaks und'
mechanism: primarySubtag('und') is 'und' (VoicePanel.tsx:63-65; compile.py:191), which is never in the card's {en, hi, ...} set, so localeMismatch returns {spoken:'und'} and G15 returns warn 'voice speaks und, card speaks en-IN' (compile.py:219-226). The catalog does hold such rows: VoiceCatalogTable renders locale==='und' as 'auto' (341-345) and provider_tts documents 'und means the vendor gave no language' (137-140). The publish dialog then asks the operator to confirm a mismatch that does not exist.
trigger: Select a Cartesia voice whose row has locale 'und'; the inspector shows 'Locale mismatch — voice speaks und' and compile reports G15 warn.
fix: Treat 'und' (and empty) as 'no claim' in both primarySubtag callers: return null / skip G15 with detail 'voice is language-agnostic'.
verify_reason: primarySubtag('und')==='und' (VoicePanel.tsx:63-65) and _primary_subtag does the same server-side (compile.py:191); 'und' is non-empty so _voice_locale_gate does not take the 'not in the catalog' skip at 211-216 and falls through to the warn at 220-225 ('voice speaks und, card speaks en-IN'), and localeMismatch at VoicePanel.tsx:219-224 renders the lozenge for the same reason. Such rows exist by construction, not by accident: provider_voice_sync writes locale 'und' for openrouter (line 222), elevenlabs (193), Fish rows with no languages (265) and Cartesia rows with no language (117); VoiceCatalogTable renders them as 'auto' (344-348) and provider_tts documents 'und means the vendor gave no language' (137-140). Warning-only gate, so MINOR is right.

title: Detail sheet Cost row still attributes Azure pricing to non-Azure voices
mechanism: tierBadge was fixed to show 'See provider' for providerId !== 'azure' (Browser:67-82), but VoiceDetailCard's Cost row (VoicePanel.tsx:900-907) still prints `~$${approxUsdPer1MChars} / 1M chars` or 'See Azure pricing'. approxUsdPer1MChars comes from LEFT JOIN tts_price_tiers on c.price_tier (db_prompt_studio.py:1180-1184) — Azure's published band — so a Fish/Cartesia row with price_tier 'standard' shows Azure's $15 and one with NULL says 'See Azure pricing'. Both name the wrong vendor.
trigger: Click the (i) on any non-Azure row.
fix: Reuse the tierBadge rule: when voice.providerId && voice.providerId !== 'azure', render 'See provider pricing' and never the number.
verify_reason: VoiceDetailCard's Cost row is provider-blind: `voice.approxUsdPer1MChars != null ? ~$X / 1M chars : 'See Azure pricing'` (VoicePanel.tsx:900-907), while tierBadge right above it in the same dialog already gates on providerId !== 'azure' → 'See provider' (VoiceCatalogBrowser.tsx:74-82). approxUsdPer1MChars is the unconditional LEFT JOIN tts_price_tiers ON t.tier = c.price_tier in both the list (db_prompt_studio.py:1143-1148) and the detail read (1173-1181), i.e. Azure's published band, and non-Azure rows land on it because provider_voice_sync inserts them without a price_tier so the column default applies. Reached by clicking the (i) on any non-Azure row (VoiceCatalogTable/Browser onOpenDetail → VoicePanel.openDetail:523-531).

title: A failed detail lookup is rendered as the business verdict 'Unknown voice … runtime will speak the fallback'; a failed warning lookup is rendered as no warning
mechanism: useSelectedCatalogVoice's `.catch` stores {voice:null} for any rejection — 404, 500, network, 401 (Browser:1010-1014) — and the header then says 'Unknown voice <id>' (VoicePanel.tsx:646-648), whose comment asserts the runtime will speak the fallback. fetchTtsVoiceWarning's catch sets warning to null (VoicePanel.tsx:334-335), so an API outage hides a real 'removed' warning; openDetail swallows too (528-530). No toast or retry in any branch.
trigger: API unreachable or returning 5xx while the Voice tab is open: every selected voice reads 'Unknown voice', no catalog warning is shown, Preview still works.
fix: Distinguish isNotFound(err) from other errors in useSelectedCatalogVoice (resolution 'error' with a retry affordance) and toast on non-404 failures of fetchTtsVoiceWarning.
verify_reason: useSelectedCatalogVoice's `.catch` stores {shortName, voice:null} for any rejection (VoiceCatalogBrowser.tsx:1010-1014) and the hook then returns resolution 'unknown' (1023-1025), which the inspector renders as the business verdict `Unknown voice ${shortName}` under a comment asserting the runtime will speak the fallback (VoicePanel.tsx:642-649). fetchTtsVoiceWarning's catch sets warning to null (VoicePanel.tsx:334-336), so a 5xx/network failure hides a real 'removed' banner that would otherwise render at 550-554; openDetail swallows identically (528-530). No toast or retry in any of the three. Contained to the tab during an API outage, so MINOR.

title: Table column sort orders only the pages loaded so far while the header implies a catalog-wide sort
mechanism: sorted = [...items].sort(...) (Table:108-119) where items is pages.flatMap (Browser:226-229) of a keyset-paginated query ordered by locale, display_name (db_prompt_studio.py:1149). Sorting 'Voice' A→Z on a 774-row result with 50 loaded shows 50 alphabetised rows; scrolling appends the next page, which re-sorts and interleaves, moving rows the operator was reading.
trigger: Filter to Azure, click the Voice header, scroll.
fix: Pass sort key/dir to /tts-voices/catalog as server-side ORDER BY (with a matching keyset cursor), or disable header sort until hasNextPage is false and say so in the header title.
verify_reason: sorted = [...items].sort(pick(a).localeCompare(pick(b)) * dir) (VoiceCatalogTable.tsx:106-119) where items is catalogQuery.data.pages.flatMap (VoiceCatalogBrowser.tsx:226-229) of a keyset query ordered by locale, display_name, short_name with a short_name cursor (db_prompt_studio.py:1149, 1125-1130). So the header sort covers only the pages fetched so far, and onEndReached (Browser:702-706) appends a page that re-sorts and interleaves under the reader. Reachable exactly as stated: filter to Azure, click the Voice header, scroll.

title: Icon-only delete button has no accessible name; its only warning is a title tooltip
mechanism: The button's only child is `<Trash2 aria-hidden-less icon />` (:229) with no aria-label and no visually hidden text; the `title` (:223-227) is the sole carrier of both the name and the "affects every card" warning. Screen-reader users hear an unnamed button in every row; the tenant-scope warning is unreachable by keyboard and on touch. Contrast with the Locale/Priority inputs in the same file, which do carry aria-label (:119, :127).
trigger: Tab to the delete control in any binding row with a screen reader.
fix: Add an aria-label that states scope and action (e.g. `Remove tenant-default text-to-speech binding — affects every card`), and move the warning into visible copy or a confirm dialog (see BINDINGS-4).
verify_reason: The central claim is wrong. Line 229 is `<Trash2 className="h-3.5 w-3.5" />` — the finding's own quotation ('aria-hidden-less icon') is a paraphrase, not the code. Under the HTML-AAM/accname algorithm, a button with no text content and no aria-label/aria-labelledby takes its accessible name from the title attribute, and this button carries one at :223-227 — so a screen-reader user does NOT hear an unnamed button, they hear either 'Inherited from the tenant — removing it affects every card' or 'Remove this binding', i.e. the warning reaches assistive tech, contradicting both sentences of the mechanism. (The lucide-react svg contributes no accessible text: it renders with no role and no title child.) What survives is narrow and cosmetic: title tooltips are not shown on keyboard focus in mainstream browsers and are unreachable on touch, so a sighted keyboard or touch operator sees no warning — a visible tone/label difference would be better. That is TRIVIAL, not MINOR. (Line 128, not 127, is the Priority aria-label.)

title: No test covers the bindings CRUD endpoints or the tab
mechanism: backend/tests covers provider_bind's fallback semantics (test_voice_provider_bind.py), the pool, preview routing and registry runtime status — but nothing exercises POST/DELETE /providers/bindings, so the missing slot/kind check (BINDINGS-2) and the voice_ref-nulling upsert (BINDINGS-7) have no failing test to catch them. There is no test file for BindingsTab.tsx anywhere under Habibi/src, so the tenant-scoped delete and the un-reset modelId are unguarded on both sides.
trigger: n/a — coverage observation.
fix: Add an API test asserting a 422 on slot/kind mismatch and that a re-upsert preserves voice_ref, and a component test asserting that changing Slot clears the chosen model and that deleting an inherited row requires confirmation.
verify_reason: The observation is factually right. Grep for 'providers/bindings|upsert_binding|delete_binding' across backend/tests returns no matches, and the only backend/tests hits for agent_provider_bindings are comments in test_rls.py:45 and test_tenant_scoping.py:61 — the provider test files that exist are test_provider_pool.py, test_provider_preview_routing.py, test_provider_registry_runtime.py and test_voice_provider_bind.py, none of which exercise the CRUD endpoints. On the frontend, enumerating every *.test.* under Habibi/src returns 19 files and none is for BindingsTab or api/providers.ts. But a coverage gap is not itself incorrect behaviour: the defects it fails to catch are already filed as BINDINGS-2 and BINDINGS-7, and severity here would double-count them. TRIVIAL as a standalone item.

title: _FLOW_CONTROL_TOOLS declares verify_identity, contradicting its own docstring and shadowing the catalog description everywhere
mechanism: The dict's docstring says it holds "Flow-control tools that exist only inside `voice.tools.build_tools` and so are absent from the channel-agnostic `agent_core.tools.CATALOG`" (flow_graph.py:766-772). `verify_identity` (flow_graph.py:775) is in the catalog — it is `VERIFY_IDENTITY` at catalog.py:188-212, and grant.py:73-80 explains at length why it is a catalog tool. Because `entries.update(_FLOW_CONTROL_TOOLS)` runs after the catalog loop (flow_graph.py:822), the palette's description for verify_identity is the short flow-control string, not the catalog's "Verify caller identity before any account details are shared. Call only after the caller has spoken digits — never with placeholder text."
trigger: The Tools tab (AgentCardPanels.tsx:159) and the skill editor's tool picker both render `t.description` as the authoritative statement of what the model is told. For this one tool — the gate every regulated write sits behind — they show a paraphrase that omits the "never with placeholder text" instruction that is actually in the prompt.
fix: Remove the `verify_identity` entry from `_FLOW_CONTROL_TOOLS` (its 9 remaining entries are genuinely catalog-absent), and reverse the merge order or use `setdefault` so a catalog description can never be shadowed again.
verify_reason: Factually correct. The docstring says these tools 'are absent from the channel-agnostic agent_core.tools.CATALOG' (flow_graph.py:766-773), yet 'verify_identity' is a key of the dict (flow_graph.py:775) while VERIFY_IDENTITY is in CATALOG (catalog.py:188-211, channels=VOICE_ONLY) and grant.py:73-80 argues at length for keeping it there. Because entries.update(_FLOW_CONTROL_TOOLS) runs after the catalog loop (flow_graph.py:822), the short flow-control string wins, and both pickers render t.description (AgentCardPanels.tsx:159, skills.$skillId.tsx via useCatalogTools) — so the author never sees 'never with placeholder text'. The entry is pure redundancy: the catalog loop already emits verify_identity on the voice filter, so deleting the key changes nothing but the description. Downgraded to TRIVIAL because the only consumer is descriptive text in an editor: the model's actual instruction comes from the ToolSpec via to_flows_schema (schema.py:158-176), unaffected; no runtime, publish or grant behaviour changes. The finding's phrase 'the authoritative statement of what the model is told' overstates it — the palette description is not what the model is told.

title: capture_call_goal is the one voice handler that skips CATALOG.normalize, making its declared alias inert
mechanism: `CAPTURE_CALL_GOAL.goal_summary` declares `aliases=("goalSummary",)` (catalog.py:177). Every other voice handler opens with `args = CATALOG.normalize("<name>", args)` — twenty call sites, e.g. verify_identity at voice/tools.py:719 — but `_capture_call_goal_handler` reads `args.get("goal_summary")` directly (voice/tools.py:632). The alias therefore resolves on no channel: the tool is VOICE_ONLY, and voice is the only place it could have been applied.
trigger: A model emitting `goalSummary` (the shape the legacy catalog published, which is why the alias exists) gets `empty_goal` and is told to "ask what they need, then call again" — a re-ask of a caller who already stated their goal. The Flows schema publishes only the canonical name, so this needs a model that drifts, not a normal turn; hence TRIVIAL.
fix: Insert `args = CATALOG.normalize("capture_call_goal", args)` at voice/tools.py:632, matching every sibling. Alternatively drop the alias from the spec if the legacy shape can no longer appear.
verify_reason: _capture_call_goal_handler opens with goal = str(args.get('goal_summary') or '').strip() and returns {'error':'empty_goal','say':'ask what they need, then call again'} when empty (voice/tools.py:628-637) — no CATALOG.normalize call anywhere in the handler. Every sibling normalises, e.g. verify_identity at voice/tools.py:719, add_customer_note at :1630, request_callback at :1555, check_product_eligibility at :1804. CAPTURE_CALL_GOAL.goal_summary declares aliases=('goalSummary',) (catalog.py:167-178) and the tool is VOICE_ONLY (catalog.py:180), so the alias resolves on no channel — normalize_args (schema.py:186-200) is the only thing that would apply it. TRIVIAL is right: it needs a model that drifts from the published schema.

title: No CRM write carries a timeout_secs while the one KB read does
mechanism: `timeout_secs` is rendered into the Pipecat `FlowsFunctionSchema` only when set (schema.py:174-176), and `search_knowledge_base` is the only spec that sets it (catalog.py:859, 20s). Every CRM write — create_promise_to_pay, flag_dispute, request_callback, request_documents, capture_lead, apply_goodwill — runs `domain.*` inside `asyncio.to_thread` (e.g. voice/tools.py:1272-1281) with no declared bound, so a saturated connection pool or a lock wait holds the audio path for as long as the driver does. `cancel_on_interruption` is correctly left False on all of them (a write must not be cancelled mid-flight), so the timeout is the only available bound.
trigger: Not demonstrated — I did not trace Pipecat Flows' own default handler timeout, so I cannot show that a hung `db.create_promise` produces unbounded dead air rather than a framework-level abort. The asymmetry itself is unambiguous: the cheapest read on the card has a ceiling and the money writes do not.
fix: Confirm the FlowManager's default (pipecat.flows) first. If there is none, give the six write specs a generous `timeout_secs` (10-15s) so the model gets a failure it can speak around — `domain` already returns `crm_write_failed` with a spoken fallback for every one of them — instead of silence.
verify_reason: The observation is factually accurate: timeout_secs is set on exactly one spec in the whole catalog (catalog.py:859, search_knowledge_base, 20s — verified by grep across catalog.py/schema.py/voice/tools.py), it is rendered into FlowsFunctionSchema only when not None (schema.py:174-176), and none of the CRM writes declare one while running domain.* inside asyncio.to_thread (voice/tools.py:1268-1281 and siblings). I also checked for a wrapper-level bound in the _spec factory region (voice/tools.py:1034-1040) and found none. But the reporter states outright that the consequence is not traced — whether Pipecat Flows applies a default handler timeout is unknown, so 'unbounded dead air on a hung db.create_promise' is asserted, not shown. Under the rule that an undecidable trigger defaults against the finding, this stays as an unproven design asymmetry rather than a defect: no demonstrated wrong behaviour, no operator-visible lie. TRIVIAL.

title: The tab's error state has no retry control, unlike the identical error state on the fleet panel
mechanism: `ChangeLogTab` destructures only `{data, isPending, isError, error}` (ChangeLogTab.tsx:177) and its error branch renders a warning box with no action (:187-197), so recovering from a transient failure requires switching tabs or reloading. The fleet panel destructures `refetch`/`isFetching` and renders a Retry button beside the same failure (agent-studio.index.tsx:229, :311-321). Both error copies are honest — neither renders the failure as an empty log — so this is a control gap, not a lie.
trigger: Change log request fails on the tab: the only affordance is to navigate away.
fix: Pull `refetch`/`isFetching` off the hook and add the same Retry button the fleet panel uses.
verify_reason: ChangeLogTab destructures only { data, isPending, isError, error } from useChangeLog (Habibi/src/components/prompt-studio/ChangeLogTab.tsx:177), so refetch is not in scope, and the error branch renders a static warning box with no button or link (:187-197). The fleet sibling destructures refetch and isFetching (Habibi/src/routes/agent-studio.index.tsx:229) and renders a Retry Button with loading/disabled state beside the same failure (:311-321). Both error copies are honest and neither renders the failure as an empty log — the tab says "Change log unavailable — chain integrity cannot be confirmed, so treat it as unverified rather than intact" (:192-193), the fleet says "this is not a record of nothing happening — it is a record that could not be shown" (:334-336). So this is a control gap, not a lie, and TRIVIAL is the right severity: recovery costs a tab switch or a reload.

title: The tab promises "Compiler G10 checks HTTPS, data-class, and health" while MCP_CLIENT_ENABLED=false makes G10 skip entirely, and no screen reports that flag
mechanism: compile.py:758-760 emits G10 "skipped — MCP client flag is off" when mcp_client_enabled() is false, and dispatch returns {"ok": False, "error": "mcp_client_disabled"} (persist.py:254-255). The shipped default is MCP_CLIENT_ENABLED=false (.env.example:325). GET /connectors still lists every row regardless of the flag (main.py:2537-2541), and GET /mcp/status reports httpEnabled, tasksEnabled and appsEnabled but not clientEnabled (main.py:2660-2670) — so neither the Studio tab nor the Integrations MCP panel can tell the operator the whole connector subsystem is switched off.
trigger: On a default deployment an author binds connectors, sees a green G10 skipped (not fail), publishes, and believes the HTTPS/data-class/health checks ran. They did not, and no connector tool binds.
fix: Add `clientEnabled: mcp_client_enabled()` to GET /mcp/status and surface it on both screens; when it is false, render a banner on the Connectors tab saying bindings are inert and G10 will skip rather than check.
verify_reason: The facts are right but the deception the severity rests on is refuted. True: G10 emits skipped 'MCP client flag is off' (compile.py:758-759), dispatch returns mcp_client_disabled (persist.py:254-255), bound_tool_names returns [] (persist.py:211-212), the shipped default is MCP_CLIENT_ENABLED=false (backend/.env.example:325), GET /connectors lists rows regardless (main.py:2525-2529), and GET /mcp/status returns httpEnabled/tasksEnabled/appsEnabled/mtls with no clientEnabled (main.py:2646-2666). False: 'no screen reports that flag'. The publish path renders the gate detail verbatim — PublishDialog.tsx:178 renders CompileReportList, which prints g.detail beside the status lozenge (AgentCardPanels.tsx:1023-1025, 1026-1038), so the author publishing sees 'G10 connectors skipped MCP client flag is off' rather than a green pass. What remains is the Connectors tab's unconditional copy 'Compiler G10 checks HTTPS, data-class, and health' (:944-945) and the missing clientEnabled field on /mcp/status — wording and a missing status field, no wrong verdict and no lie at publish time.

title: allow_prefixes are a bind-time filter only — dispatch never checks them
mechanism: dispatch resolves the connector from `connector_id` or from `name.split(".")[1]` (persist.py:258-261), checks status and circuit, then calls _call_remote — it never asks whether `name` falls inside the connector's or the card's allow_prefixes. Enforcement lives only in bot_tools.execute_tool's `ctx.allowed_tools` membership check (bot_tools.py:806), which is derived from the Grant. Any caller that reaches dispatch directly — _tool_get_customer_context (bot_tools.py:158-160) does exactly that — bypasses the prefix restriction entirely.
trigger: A future direct dispatch call (or a Grant computed from a different card than the one running) invokes an ext.* name outside the bound prefixes; the registry lets it through.
fix: Move the prefix check into dispatch: resolve the connector, then refuse with {"ok": False, "error": "connector_prefix_not_bound"} unless `name` starts with one of the connector's allow_prefixes. Enforcement belongs at the point of execution, the way grant.may_execute does for catalog tools.
verify_reason: The mechanism is real — dispatch resolves the connector from connector_id or name.split('.')[1] (persist.py:257-261), checks flag, status and circuit (:254, :262-265) and calls _call_remote with no prefix test anywhere in :238-289 — but no trigger is reachable today, so MAJOR-adjacent MINOR is inflated. The Grant path is closed: execute_tool requires name in ctx.allowed_tools (bot_tools.py:806-808) and that set comes from bound_tool_names, which applies the prefixes (persist.py:224, :233). The one direct caller, _tool_get_customer_context (bot_tools.py:158-160), passes a fixed first-party name that dispatch routes through FIRST_PARTY_TOOLS below the status and circuit gates (persist.py:266-271) — deliberate, and pinned by backend/tests/test_connector_governance.py:1-20. The stated trigger is explicitly hypothetical ('a future direct dispatch call'). What survives is defence-in-depth: the registry would not stop a prefix-violating name if a caller ever reached it, plus the fact that the paylink prefetch is gated by registry status rather than by the card's binding. Would be re-raised by any new direct dispatch caller with a model-supplied name.

title: eval_tasks.pass_bar is written by every seeder and read by nothing
mechanism: The column exists with a default of 'all' and every insert path sets it explicitly (fixtures.py:452,494,533,638,651; corpus.py:81-83; graduate.py:40-41; sql/23_outbound_evals.sql:42+). load_suite_fixtures does not select it (run.py:47-52) and run_suite_fixtures hardcodes all-must-pass — `status = "pass" if failed == 0` (harness.py:27). A task written with any other bar would be graded as 'all' silently.
trigger: Set pass_bar='majority' on a task; nothing changes.
fix: Honour it in the harness or drop the column.
verify_reason: Verified: eval_tasks.pass_bar exists (sql/14_agent_factory.sql:26) and every insert path sets it — fixtures.py:452 and :494 (regression/outbound), :631/:643 (capability/twin), corpus.py:78-83 ('all' hardcoded in the INSERT), graduate.py:40-41. load_suite_fixtures selects only id, name, grader, fixture (run.py:47-52) so pass_bar never reaches the harness, and run_suite_fixtures hardcodes all-must-pass: `status = "pass" if failed == 0 else "fail"` (harness.py:27). A task written with any other bar is graded as 'all' silently. TRIVIAL is right — no shipped row uses another value.

title: get_latest_eval_report — the gate's only input — has no tenant predicate
mechanism: The gate lookup filters `WHERE r.bot_id = :bot AND s.kind = :kind` only (db_inbox.py:1593), while its neighbour list_eval_reports opens with `r.tenant_id = :tenant` (db_inbox.py:1673). Unreachable today because bots.id is a global primary key so one bot belongs to one tenant, but this is the single query that decides G7, G8 and G-OB9, and it is the one that does not name the tenant.
trigger: None reachable at present; a future bot-id scheme that is unique per tenant rather than globally would make a cross-tenant report satisfy a publish gate.
fix: Add `AND r.tenant_id = :tenant` for symmetry with every other read in the module.
verify_reason: Verified and correctly rated TRIVIAL: get_latest_eval_report's WHERE is `r.bot_id = :bot AND s.kind = :kind` with no tenant predicate (db_inbox.py:1588-1594), while the neighbouring list_eval_reports opens its clause list with r.tenant_id = :tenant (db_inbox.py:1674). Not exploitable today because eval_reports.bot_id references the global bots primary key (sql/14_agent_factory.sql:45), so a bot id belongs to one tenant. Note this overlaps EVALS-1 on the same query but reports a distinct missing predicate, so it is not a duplicate.

title: Fleet and editor can disagree on reachability for targets of a first-party card that has no prompt version yet
mechanism: list_agent_studio_cards walks edges from every summary's agentCard, which for a first-party bot with no draft/published row is card_dump(bot_id) (db_prompt_studio.py:438-440) — Intake's default handoffs to Collections and Insurance count. get_agent_studio_card instead walks _handoff_edges(), a query over prompt_versions joined to bots (:523-531) that yields nothing for a bot without a version row, plus the requested card itself (:610). On a fresh install where intake-v1 has never been given a version, the fleet shows Insurance 'via handoff' while GET /agent-studio/cards/insurance-v1 (editor header, graph tab nodes at main.py:2277-2287 use the list, but the card's own row uses get) reports 'direct'.
trigger: Fresh database after migrations (bots seeded by alembic 0073, no prompt_versions for intake-v1); compare the fleet chip on insurance-v1 with the single-card GET.
fix: Have _handoff_edges union in card_dump defaults for FIRST_PARTY_BOTS that have no version row, or have get_agent_studio_card reuse list_agent_studio_cards' edge list.
verify_reason: The divergence is real but the auditor's stated outcome is wrong and there is no operator-visible symptom, so MINOR is inflated. Real part: list_agent_studio_cards walks `c["agentCard"]`, which for a first-party bot with no draft/published row falls back to card_dump(bot_id) (db_prompt_studio.py:438-442), whereas get_agent_studio_card walks _handoff_edges(), a query over prompt_versions (:507-536) that yields nothing for a bot with no version row. Wrong part: on the fresh-DB scenario the auditor describes, _handoff_edges returns nothing at all and _live_deployment_bot_ids returns nothing (:538-566), so `deployed` is empty and reachability() falls through to "unreachable" (routing.py:105-118), not "direct" — `direct` requires an active production deployment the scenario stipulates does not exist. Not-reachable part: nothing renders the single-card GET's reachability. A grep for `reachability` over Habibi/src finds it only in agent-studio.index.tsx (the fleet, which uses the LIST), AgentCardPanels.tsx:674/694 (graph nodes, which main.py:2288-2291 also builds from db.list_agent_studio_cards), and the agent-roster.ts type — the studio shell never displays it. So this is an API-only inconsistency between two internal code paths with no UI consequence: TRIVIAL. What would settle it as higher: a UI surface that renders GET /agent-studio/cards/{id}.reachability, or a fresh-install repro showing the two endpoints returning different values with a deployment present.

title: Toggling 'Show archived' replaces the whole roster with the loading spinner
mechanism: includeArchived is part of the query key (agent-studio.ts:209) and the query sets no placeholderData, so the first render after the checkbox flips has data undefined and isLoading true → the `isLoading && !data` branch (index.tsx:523) unmounts every card and shows 'Loading fleet'; focus on the checkbox survives but the grid the user was reading jumps to a spinner and back.

verify_reason: useAgentStudioCards puts includeArchived in the query key — `queryKey: ["agent-studio", "cards", includeArchived]` (agent-studio.ts:207-217) — and passes no placeholderData/keepPreviousData. Toggling the checkbox (index.tsx:386, 453-458) therefore switches to a cache entry with data undefined and isLoading true, which hits the `isLoading && !data` branch at :523-526 and replaces the entire grid with <LoadingState label="Loading fleet" />. TRIVIAL is right: the roster returns intact, focus stays on the checkbox, only the reading position is lost.

title: Create draft has no in-flight indicator, unlike every sibling control on the screen
mechanism: The Retry buttons (index.tsx:316-317, 536-537) and ReasonedAction (:165-166) pass `loading` alongside `disabled`; the Create draft button only sets `disabled={clone.isPending || !templateId}` (:503), so a slow clone (bots INSERT + prompt_versions INSERT + full card summary) reads as an inexplicably greyed button rather than a pending action.

title: Copy drift: card-vocabulary returns 'inbound' although the inspector comment says the endpoint excludes it; reload toasts say 'steps' vs 'nodes'
