title: whenDraft shadows the saved `when` after Remove/Allow or an external draft change
mechanism: whenDraft is per-target local state that is never cleared; the input value is `whenDraft[n.id] ?? on.when`, so after Remove then Allow the old text reappears (and Allow at :718 writes it back), and if the draft is discarded/restored while the graph tab stays mounted the input keeps showing text the card no longer holds until the next blur rewrites it.
trigger: Type a when, Remove, Allow again; or Discard draft with the graph tab open.
fix: Delete whenDraft[n.id] in setHandoff (on remove and on blur commit) and key the input on the card's when.
verify_reason: Verified in the source: `const [whenDraft, setWhenDraft] = useState<Record<string,string>>({})` (AgentCardPanels.tsx:587) is never reset — there is no setWhenDraft call other than the input's onChange (:710). The input renders `value={whenDraft[n.id] ?? on.when ?? ''}` (:709), and the Allow/Remove button passes `whenDraft[n.id] ?? ''` back into setHandoff on re-Allow (:718). So after typing a condition, Removing, and Allowing again the stale text is written back to the card, and a draft discard that leaves the tab mounted keeps showing text the card no longer holds. Confidence SUSPECTED is fair but the code is unambiguous. TRIVIAL is correct — the value is dead config anyway (GRAPH-3) and the next blur rewrites it.

title: Duration readout rounds half-minutes and out-of-range stored values are shown clamped while state keeps the raw number
mechanism: The slider steps by 30s but the label prints Math.round(maxSeconds/60)+'m', so 150s reads '3m' and 450s reads '8m'. _prompt_guardrails coerces but does not clamp (db_prompt_studio.py:145-146), so a row holding maxTurns=3 or maxSeconds=60 renders the thumb at the slider minimum while the fingerprint/autosave keeps the raw value; nudging the thumb silently rewrites it into range. The word input also still has no aria-label (prior 2f trivia).
trigger: Drag Max call duration to 2.5 minutes; or open a version whose guardrails were written outside the Studio.
fix: Format as m:ss (or step by 60), and clamp in _prompt_guardrails or show the raw value in the readout.
verify_reason: Readout is Math.round(value.maxSeconds / 60) + 'm' at GuardrailsPanel.tsx:160 with step={30} min={120} max={900} at :163-168, so the reachable values 150s and 450s render '3m' and '8m'. db_prompt_studio.py:145-146 coerces with int(...) and applies no clamp, so a row holding maxSeconds=60 or maxTurns=3 is returned as-is while the Slider renders the thumb at its min — the first drag writes an in-range value over it. The prohibited-word <input> at GuardrailsPanel.tsx:98-104 still carries only a placeholder, no aria-label (matches prior 2f trivia, but the rounding and clamp halves are new information, so this is not a pure duplicate). TRIVIAL stands.

title: WhatsApp's own 'already disclosed' detector uses substring markers that diverge from the canonical disclosure regex
mechanism: _history_already_disclosed_recording matches 'recorded for quality', 'call is recorded', 'whatsapp is recorded', 'recorded for compliance' as bare substrings (bot_runtime.py:259) and drives the dialog-control line 'Recording disclosure was already given — do not repeat it' (:280-283). mentions_recording_disclosure (guardrails.py:31-46) is the declared canonical home ('so the authoring gate and the runtime detector cannot drift apart') and does not accept 'this WhatsApp is recorded' (subject must be call/conversation/chat) while it does accept wordings the substring list misses ('we are recording this conversation'). The same turn can be 'disclosed' for the prompt and 'missing' for the guardrail, or vice versa.
trigger: Bot writes 'This WhatsApp chat is recorded for quality' — dialog block says disclosed; evaluate_guardrails (once GUARDRAILS-1 is fixed by threading recording_disclosed) would still count it as missing unless both use one predicate.
fix: Replace the marker tuple with agent_core.guardrails.mentions_recording_disclosure and pass the result as recording_disclosed to evaluate_and_flag_bot_turn.
verify_reason: The divergence is real: bot_runtime.py:258-266 matches four bare substrings ('recorded for quality', 'call is recorded', 'whatsapp is recorded', 'recorded for compliance') and drives the dialog line at :280-283, while the canonical mentions_recording_disclosure (guardrails.py:30-56) requires subject call/conversation/chat or the 'recorded for <quality|training|compliance|verification|monitoring>' clause. Genuine divergences exist in both directions ('we are recording this conversation' → canonical yes, markers no; 'this WhatsApp is recorded' → markers yes, canonical no). But the auditor's own trigger example is WRONG: 'This WhatsApp chat is recorded for quality' matches BOTH — the marker 'recorded for quality' and the canonical alternative r'\brecorded\s+for\s+(?:quality|…)' — so the stated demonstration does not demonstrate anything. More importantly the consequence the finding leans on is conditional on GUARDRAILS-1 being fixed: today bot_runtime never passes recording_disclosed, so the two predicates never judge the same fact, and the sole live effect of a marker miss is one optional 'do not repeat it' prompt line on a channel whose prompt already forbids the disclosure outright (prompt.py:117-125). Latent, cosmetic today: TRIVIAL.

title: Toggle hint 'Flags missing disclosure on turn 1' understates the check; the mock lint uses a looser 'record' substring than the server
mechanism: The flag fires on every bot turn with turn_index >= 1 until a disclosure has been heard (guardrails.py:250-253), not 'on turn 1'. Separately the USE_MOCK lint path tests /record/i (prompt-studio.ts:779) while the server uses the strict mentions_recording_disclosure regex (prompt_lint.py:140), so mock mode reports 'duplicated' for a prompt containing 'record your promise to pay' that the real server would not flag.
trigger: Read the hint; or run the UI in mock mode with such a prompt.
fix: Change the hint to 'Flags every turn until the disclosure has been made' and reuse the same disclosure regex in the mock.
verify_reason: Both halves check out. (a) GuardrailsPanel.tsx:40 says 'Flags missing disclosure on turn 1'; guardrails.py:240-243 flags on EVERY bot turn with turn_index >= _DISCLOSURE_DEADLINE_TURN (=1, :22) until a disclosure is seen, so the hint understates it. (b) Habibi/src/api/prompt-studio.ts:779 is 'const discloses = /record/i.test(input.prompt)' while prompt_lint.py:140 uses the strict mentions_recording_disclosure; a prompt containing 'record your promise to pay' therefore reports recording_disclosure_duplicated in USE_MOCK and nothing on the server. TRIVIAL stands (wording + mock-only divergence).

title: A card that has never published offers "Publish v1.1" — v1.0 can never be minted
mechanism: `nextLabel = nextVersionLabel(publishedRow?.label ?? "v1.0")`. When nothing is published the fallback "v1.0" is fed through the incrementer, which returns "v1.1" (prompt-studio-seed.ts:364). So the first version of every new or cloned card is stamped v1.1 and the header reads "never published" beside "Publish v1.1" (StudioHeader.tsx:79, 173). The stored id also becomes `v1_1` (db_prompt_studio.py:1617,1534), so a card's history can never contain a v1.0 authored through the Studio.
trigger: Clone a card and look at the header before the first publish.
fix: Pass the seed label rather than its predecessor: `const nextLabel = publishedRow ? nextVersionLabel(publishedRow.label) : "v1.0"` at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:541.
verify_reason: Confirmed at the lines. nextVersionLabel returns "v1.0" only for a non-matching input and otherwise increments (seed:362-364), so nextVersionLabel("v1.0") is "v1.1"; with nothing published, nextLabel = nextVersionLabel(publishedRow?.label ?? "v1.0") = "v1.1" (lazy.tsx:541), the header shows the "never published" lozenge (StudioHeader.tsx:78-79) beside "Publish v1.1" (:173), and the created row's id is slugged from the label to "v1_1" (db_prompt_studio.py:1530-1537, 1617). One refinement to the trigger: the button text is nextVersion={draftLabel} (:1253, :546-549), so it reads "v1.1" only while no draft row exists — once autosave has created the draft it shows that draft's label, which for a fresh card was itself minted from nextLabel and so is also v1.1. The conclusion holds: no Studio-authored card can contain a v1.0. TRIVIAL.

title: "Restore" leaves the History drawer open on top of the editor it just repopulated, while "Load" closes it
mechanism: `onLoadDraft` wraps `loadDraft(v)` with `setHistoryOpen(false)` (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1565-1568) and `onCompare` closes the drawer too (:1562). `onRestore={(v) => void restore(v)}` (:1564) does not, even though `restore` ends in the same `loadDraft` (:933) and produces the same "you are now editing something else" state change. The operator is left looking at a modal sheet over an editor whose contents just changed under it.
trigger: Open History and click Restore on any archived version.
fix: Close the drawer in the restore handler the way the load handler does — `onRestore={(v) => { setHistoryOpen(false); void restore(v); }}` at prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1564.
verify_reason: Confirmed, lines exact. onCompare closes the sheet (:1562) and onLoadDraft closes it (:1567), but onRestore={(v) => void restore(v)} at :1564 does not, and restore ends in the same loadDraft (:933) that repopulates the whole editor. The Restore button is the one rendered for every non-draft row (VersionHistory.tsx:287-292), so the operator is left on a modal sheet over an editor whose contents changed behind it. Cosmetic and self-recoverable (Esc or the overlay closes it), so TRIVIAL is right.

title: PublishDialog recomputes the full O(m·n) LCS diff on every Studio render, including every keystroke while the dialog is closed
mechanism: `<PublishDialog>` is mounted unconditionally (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:1583) with `to={{prompt, ...}}` rebuilt from live editor state on every render. The component body has no `open` guard and no memo: `const lines = diffStudioVersions(from, to)` runs at PublishDialog.tsx:72, plus three `stableStringify` pairs at :88-92, before any early return. `diffPrompts` allocates a full `(m+1)×(n+1)` number matrix and fills it (prompt-studio-seed.ts:330-335). For a 500-line prompt that is a ~275k-cell allocation and fill on every keystroke of the System Prompt tab, for a dialog nobody has opened. DiffModal has the same shape but is protected by its `if (!base) return null` at DiffModal.tsx:44.
trigger: Type into the System Prompt tab of a card with a long prompt; the LCS runs per render with the publish dialog closed.
fix: Add `if (!open) return null;` at the top of PublishDialog (the reset effect at :144-149 already keys on `open`, and Radix unmounts the content anyway), or wrap `lines` and the three changed-flags in `useMemo` keyed on `open` plus the stringified sides.
verify_reason: The mechanism is exactly as described and the lines are exact: PublishDialog is mounted unconditionally (lazy.tsx:1583) with a `to` object rebuilt from live editor state on every render (:1589-1601), the component body has no open guard and no memo, and diffStudioVersions runs at PublishDialog.tsx:72 followed by three stableStringify pairs at :88-92 before any early return; diffPrompts allocates and fills a full (m+1)x(n+1) matrix (seed:330-335); DiffModal's `if (!base) return null` at :44 is indeed the contrasting guard. But nothing behaves incorrectly — no wrong value, no wrong verdict, no lost data — and the cost is asserted, not measured: the 500-line prompt in the write-up is a hypothetical, real cards are an order of magnitude smaller, and the same render already re-runs the dirty/unsaved fingerprints and the auto-lint. Wasted work on the authoring surface is worth fixing (wrap the body in `if (!open) return null`), but at TRIVIAL, not MINOR. A profile showing per-keystroke frame cost would move it back.

title: VersionHistory's attempt-numbering docstring describes label inheritance the backend does not implement
mechanism: The docstring above `attemptSuffixes` states "A draft inherits the label of the version it descends from, and autosave, a sandbox promote and an authored edit each write one". restore-as-draft — the only write path that descends a draft from another version — stores `label: None` (db_prompt_studio.py:2252) and the row surfaces with its id as the label (:180). So restored drafts never share a label bucket with their parent and never get an "attempt N" suffix; the four-consecutive-v1.5 case the comment cites comes from repeated create-from-`nextLabel`, not from inheritance.
trigger: Restore any archived version and look at the timeline: the new row is labelled `<parent-id>-r-<hex>`, not the parent's label, and carries no attempt suffix.
fix: Either make restore inherit the label (see HEADER-2's fix, which makes the comment true) or correct the comment to say drafts are labelled from `nextVersionLabel` and that restores are id-labelled.
verify_reason: Accurate at the lines. The docstring at :74-76 asserts that a draft inherits the label of the version it descends from; no write path implements that. restore-as-draft stores label None (2252) and the row surfaces with its id as the label (:180), so a restored draft lands in its own bucket in attemptSuffixes (which keys on v.label || v.id, :85) and can never carry an "attempt N" suffix; the studio's other create path names a draft from nextLabel (lazy.tsx:541, 546-549), which is an increment, not an inheritance; and sandbox promote publishes an existing version rather than writing a labelled row (routes/sandbox.lazy.tsx:442-446). TRIVIAL is right — it is a stale comment. Note it carries no information beyond HEADER-2's mechanism plus the comment's location, so it should be folded into that finding's fix rather than tracked separately.

title: Two reachability label vocabularies, and the comment introducing the second one says they are the same
mechanism: `agent-studio.index.tsx:55-85` defines `ROUTING`, mapping the four backend states plus `archived` to operator-facing labels: "takes inbound", "via handoff", "direct only", "unreachable", "archived", each with its own help sentence. `AgentCardPanels.tsx:744-757` defines a second map, `ROUTE_TONE` + `ROUTE_HELP`, over the same five states — with different help text and no labels at all, so line 696-698 renders the raw enum word (`entry`, `handoff`, `direct`) as the chip. The comment at AgentCardPanels.tsx:743 asserts "Same vocabulary the fleet index uses, so one word does not mean two things" — the fleet says "takes inbound" and the Agent graph tab, one click away, says "entry" for the same card. The fleet's `routing()` helper (:88-90) also has an unknown-value fallback that the panel's `?? "neutral"` does not match.
trigger: Open the fleet index, note a card badged "direct only", click into it, open the Agent graph tab: the same card is badged "direct" with a differently worded tooltip.
fix: Move `ROUTING` out of `agent-studio.index.tsx` into `Habibi/src/lib/reachability.ts` alongside its `routing()` fallback, export `label`/`tone`/`help`, import it in `AgentCardPanels.tsx:694-698`, and delete `ROUTE_TONE`/`ROUTE_HELP`. This is the same shape as the `gate-status.ts` fix in ORG-02 and should land with it.
verify_reason: Facts check out, weight does not. agent-studio.index.tsx:55-85 defines ROUTING with labels ('takes inbound', 'via handoff', 'direct only', 'unreachable', 'archived') and per-state help; AgentCardPanels.tsx:743 carries the comment 'Same vocabulary the fleet index uses…', :744-751 ROUTE_TONE and :752-758 ROUTE_HELP; :694-701 renders `{n.reachability}` — the raw enum word — with `ROUTE_TONE[...] ?? "neutral"`, while the fleet's routing() helper (:88-90) falls back to ROUTING.unreachable. But the two TONE maps agree value-for-value on all five states (entry success, handoff information, direct information, unreachable warning, archived neutral), so no state is coloured two ways; the divergence is label text and help wording only, and the graph tab prints the enum beside the id it belongs to. title: Server accepts any persona.language string and any trait integer; an unregistered language publishes with G15 silently skipping and the recogniser silently unchanged
mechanism: PersonaTraits are unbounded ints and PersonaState.language is a bare str (schemas.py:2147-2162); _prompt_persona coerces but does not clamp or check the registry (db_prompt_studio.py:76-95). A language outside agent_core.languages yields no tag, so voice_locale_facts returns [] and G15 reports 'skipped — no voice or no card language' rather than a warning (compile.py:209-210); at call time tuning_apply only logs a warning (:419-427). Traits of 500 or -20 pass straight into persona_style_line's cut-points. The UI cannot author these values (select bound to LANGUAGES, sliders 0-100), so the trigger is API/legacy-row only.
trigger: PUT /prompt-versions/{id} with persona.language='Hinglish' or traits.empathy=500; publish succeeds with a green/skipped G15.
fix: Constrain PersonaTraits with Field(ge=0, le=100) and validate language against languages.names() (or make G15 'warn' when the primary language has no tag instead of 'skipped').
verify_reason: The mechanism is real but the consequences do not reach MINOR. Verified: PersonaTraits fields are bare `int` with no Field(ge/le) and PersonaState.language is a bare `str` (schemas.py:2147-2162); _prompt_persona coerces with int()/str() and neither clamps nor checks the registry (db_prompt_studio.py:71-91); an unregistered name yields no tag from languages.tag_for so voice_locale_facts returns [] (db_prompt_studio.py:1004-1011) and G15 reports 'skipped — no voice or no card language' rather than warning (compile.py:207-210); tuning_apply.py:419-427 only logs. But the harm is nil-to-cosmetic: out-of-range traits are only compared against the 35/65 cut-points (natural.py:114-121), so 500 behaves exactly as 100 and -20 as 0 — no crash, no wrong instruction; and an unmapped language changes no recogniser behaviour beyond what PERSONA-1 already establishes for every language. The auditor concedes the UI cannot author either value (select bound to LANGUAGES, which mirrors agent_core/languages.py:38-45 exactly; sliders min 0 max 100), so the only trigger is a hand-rolled authenticated API call, and no legacy row with an off-registry language was demonstrated. This is input hardening, not a defect with a live consequence — TRIVIAL. What would raise it back to MINOR: evidence of an existing prompt_versions row whose persona.language is outside the registry, or a G15 consumer that treats 'skipped' as 'pass'.

title: Changing the primary language leaves the old primary (or the new one) inside fallbackLanguages, hidden by the chip filter but persisted and rendered on text channels

title: The tab restates the six-key policy vocabulary locally and imports the shared constant without using it

mechanism: Every `owner_user_id` in the backend belongs to leads, promises or work items (db.py:4333, db_dashboard.py:364, etc.). The card's own owner is never read — not by authz.py for a permission check, not by the change log for attribution (which uses the acting user, agent_core/change_log.py), and not by any gate.

title: policy_bindings can only ever hold one value, so G3's binding half is unfalsifiable
mechanism: `PolicyBinding = Literal["required"]` (schema.py:20), so `getattr(card.policy_bindings, key, None) != "required"` at compile.py:601 can never be true for a card that parsed — any other value fails G0 first. Only the second half of G3 (`missing_locked`, :604) can actually fail. The six bindings are therefore a display-only structure, and no runtime path reads them: the reco/treatment/authority/live_qa engines take their mode from env (agent_core/reco/config.py:54, treatment/config.py:51, authority/config.py:24, live_qa/config.py:35), not from the card.
trigger: None — the branch is unreachable by construction. The visible symptom is a Policy tab presenting six controls whose only legal value is the one shown.
fix: Say so: collapse the six fields to a single computed assertion in the compile report, and have the Policy tab render the engines' actual runtime modes (which are env-driven and can legitimately be shadow) rather than six lozenges that cannot change.
verify_reason: Verified. PolicyBinding = Literal['required'] at schema.py:20 with all six PolicyBindings fields defaulting to 'required' (:133-141), so the `getattr(card.policy_bindings, key, None) != 'required'` comparison at compile.py:601 cannot be true for any card that parsed (extra='forbid' + the Literal make any other value fail parse first); only missing_locked (:604) can fail G3. policy_bindings has no reader outside compile.py:596-616, and the four engines take their mode from env config modules. TRIVIAL correct — the visible symptom is a display-only control set.

title: Sandbox tool-iteration budget is 4 where the live text runtime allows 6
mechanism: `_SANDBOX_MAX_TOOL_ITERS = 4` is a module constant with no env override (backend/sandbox_runtime.py:178); live reads BOT_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS with a default of 6 (backend/bot_runtime.py:54). A multi-tool turn that completes live can exhaust the budget in the sandbox and fall to the tool-free final completion (backend/sandbox_runtime.py:325-352).

verify_reason: Both constants are where claimed: _SANDBOX_MAX_TOOL_ITERS = 4 is a module constant with no env override (backend/sandbox_runtime.py:178) and the live text runtime reads BOT_MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS with a default of 6 (backend/bot_runtime.py:53-54, used at :958). On budget exhaustion the sandbox falls to a tool-free final completion (backend/sandbox_runtime.py:336-359). Latent behind SANDBOX-01, TRIVIAL as filed.

title: VoiceSandboxStartRequest declares four fields the handler never reads

title: Opening a bot whose versions store an empty card writes the server's default/scaffold card into the draft with zero operator action
mechanism: Hydration sets local card from the version row (asCard({}) → null, lazy.tsx:399) and markSaved with card=null; effectiveCard then falls to cardQuery.data.agentCard (:438-441), which get_agent_studio_card fills from card_dump or scaffold_card when no version carries a card (db:429-441). `dirty` compares that resolved card against publishedCard/published.agentCard (null) (:493-505) → true on load; `unsaved` is true too; after 1200 ms autosave PATCHes agentCard = scaffold (:654) or creates a draft. The card the bot 'has' changes because someone looked at it.
trigger: A tenant bot whose draft/published rows have agent_card = '{}' (create_prompt_version falls back to {} when inheritance and card_dump both miss, db:1633-1660) — open its editor and wait.
fix: Hydrate `card` from the same resolved source the server used, or exclude a server-supplied default from `dirty`/autosave until a card tab is touched.
verify_reason: The write is real; 'with zero operator action' is not. Verified: get_agent_studio_card resolves `card = _card_of(draft) or published_card` and falls back to card_dump(bot_id) or scaffold_card when both are empty, while `publishedCard` is returned as `{}` (db_prompt_studio.py:418-441, 502-503). Hydration sets local card from the version row only (asCard({}) → null, lazy.tsx:399) and markSaved with card=null; effectiveCard then resolves to the server's default/scaffold (lazy.tsx:438-441); both `dirty` (:493-505, publishedCard {} → null) and `unsaved` (:528-537) are true, and the autosave sends `agentCard: asCard(effectiveCard)` (lazy.tsx:654). But the autosave effect has an explicit dependency array (lazy.tsx:688-704) and skipAutosave.current is cleared inside a setTimeout(0) that schedules no re-render (lazy.tsx:404-406), so after hydration settles nothing re-enters the effect on its own — cardQuery.data.agentCard keeps its reference across refetches under TanStack structural sharing, so effectiveCard's identity is stable. The trigger is 'open the editor and type one character on any tab', not 'open it and wait'. Harm is also smaller than stated: publish already sends effectiveCard (lazy.tsx:952), so the scaffold would ship on publish regardless; the autosave only materialises it into the draft row early, flipping get_agent_studio_card's `source` from 'scaffold'/'default' to 'draft'. TRIVIAL.

title: prompt-studio.lazy.tsx route component is unreachable dead code with a second hardcoded kaia-v2-4

verify_reason: prompt-studio.tsx's beforeLoad throws unconditionally — a redirect to /agent-studio/$botId when search.unansweredId is set, otherwise to /agent-studio (prompt-studio.tsx:13-21) — so the lazy Route's component, which renders PromptStudioPage with botId="kaia-v2-4" (prompt-studio.lazy.tsx:104-107), can never mount. Note the head() meta the auditor calls unused lives in prompt-studio.tsx:22-32, not in the lazy file (whose Route declares only `component`); it is likewise never applied because beforeLoad throws first. Second hardcoded kaia-v2-4 is real — the redirect itself carries the first (prompt-studio.tsx:16). TRIVIAL.

title: The first version of a never-published bot is labelled v1.1
mechanism: nextLabel = nextVersionLabel(publishedRow?.label ?? "v1.0") increments the fallback, so with nothing live the first draft/publish is 'v1.1'.
trigger: Open a bot with no published row; header reads 'Publish v1.1'.

verify_reason: lazy.tsx:541 is exactly `const nextLabel = nextVersionLabel(publishedRow?.label ?? "v1.0");` and nextVersionLabel increments the minor when the string matches /^v(\d+)\.(\d+)$/ (prompt-studio-seed.ts:360-365), so 'v1.0' becomes 'v1.1'. With no published row, draftLabel falls through to nextLabel (lazy.tsx:546-549) and the header reads 'Publish v1.1' for a bot's very first version. TRIVIAL.

title: Draft-count dot on the History button is a role-less span with aria-label

DEFAULT_PERSONA` etc., lazy.tsx:857-859) and so does discardDraft (:902-904), but publish assigns raw at lazy.tsx:966-968 (setPersona(publishedRow.persona) / setVoice / setGuardrails) and onRollback at :1005-1007. title: trafficPct on the publish request is unbounded: >100 compiles as "full ship" and then dies as a constraint violation
mechanism: PromptVersionPublishRequest.trafficPct is `int | None` with no bounds (schemas.py:2409) while the card model constrains it to 0..100 (schema.py:358). compile.py:878 clamps the value before G12, so trafficPct=500 reports "G12 canary pass — full ship", after which the unclamped pct is inserted into bot_deployments.traffic_pct (db_prompt_studio.py:2119) and violates `CHECK (traffic_pct BETWEEN 0 AND 100)` (09_bot_config.sql:256) → 409 constraint_violation.
trigger: Any API client (not the slider) publishing with trafficPct>100.
fix: `trafficPct: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100)`, so the rejection is a 422 naming the field rather than a gate that passed followed by a database error.
verify_reason: Verified end to end. PromptVersionPublishRequest.trafficPct is `int | None = None` with no Field bounds (schemas.py:2409) while CardExperiment.traffic_pct is `Field(default=100, ge=0, le=100)` (cards/schema.py:364). main.py:3250 forwards payload.trafficPct into db.publish_prompt_version, which sets `pct = traffic_pct if traffic_pct is not None else ...` with no clamp (db_prompt_studio.py:1890) and passes it to compile_card (1919), where G12 clamps with `pct = max(0, min(100, int(pct)))` (compile.py:878) and therefore reports "G12 canary pass — full ship" (881). The same unclamped pct is then bound into the bot_deployments INSERT (db_prompt_studio.py:2121) against `traffic_pct INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 100 CHECK (traffic_pct BETWEEN 0 AND 100)` (sql/09_bot_config.sql:256) → IntegrityError → 409 constraint_violation (main.py:834-838). Transaction rolls back, so nothing ships. TRIVIAL is correct: API-only (the slider is min=0/max=100, ShipTab.tsx:161-162), fails loudly, no state change.

title: Two unrelated things are called a canary; the Ship tab shows neither the model canary nor considers it on rollback
mechanism: llm_gateway.canary.model_for (canary.py:73-89) silently overrides the live model per profile for the whole tenant, driven from the Integrations screen (integrations.ts:452-472). The Ship tab, the screen that claims to own what is shipping, never reads it, and canary.sweep_rollbacks has no branch that pulls a model canary when a mouth canary's triggers fire (agent_core/canary.py:370-421) — the two rollout axes are unaware of each other, so a bad turn during a mouth canary may be the model's.
trigger: A gateway model canary running at the same time as a deployment canary.
fix: Surface the active gateway canary (candidate model + stage) as a read-only row on Ship, and record it in the deployment experiment so a rollback reason can be attributed to the right axis.
verify_reason: Verified as an accurate observation at TRIVIAL. llm_gateway.canary.model_for (canary.py:73-89) returns the candidate model for whichever profiles the current tenant-wide gateway canary's stage allows, driven from the Integrations screen (integrations.ts:446-478 → POST /gateway/canary main.py:2895 and /gateway/canary/{id}/promote main.py:2910). agent_core.canary.sweep_rollbacks (canary.py:351-425) has no branch that reads or pulls a gateway canary, and ShipTab.tsx never imports anything from api/integrations. So the two rollout axes genuinely cannot see each other and a bad turn during a mouth canary may be the model's. Keeping TRIVIAL: this is a cross-subsystem design gap with no incorrect line of code — nothing here computes a wrong value or takes a wrong action.

title: Exporting a skill with no resolvable latest version returns a 200 zip containing an empty SKILL.md
mechanism: `get_skill` sets `markdown` only inside `if latest:` (persist.py:210-215). If `latest_version_id` is NULL or points at a row that is not in the version list, the key is absent and the export writes `zf.writestr("SKILL.md", row.get("markdown") or "")` — a valid zip with a zero-byte SKILL.md, served as 200 with the correct filename. Re-importing it raises `skill_missing_frontmatter`, which is itself a 500 (SKILLS-13). The FK is `ON DELETE SET NULL` (sql/15_skills.sql:44-48), so a NULL latest is representable.
trigger: Export a skill row whose `latest_version_id` is NULL.
fix: 404 (or 409 `skill_has_no_version`) when `markdown` is absent rather than streaming an empty pack.
verify_reason: Mechanism verified. `get_skill` assigns `markdown` only inside `if latest:` where `latest = next((v for v in summary["versions"] if v["id"] == summary["latestVersionId"]), None)` (persist.py:209-215), so a NULL or dangling `latest_version_id` leaves the key absent. The export writes `zf.writestr("SKILL.md", row.get("markdown") or "")` (main.py:2438) and returns 200 with the correct Content-Disposition (main.py:2444-2449) — a valid zip holding a zero-byte SKILL.md. Re-importing it raises `skill_missing_frontmatter` from pack.py:126, which is a 500 per SKILLS-13. The FK is confirmed `ON DELETE SET NULL` at backend/sql/15_skills.sql:44-47. Reachability is the weak link and the reporter labelled it correctly: I found no code path that deletes a single version row — `delete_skill` NULLs the pointer then deletes the whole skill (persist.py:553-563) — so a NULL latest is representable in the schema but not produced by any endpoint I can see. TRIVIAL/SUSPECTED stands as filed.

title: The key-rotation runbook in .env.example understates what rotation does to tenant packs
mechanism: The comment says "Rotating this key: restart the API so ensure_first_party_skills re-signs disk packs. Tenant drafts stay unsigned until a human signs them again." Tenant *drafts* were already unsigned; the affected rows are tenant packs that WERE signed. Those keep `signature_status='signed'` in the database, keep rendering green in the library (persist.py:60), keep granting their skill-gated tools and injecting their bodies on live calls (intersect.py:113-114 — see SKILLS-03), and fail only at the next publish of a card that names them. The runbook gives an operator no reason to expect any of that.
trigger: Follow the documented rotation procedure on an install with tenant-signed packs.
fix: Correct the comment, and give the rotation a real procedure: re-sign or explicitly retire every tenant-signed version, and have the library show verification state (SKILLS-05) so the blast radius is visible.
verify_reason: The reading of the comment is correct but MINOR overstates it. The runbook text is at backend/.env.example:336-340 (not 337-341) and does say only that disk packs are re-signed on restart and that "Tenant drafts stay unsigned until a human signs them again" — silent on previously-signed tenant packs, which do keep `signature_status='signed'` (persist.py:60 renders them green), keep unlocking their gated tools (intersect.py:113-114) and keep injecting their bodies, failing only at the next G9 (compile.py:731). All of that is true. But it is a comment in an example env file: no behaviour, no runtime path, no operator-facing surface in the product, and every consequence it fails to mention is already carried by SKILLS-03 and SKILLS-05 as the defects that actually need fixing. Documentation that is incomplete about a behaviour reported elsewhere is TRIVIAL under this rubric — fixing the comment without fixing SKILLS-03 would change nothing.

title: No pending state for the catalog; any compile HTTP error is labelled 'compiler unreachable'
mechanism: While useFlowTools is pending, rows = [] (:86) and the empty/error branches are both suppressed (:195), so the table renders a bare header with no loading indicator. For the preview, `preview.isError` (:129) covers a 500 from compile_card as well as a network failure, yet the lozenge always says 'compiler unreachable'; the endpoint returns 200 for gate failures (main.py:2195-2212), so an error here is a compiler crash, not unreachability.
trigger: Slow /flow/tools: table header with no rows and no spinner. A compile 500: 'compiler unreachable'.
fix: Render LoadingState while toolsQuery.isPending; show the error message (or status) in the preview lozenge title instead of the fixed 'unreachable' text.
verify_reason: Both halves read as claimed. AgentCardPanels.tsx:86 `rows = toolsQuery.data ?? []`; the footer at :188-197 is `toolsQuery.isError ? <error> : !toolsQuery.isPending && rows.length === 0 ? <empty> : null`, so while the query is pending both branches are null and the table paints a header with no body and no spinner. For the preview, :129-130 keys the fixed text 'compiler unreachable' off preview.isError alone; main.py:2194-2212 raises nothing for gate failures (it returns db.compile_agent_studio_card's report as a 200), so a non-2xx here is a compiler exception, not unreachability, and the lozenge misattributes it. TRIVIAL as rated.

title: PLATFORM_SKILL_TOOLS granted to cards with no skills, contrary to the module's own comment
mechanism: The comment at intersect.py:50 says load_skill/run_skill_script are 'Always offered when the card has skills', but `platform = PLATFORM_SKILL_TOOLS & catalog_names` is unioned into `names` at :106 and re-added after channel filtering at :116 with no `card.skills` condition. run_skill_script executes scripts; a card whose author left it off include (supervisor-brief: include=['add_customer_note'], defaults.py:118) still receives it in the grant, widening the grant beyond the card (ADR-0001).
trigger: Resolve the supervisor-brief card through MouthTurn.tools: allowed contains load_skill and run_skill_script though include names neither and no skill packs are attached to require them.
fix: Gate `platform` on `bool(card.skills) or attached_skills` (as the comment states) or on membership in include, and update the comment to match whichever rule is chosen.
verify_reason: The code claim is true — intersect.py:105-106 computes `platform = PLATFORM_SKILL_TOOLS & catalog_names` and unions it into names with no card.skills condition, re-adding it at :114 and :116, while the comment at intersect.py:50 says 'Always offered when the card has skills'. But the cited trigger is false and it was the whole of the stated harm: supervisor-brief DOES have skills — cards/defaults.py:330 passes skills=skill_refs(*SUPERVISOR_SKILLS) and skills/defaults.py:35 makes that ('supervisor-brief','qa-examiner') — so for that card the comment's own condition holds and nothing is widened beyond what the comment sanctions. All four first-party cards attach skills (cards/defaults.py:173, :293, :314, :330), so the divergence needs a card with every pack detached, and even then the widening is load_skill (which can only load an attached pack's body) and run_skill_script, whose spec is an enum of two pure functions with no shell, network or ledger write (catalog.py:623-645). Real, but it is a stale comment with no demonstrated grant-widening on any shipped card: TRIVIAL. What would settle a MINOR rating: a card in the fleet with tools.skills == [] whose resolved MouthTurn.tools contains run_skill_script.

title: CompileReport.mission_entries is computed, serialised and never consumed; its docstring names a consumer that reads a different endpoint
mechanism: `CompileReport.mission_entries: dict[str, str]` is populated on every compile (`mission_entries=_mission_entries(flow)`, compile.py:952) and shipped as part of the `response_model=CompileReport` body of POST /agent-studio/cards/{bot_id}/compile. Its docstring says "The Outbound tab renders this beside what the card claims, because the two disagreeing is the failure G-OB2 exists to catch". The TypeScript `CompileReport` (agent-studio.ts:60-71) declares seven members and not this one; grepping Habibi/src for `mission_entries` or `missionEntries` returns nothing. The Outbound tab does render both halves — from `graphEntries` and `graphEntryNode`/`agrees` on GET /outbound/missions (main.py:5344-5361), a second, independently computed copy of the same fact.
trigger: Open the compile preview on any card. `mission_entries` is computed and sent on every keystroke-debounced compile (useCompilePreview, agent-studio.ts:230-260) and discarded. The cost is a stale docstring pointing a future reader at the wrong producer for a G-OB2 disagreement.
fix: Either declare `mission_entries: Record<string, string>` on the TS CompileReport and let the Outbound tab read the compile report it already holds (dropping the second source), or delete the field from CompileReport and correct the docstring to name /outbound/missions. Two independently derived copies of "where does this mission start" is exactly the shape G-OB2 exists to police.
verify_reason: The facts check out but the severity does not. CompileReport.mission_entries is declared at compile.py:78-81 with the docstring "The Outbound tab renders this beside what the card claims…", and is populated on every compile at compile.py:953 (not :952, which is skill_description_tokens). TS CompileReport (agent-studio.ts:62-74) declares seven members without it, and `grep -rn "mission_entries|missionEntries" Habibi/src` returns nothing. The Outbound tab does get the same fact from GET /outbound/missions, which computes fg.parse_graph(version.flow).entry_objectives() itself and ships it as graphEntries plus per-objective graphEntryNode/agrees (main.py:5337, 5344-5348, 5363). So: a field that is computed and serialised with no consumer, plus a docstring naming a consumer that reads a different endpoint. No wrong runtime behaviour, no unreachable data (the same fact is reachable, from elsewhere), nothing an operator can trip. That is documentation rot plus a dead wire field — TRIVIAL, not MINOR.

title: PromptVersion omits `tuning`, the column publish reads and VoicePanel writes through
mechanism: `PromptVersionResponse.tuning: dict[str, Any]` (schemas.py:2224) is served on every version read. The TypeScript `PromptVersion` (api/types/prompt-studio.ts:59-82) declares id, label, author, status, createdAt, summary, prompt, persona, voice, guardrails, flow, flowUnreadable, botId, agentCard — no `tuning`. The field is not decorative: `patch_prompt_version` folds the VoicePanel's voice config into it on every autosave (`apply_voice_config_overlay`, db_prompt_studio.py:1735-1745) with the comment "publish reads this", and an explicit Tuning Studio write overrides it (db_prompt_studio.py:1755-1761). So the studio edits `tuning` indirectly and can never read back what it produced.
trigger: Adjust a voice slider, autosave, then look at the version: the derived tuning that will ship is on the wire and invisible to the editor, to the diff and to the version-history comparison.
fix: Add `tuning?: Record<string, unknown>` to `PromptVersion` (api/types/prompt-studio.ts) and include it in the version diff, so a publish cannot change the runtime tuning without the diff saying so.
verify_reason: The mechanism is exactly as described — PromptVersionResponse.tuning: dict[str, Any] at schemas.py:2224 is served on every version read; TS PromptVersion (api/types/prompt-studio.ts:61-85) names 14 members and not tuning; patch_prompt_version folds the VoicePanel's voice config into tuning on every autosave via apply_voice_config_overlay (db_prompt_studio.py:1735-1749, comment "publish reads this") and an explicit Tuning Studio write overrides it (db_prompt_studio.py:1755-1762). But the claim that the derived tuning is invisible does not survive: both ends of the derivation are already on screen. The inputs are readable — voice.speed/pitch/warmth/params are VoiceConfig fields the VoicePanel draws, and VoiceParamsPanel.tsx:340 tells the author in prose that they are "saved on the version and folded into the deployment's tuning". The result is readable — BotDeployment.tuning IS typed (prompt-studio.ts:45) and VersionHistory.tsx:164-166 actually reads activeDeployment.tuning.tts.voice. So what is unreachable is only the intermediate on the draft row, a deterministic function of values the editor already shows. Cosmetic type incompleteness: TRIVIAL.

title: agent-card.ts restates six closed vocabularies that the backend guards against each other, and a cast in the editor makes the TypeScript half unenforceable
mechanism: agent-card.ts restates `Objective` (13 members), `Direction`, `VoicemailMode`, `TimeOfDay`, `PoolKind` and `PostCallQa`. Backend-side these are well policed: test_outbound_card_vocabulary.py asserts the /outbound/card-vocabulary lists equal `fg.OBJECTIVES` and each `get_args(schema.<Literal>)`, and its docstring says the whole defence is that "the frontend restates nothing". The frontend does restate them. Only `ROLLBACK_TRIGGERS` has a matching TS assertion (test_agent_card_schema_drift.py:86-101) — added, per its own docstring, after exactly this class of bug. Worse, the restatement cannot even fail loudly: OutboundCardEditor casts the server-supplied option with `key as Objective` (line 659) and `o as Objective` (line 653), so a vocabulary the backend widened flows through the TypeScript union untouched.
trigger: Add a member to `flow_graph.OBJECTIVES` and `schema.Objective`. Every backend test passes, /outbound/card-vocabulary offers it, the `as Objective` cast accepts it — and the stale TS `Objective` union is now a comment claiming to be a type. In the opposite direction (a member removed from the Literal but left in the TS union) the editor's own type would still bless a value the card rejects at parse.
fix: Extend test_agent_card_schema_drift.py with the same regex-and-compare treatment ROLLBACK_TRIGGERS already gets, for `Objective`, `Direction`, `VoicemailMode`, `TimeOfDay`, `PoolKind`, `Channel`, `DataClass`, `MemoryScope`, `EvalRequire` and `HumanGateRequire` against `get_args()` of each Literal. Then drop the `as Objective` casts in OutboundCardEditor.tsx:653,659 in favour of a narrowing predicate, so the union actually gates.
verify_reason: The observations are accurate but the causal claim inverts. Confirmed: agent-card.ts:76-101 restates Objective (13 members), Direction, VoicemailMode, TimeOfDay, PoolKind and PostCallQa; test_outbound_card_vocabulary.py:1-18 says the whole defence is that "the frontend restates nothing"; only ROLLBACK_TRIGGERS has a TS-side assertion (test_agent_card_schema_drift.py:88-101). But the casts are the mitigation, not the aggravation. `available = vocab.objectives.filter(...)` (OutboundCardEditor.tsx:653) and `key: key as Objective` (:660) mean the dropdown's contents come from /outbound/card-vocabulary, so a widened backend list is offered and stored correctly the moment the endpoint returns it — the stale TS union causes no wrong option and no publish 422. The removal direction is likewise safe: the endpoint stops offering the removed member, so nothing draws it. I checked every use of `Objective` in Habibi/src (agent-card.ts:88/206, OutboundCardEditor.tsx:36/653/660) — there is no exhaustive switch, no Record keyed by it, no label map that could go stale; FlowInspector.tsx:178-198 is explicit that its mission list comes from the endpoint, not a constant. So the residual defect is that a test docstring's premise ("restates nothing") is factually false while the restatement is load-bearing for nothing: TRIVIAL.

title: nullability.test.ts covers three non-studio files while ~40 nullable studio wire fields go unpinned
mechanism: The nullability suite reads `api/types/customer360.ts`, `api/types/audit.ts` and `api/customers.ts` and asserts string literals in them (`summary: string | null;` etc.). It names no studio file. Meanwhile the studio wire is full of `X | None`: AgentStudioCardResponse has six (`trafficPct`, `lastPublish`, `promptVersionId`, `draftVersionId`, `archivedAt`, plus AgentStudioChangeLogEntryResponse's fifteen), AgentStudioGraphEdgeResponse.to, AgentStudioSkillSummaryResponse.latestVersionId, BotDeploymentResponse's five, PromptTokenEstimateResponse's two. TYPES-06 (`to: string` vs `str | None`) and TYPES-07 (`latestVersionId?: string` vs `str | None`) are both instances the existing suite is shaped to catch and does not, because it was written for one work-package's files and never widened.
trigger: A nullable studio field is typed non-nullable; `strict` TypeScript compiles clean because the assertion lives in a test that reads different files.
fix: Add a studio block to nullability.test.ts covering api/agent-studio.ts, api/prompt-studio.ts, api/types/prompt-studio.ts and api/sandbox.ts — or, better, generate the assertions from the Pydantic models in the drift test proposed in TYPES-03, where `field.annotation` already knows whether None is allowed.
verify_reason: The coverage facts are right — nullability.test.ts:11-63 reads only api/types/customer360.ts, api/types/audit.ts and api/customers.ts and names no studio file, while AgentStudioGraphEdgeResponse.to (schemas.py:3593), AgentStudioSkillSummaryResponse.latestVersionId (schemas.py:3633) and BotDeploymentResponse's nullables (schemas.py:2347-2353, :2358) are all `X | None`. But this carries no defect of its own. Structurally it is TYPES-03 restricted to the nullability axis: same absent guard, same file set, and its only two concrete instances are TYPES-06 and TYPES-07, both already filed and confirmed separately. Counting it as a third MINOR triple-counts one gap. As a standalone item it is a note that an existing suite was scoped to one work package and never widened: TRIVIAL, and it should be folded into TYPES-03's fix rather than tracked apart.

title: Provider-chip counts and 'All' total ignore the active status filter
mechanism: list_tts_voice_provider_counts hardcodes status='GA' (db.py:7460) while the Browser lets the operator switch status to Preview (514-522); the chips keep GA counts, so 'Azure · 774' sits over a list of 12 Preview voices.
trigger: Filters → Status → Preview.
fix: Accept ?status= on /tts-voices/catalog-provider-counts and key the query on it, or hide counts when status !== 'GA'.
verify_reason: list_tts_voice_provider_counts hardcodes `AND status = 'GA'` in its WHERE (db.py:7458-7461) and takes no status argument, while the Browser lets the operator switch status to Preview (VoiceCatalogBrowser.tsx:514-522) and the chips plus the 'All' total are built from that unfiltered count map (386-411, 395). So the chips keep GA tallies over a Preview list. Same defect applies to list_tts_voice_locale_counts (db.py:7485-7487), which feeds the locale dropdown's '· N' labels (localeChoices, 368-384) — worth adding to the fix. Cosmetic count mismatch, TRIVIAL is right.
